lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Getting Started — Let's Talk

  • Q: What behaviour do we need to show while working in a group?
    Ans: While working in a group we should be patient, polite and helpful. We should listen to others, share things with them, finish our own part of the work on time and never misbehave with group members.
  • Q: What is the importance of patience while working with friends?
    Ans: Patience is very important while working with friends. If we stay patient, we do not get angry over small delays or mistakes. Like Ayesha in the story, we can help a friend finish his work instead of scolding him, and the group work is completed happily and on time.
  • Q: What would you do if you were Azlan?
    Ans: If I were Azlan, I would not hide my laziness or misbehave with my group members. I would start my part of the project on time, and if I was late, I would say sorry to my friends and work hard to finish it quickly.

Pre-reading

  • Q: Have you ever faced any situation in which you showed patience? How?
    Ans: Yes. Once my younger brother broke my pen by mistake. I wanted to scold him, but I stayed calm and patient. I forgave him and shared another pen with him. In this way I showed patience and avoided a quarrel.

While-reading

  • Q: If someone misbehaves with you, what would be your reaction?
    Ans: If someone misbehaves with me, I will stay patient like Rasoolullah (PBUH). I will not scold or fight with that person. I will speak politely, forgive him and pray for his guidance, because patience always brings a good result.

Post-reading

  • Q: Who is your role model and why? Discuss.
    Ans: My role model is Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH). He is complete in all aspects. He was called Saadiq and Al-Amin for his honest nature, he always spoke the truth, and he showed great patience even when his enemies hurt him. I want to follow his teachings in my life.
  • Q: Do you think helping others is good for us?
    Ans: Yes, helping others is good for us. When we help someone in a difficult time, like Ayesha helped Azlan, we make good friends and earn respect. Helping others also makes us kind and patient, and Allah is pleased with those who help others.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension i. Answer these questions

  • Q: How did the people of Taif treat Rasoolullah (PBUH)?
    Ans: The people of Taif treated Rasoolullah (PBUH) very badly. He stayed in Taif for ten days and invited the tribal chiefs to embrace Islam, but they rejected his message and mocked him. One day a mob pelted him with pebbles and injured him.
  • Q: Why was Rasoolullah (PBUH) called Saadiq and Al-Amin?
    Ans: Rasoolullah (PBUH) was called Saadiq and Al-Amin for his honest nature. He always spoke the truth without considering the consequences, so the people gave him these titles.
  • Q: How did Rasoolullah (PBUH) treat his opponents?
    Ans: Rasoolullah (PBUH) treated his opponents with patience and kindness. He never got scared of them, never lost his patience and never scolded them. He always prayed to Allah to guide them towards the right path and to forgive them. Even at Taif, despite his injuries, he prayed for the people who had hurt him.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension ii. Digraphs, trigraphs and silent letters in the given sentences

  • Q: In 'The farmer is cutting wheat', which letters make the digraph?
    Ans: The letters 'wh' in 'wheat' make a digraph — two letters that make one sound.
  • Q: In 'The children are playing in the park', which letters make the digraph?
    Ans: The letters 'ch' in 'children' make a digraph — two letters that make one sound.
  • Q: In 'The boys are playing the match', which letters make the trigraph?
    Ans: The letters 'tch' in 'match' make a trigraph — three letters that make one sound.
  • Q: In 'Do not fight with each other', which letters make the trigraph?
    Ans: The letters 'igh' in 'fight' make a trigraph — three letters that make one sound.
  • Q: In 'Sana is climbing the mountain', which letter is silent?
    Ans: The letter 'b' in 'climbing' is silent.
  • Q: In 'He wrapped the wrist watch', which letter is silent?
    Ans: The letter 'w' in 'wrist' is silent.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension iii. Circle the digraphs in red, trigraphs in green (given text)

  • Q: In the given text ('It was a Wednesday morning...'), find the digraph 'th'. In which words does it occur?
    Ans: The digraph 'th' occurs in 'the' (in 'in the ground', 'for the cricket match' and 'reached the playground') and in 'together' ('We had together in the ground'). Circle 'th' in red in these words.
  • Q: Find the digraph 'ch' in the given text.
    Ans: The digraph 'ch' occurs in 'reached' ('Everyone reached the playground at 8 o'clock') and in 'match'. Circle 'ch' in red.
  • Q: Find the digraph 'ph' in the given text.
    Ans: The digraph 'ph' occurs twice in 'photographs' ('We were very excited and took photographs'). Circle both 'ph' in red.
  • Q: Find the trigraph in the given text.
    Ans: The trigraph 'tch' occurs in 'match' ('for the cricket match'). Circle 'tch' in green.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension iv. Topic sentence and supporting sentences

  • Q: Read the given paragraph about Ayesha and Azlan. What is its topic sentence, and what are the supporting sentences?
    Ans: Topic sentence: 'Ayesha is a good friend of Azlan who helped him in his difficult time.' Supporting sentences: 'A good friend is a blessing of Allah. A good friend is one who stands by your side at all times like Ayesha. Her friendship is like a precious jewel for Azlan. We should value our friends and take care of them.' The supporting sentences explain and support the topic sentence.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension v. Main idea of the paragraph

  • Q: What is the main idea of the paragraph given on page 5?
    Ans: The main idea is: A good friend is one who helps us in times of need. Such a friend is definitely a valuable asset.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension vi. Fill in the blanks

  • Q: Rasoolullah (PBUH) was called ______ due to his truthfulness.
    Ans: Saadiq
  • Q: The people of Taif refused to accept ______.
    Ans: Islam
  • Q: Rasoolullah (PBUH) stayed in Taif for ______.
    Ans: ten days

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 2. Analytical Reading

  • Q: Read any incident about patience and note it down in your notebook.
    Ans: Model note — The incident of Taif: Rasoolullah (PBUH) went to Taif with Hazrat Zaid bin Haritha (RA) to spread the message of Islam. The chiefs rejected his message and a mob pelted him with pebbles and injured him. Even then he did not curse them. When an angel asked permission to destroy the city, he prayed, 'O Allah, guide the people of Taif to the right path.' This is the greatest example of patience.

lessons.title: Sounds and Speaking
lessons.notes_html:
A) Oral Communication — 1. Learning the Sounds: Silent Letters

  • Q: Read: 'Hamza and Azlan walked to school.' Which letter is silent in the word 'walked'?
    Ans: The letter 'l' is silent in 'walked'. The word is pronounced without the 'l' sound.
  • Q: Read: 'Please give me this knife.' Which letter is silent in 'knife'?
    Ans: The letter 'k' is silent in 'knife'. The word begins with the 'n' sound.
  • Q: Read: 'Write an essay about your best friend.' Which letter is silent in 'Write'?
    Ans: The letter 'W' is silent in 'Write'. The word begins with the 'r' sound.
  • Q: Read: 'He is climbing the mountain.' Which letter is silent in 'climbing'?
    Ans: The letter 'b' is silent in 'climbing'. The word ends with the 'm' sound and the 'b' is not pronounced.
  • Q: Write ten more words with silent letters and pronounce them.
    Ans: Ten more words with silent letters are: listen (silent 't'), know (silent 'k'), honest (silent 'h'), hour (silent 'h'), wrap (silent 'w'), knee (silent 'k'), comb (silent 'b'), lamb (silent 'b'), castle (silent 't') and island (silent 's').

A) Oral Communication — 2. Learning to Speak

  • Q: Arrange a role-play activity in the class and use the routine greetings and social courtesies (as in the Ali and Danish dialogue) in your dialogues.
    Ans: Model role-play: Ahmed: Assalaamu Alaikum, Bilal! How are you? Bilal: Wa Alaikum Asalaam! I am fine. Nice to see you here in the park. Ahmed: Thank you. I have come here to practise for a football match. Bilal: Oh! That is great. Ahmed: Tomorrow my school team has its final match with another school. Bilal: Best of luck!

mcqs.q: Which letter is silent in the word 'walked'?
mcqs.why: The solved answer says the letter 'l' is silent in 'walked' and the word is pronounced without the 'l' sound.

mcqs.q: Which letter is silent in the word 'knife'?
mcqs.why: The solved answer says the letter 'k' is silent in 'knife' and the word begins with the 'n' sound.

mcqs.q: Which letter is silent in the word 'Write'?
mcqs.why: The solved answer says the letter 'W' is silent in 'Write' and the word begins with the 'r' sound.

mcqs.q: Which letter is silent in the word 'listen', from the ten extra silent-letter words?
mcqs.why: The solved list of ten more silent-letter words gives 'listen' with a silent 't', along with know, honest, hour and others.

mcqs.q: Which letter is silent in the word 'honest'?
mcqs.why: The solved list of ten more silent-letter words gives 'honest' with a silent 'h', so the word begins with the 'o' sound.

mcqs.q: Which letter is silent in the word 'island'?
mcqs.why: The solved list of ten more silent-letter words gives 'island' with a silent 's', along with comb, lamb and castle.

mcqs.q: Which letter is silent in the word 'castle'?
mcqs.why: The solved list of ten more silent-letter words gives 'castle' with a silent 't', the same silent letter as in 'listen'.

mcqs.q: In the model role-play, how does Bilal answer Ahmed's greeting?
options: Wa Alaikum Asalaam! I am fine
mcqs.why: In the solved model role-play Bilal replies 'Wa Alaikum Asalaam! I am fine. Nice to see you here in the park.'

mcqs.q: In the model role-play, why has Ahmed come to the park?
options: To practise for a football match
mcqs.why: Ahmed says in the solved role-play, 'I have come here to practise for a football match,' because his school team has its final match tomorrow.

mcqs.q: In the model role-play, what does Bilal say at the end?
mcqs.why: When Ahmed tells Bilal about the final match tomorrow, Bilal wishes him 'Best of luck!' at the end of the solved role-play.

lessons.title: Language Focus
lessons.notes_html:
C) Language Focus — 1. Vocabulary Building i. Words with their meanings

  • Q: Match: inspiration
    Ans: a person or thing that motivates
  • Q: Match: personality
    Ans: the various aspects of a person's character
  • Q: Match: honest
    Ans: the person who always tells truth
  • Q: Match: patience
    Ans: tolerance
  • Q: Match: betterment
    Ans: improvement

C) Language Focus — 1. Vocabulary Building ii. Naming, action and describing words (Fruits and Vegetables Mall advertisement)

  • Q: From the advertisement, write a naming word and use it in your own sentence: fruits
    Ans: Naming word: fruits. Sentence: We should eat fresh fruits every day.
  • Q: From the advertisement, write a naming word and use it in your own sentence: vegetables
    Ans: Naming word: vegetables. Sentence: My mother cooks vegetables for dinner.
  • Q: From the advertisement, write an action word and use it in your own sentence: get
    Ans: Action word: get. Sentence: I get up early in the morning.
  • Q: From the advertisement, write an action word and use it in your own sentence: delivered
    Ans: Action word: delivered. Sentence: The postman delivered the parcel at our doorstep.
  • Q: From the advertisement, write a describing word and use it in your own sentence: fresh
    Ans: Describing word: fresh. Sentence: We get fresh air in the garden.
  • Q: From the advertisement, write a describing word and use it in your own sentence: healthy
    Ans: Describing word: healthy. Sentence: Healthy food keeps us strong and active.

C) Language Focus — 2. Learning to Spell: Fill in the missing letters to complete the words

  • Q: worl______
    Ans: world
  • Q: com______let______
    Ans: complete
  • Q: hon______s______
    Ans: honest
  • Q: t______uth
    Ans: truth
  • Q: for______iv______
    Ans: forgive
  • Q: d______z______n
    Ans: dozen

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar: Common and Proper Nouns i. Notice the use of common and proper nouns

  • Q: In 'My grandmother lives in a village', which are the common nouns?
    Ans: 'grandmother' and 'village' are common nouns. They are general names of a person and a place.
  • Q: In 'I made a cake for my mother', which are the common nouns?
    Ans: 'cake' and 'mother' are common nouns. They are general names of a thing and a person.
  • Q: In 'There is a masjid near my house', which are the common nouns?
    Ans: 'masjid' and 'house' are common nouns.
  • Q: In 'She likes to play with a doll', which is the common noun?
    Ans: 'doll' is a common noun. It is the general name of a thing.
  • Q: In 'There are beautiful mountains in my country', which are the common nouns?
    Ans: 'mountains' and 'country' are common nouns.
  • Q: In 'Allama Iqbal is our national poet', which is the proper noun?
    Ans: 'Allama Iqbal' is a proper noun. It is the name of a particular person and begins with a capital letter.
  • Q: In 'They went to the Faisal Masjid', which is the proper noun?
    Ans: 'Faisal Masjid' is a proper noun. It is the name of a particular place.
  • Q: In 'Nida reads the Holy Quran in the morning', which are the proper nouns?
    Ans: 'Nida' and 'Holy Quran' are proper nouns. They are the names of a particular person and a particular book.
  • Q: In 'Muhammad Ali Jinnah is the founder of Pakistan', which are the proper nouns?
    Ans: 'Muhammad Ali Jinnah' and 'Pakistan' are proper nouns.

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar ii. Underline the nouns and write whether they are common or proper nouns

  • Q: 'We will go to Rawal Lake next week.' Underline the noun and state its kind.
    Ans: Rawal Lake — proper noun (the name of a particular lake).
  • Q: 'My father is a hard-working man.' Underline the nouns and state their kind.
    Ans: father, man — common nouns (general names of persons).
  • Q: 'It is a huge building.' Underline the noun and state its kind.
    Ans: building — common noun (the general name of a thing).
  • Q: 'Islamabad is a beautiful city.' Underline the nouns and state their kind.
    Ans: Islamabad — proper noun (the name of a particular city); city — common noun.
  • Q: 'K-2 is the highest peak of Pakistan.' Underline the nouns and state their kind.
    Ans: K-2 — proper noun; Pakistan — proper noun; peak — common noun.

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar iii. Countable, uncountable and collective nouns in the given paragraph (Hira at the shopping mall)

  • Q: From the paragraph, list the countable nouns.
    Ans: Countable nouns: shops, fruits, vegetables, onions, bananas, bookstore and storybook. These nouns can be counted and have plural forms.
  • Q: From the paragraph, list the uncountable nouns.
    Ans: Uncountable nouns: tea and chocolate (in 'chocolate cake'), and experience. These nouns cannot be counted and do not have plural forms.
  • Q: From the paragraph, list the collective nouns.
    Ans: Collective nouns: a bunch of grapes, a dozen bananas and a bouquet of flowers. These name a group or collection of things.

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar iv. Write three countable, uncountable and collective nouns and use them in sentences

  • Q: Write three countable nouns and use them in your sentences.
    Ans: Countable nouns: (1) book — I have two books in my bag. (2) apple — She ate an apple. (3) chair — There are four chairs in the room.
  • Q: Write three uncountable nouns and use them in your sentences.
    Ans: Uncountable nouns: (1) water — Please give me some water. (2) rain — The rain fell all night. (3) milk — Milk is good for health.
  • Q: Write three collective nouns and use them in your sentences.
    Ans: Collective nouns: (1) team — Our cricket team won the match. (2) class — My class has forty students. (3) flock — A flock of birds flew over the river.

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar: Articles 'a' and 'an' v. Notice the use of articles in the given paragraph

  • Q: In the given paragraph ('There were dark clouds in the sky...'), which words are used with 'a' and which with 'an'? Why?
    Ans: 'an' is used before 'umbrella' and 'ice cream' because these words begin with a vowel sound. 'a' is used before 'cat', 'tree' and 'packet' because these words begin with a consonant sound. 'a' is used before a noun starting with a consonant sound and 'an' before a word starting with a vowel sound.

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar vi. Tick the correct option (a / an)

  • Q: There is ______ book on the table.
    Options: a / an
    Ans: a
  • Q: Sara had ______ egg for breakfast.
    Options: a / an
    Ans: an
  • Q: Please give me ______ apple.
    Options: a / an
    Ans: an
  • Q: She goes to ______ university.
    Options: a / an
    Ans: a
  • Q: Maria is ______ honest girl.
    Options: a / an
    Ans: an

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar: Adjectives vii. Types of adjectives in the given sentences

  • Q: Which type of adjective is 'red' in 'She bought a red dress'?
    Ans: 'red' is an adjective of colour. It describes the colours of a noun.
  • Q: Which type of adjective is 'honest' in 'Azlan is an honest child'?
    Ans: 'honest' is an adjective of quality. It describes the characteristics of a noun.
  • Q: Which type of adjective is 'big' in 'They live in a big house'?
    Ans: 'big' is an adjective of size. It describes the size of a noun.
  • Q: Which type of adjective is 'round' in 'We have a round dining table'?
    Ans: 'round' is an adjective of shape. It describes the shape of a noun.
  • Q: Which type of adjective is 'Pakistani' in 'Maha is a Pakistani girl'?
    Ans: 'Pakistani' is an adjective of origin. It describes where someone or something comes from.
  • Q: Which type of adjective is 'many' in 'There were many trees in the park'?
    Ans: 'many' is an adjective of quantity/number. It describes the quantity of a noun and answers the question 'How many?'

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar viii. Put the following adjectives in the correct boxes

  • Q: Adjective of quality: which words from the list (intelligent, large, black, few, round, American, Chinese, oval, one, short, truthful, yellow) belong here?
    Ans: intelligent, truthful
  • Q: Adjective of shape: which words from the list belong here?
    Ans: round, oval
  • Q: Adjective of colour: which words from the list belong here?
    Ans: black, yellow
  • Q: Adjective of origin: which words from the list belong here?
    Ans: American, Chinese
  • Q: Adjective of size: which words from the list belong here?
    Ans: large, short
  • Q: Adjective of quantity: which words from the list belong here?
    Ans: few, one

lessons.title: Writing
lessons.notes_html:
D) Writing — 1. Learning to Write i. Words with their syllable division

  • Q: Give the syllable division and number of syllables of 'model'.
    Ans: mod.el — 2 syllables.
  • Q: Give the syllable division and number of syllables of 'tolerance'.
    Ans: tol.er.ance — 3 syllables.
  • Q: Give the syllable division and number of syllables of 'personality'.
    Ans: per.son.al.i.ty — 5 syllables.
  • Q: Give the syllable division and number of syllables of 'forgiveness'.
    Ans: for.give.ness — 3 syllables.
  • Q: Give the syllable division and number of syllables of 'beautiful'.
    Ans: beau.ti.ful — 3 syllables.

D) Writing — 1. Learning to Write ii. Divide the given words into their syllables and write the number of syllables

  • Q: Divide 'vegetable' into syllables and write the number of syllables.
    Ans: veg.e.ta.ble — 4 syllables.
  • Q: Divide 'project' into syllables and write the number of syllables.
    Ans: pro.ject — 2 syllables.
  • Q: Divide 'complete' into syllables and write the number of syllables.
    Ans: com.plete — 2 syllables.
  • Q: Divide 'computer' into syllables and write the number of syllables.
    Ans: com.put.er — 3 syllables.
  • Q: Divide 'mountain' into syllables and write the number of syllables. Also write multi-syllabic words of your own.
    Ans: moun.tain — 2 syllables. Multi-syllabic words of my own: banana (ba.na.na, 3 syllables), elephant (el.e.phant, 3 syllables) and tomorrow (to.mor.row, 3 syllables).

D) Writing — 1. Learning to Write iii. First paragraph of the lesson: topic sentence, supporting details and main idea

  • Q: Read the first paragraph of the lesson carefully. Write its topic sentence and supporting details, and write its main idea in your own words.
    Ans: Topic sentence: 'Everyone in the world needs some inspiration.' Supporting details: We get inspired and make someone our role model or ideal to be followed. The writer's own role model is Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH), who is complete in all aspects. He was called Saadiq and Al-Amin for his honest nature and always spoke the truth without considering the consequences. Main idea (in my own words): Every person needs a role model to follow, and the best role model for us is Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) because of his truthfulness and complete personality.

D) Writing — 2. Creative Writing: Good Qualities

  • Q: Write some good qualities which you can show in school/classroom. Also write how they would help you in becoming a better person.
    Ans: Good qualities I can show in school and classroom are: (1) Patience — I listen to my teacher and classmates calmly and do not get angry. (2) Honesty — I always speak the truth and do my work myself. (3) Kindness and helping others — I help my classmates in their studies and share my things with them. (4) Punctuality and cleanliness — I come to school on time and keep my classroom clean. These qualities will make me a better person because teachers and friends will trust and respect me, and I will learn good habits for my whole life.

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Getting Started — Look at the pictures and write the names of the given blessings

  • Q: Name the blessing shown in picture 1 (top row, first picture).
    Ans: Apple
  • Q: Name the blessing shown in picture 2 (top row, second picture).
    Ans: Pineapple
  • Q: Name the blessing shown in picture 3 (top row, third picture).
    Ans: Strawberry
  • Q: Name the blessing shown in picture 4 (top row, fourth picture).
    Ans: Banana
  • Q: Name the blessing shown in picture 5 (top row, fifth picture).
    Ans: Pear
  • Q: Name the blessing shown in picture 6 (bottom row, first picture).
    Ans: Tomato
  • Q: Name the blessing shown in picture 7 (bottom row, second picture).
    Ans: Potato
  • Q: Name the blessing shown in picture 8 (bottom row, third picture).
    Ans: Carrot
  • Q: Name the blessing shown in picture 9 (bottom row, fourth picture).
    Ans: Brinjal
  • Q: Name the blessing shown in picture 10 (bottom row, fifth picture).
    Ans: Capsicum

Getting Started — Let's Talk

  • Q: What is your favourite fruit or vegetable?
    Ans: My favourite fruit is the apple. (Answers may vary; this is a model answer.)
  • Q: Describe why you like it the most.
    Ans: I like the apple the most because it is sweet, juicy and crunchy. It is easy to eat, keeps me full and is available in every season.
  • Q: Can you explain the nutritional value of the chosen fruit or vegetable?
    Ans: An apple is full of vitamins and fibre. It gives us energy, keeps our stomach healthy and makes our body strong. That is why it is said that an apple a day keeps the doctor away.
  • Q: Imagine what life would be like if these blessings were not created by Allah.
    Ans: If fruits and vegetables were not created by Allah, we would have very little to eat. We would not get vitamins and energy, we would fall ill again and again, and life would become very difficult.
  • Q: Name a few more natural things without which life is not possible.
    Ans: Water, air, sunlight, trees and soil are natural things without which life is not possible. We need water to drink, air to breathe and sunlight for plants to grow and give us food.

Pre-reading (Poem: Oh Allah Love Me)

  • Q: Look at the pictures and read the title of the lesson. Guess five words related to it.
    Ans: Five words related to the title 'Oh Allah Love Me' are: love, blessings, stars, night and care.
  • Q: Name some blessings of Allah for us.
    Ans: Some blessings of Allah for us are the sun, the moon and stars, air, water, trees, flowers, birds, fruits and vegetables, and our parents and friends who care for us.

While-reading

  • Q: Which attribute of Allah is discussed in the second stanza of the poem?
    Ans: The second stanza discusses that Allah is always present and caring. When the flowers bloom in a queue and sleep at night with dew, and when the poet needs a lot of care, she feels Allah's presence there. It shows that Allah is always near us and takes care of us.

Post-reading

  • Q: How do you show your love for Allah? Discuss different ways.
    Ans: We show our love for Allah by obeying His commands, offering prayers, speaking the truth, helping others and being thankful to Him for His blessings. We should also take care of His creations, like birds, trees and animals.
  • Q: Write a note on the blessings of Allah for us.
    Ans: Allah has given us countless blessings. He gave us the sun for light and heat, stars and the moon at night, air to breathe, water to drink, trees that sway in the air, flowers that bloom, and birds that enjoy their share. He is always with us when we smile or weep and when we need care. We should be grateful to Allah for all these blessings and thank Him every day.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension i. Answer these questions

  • Q: In which things does the poet see Allah?
    Ans: The poet sees Allah in the stars when the night glows with spark, in the trees swaying in the air, and in the birds enjoying their share. She also feels His presence in the flowers blooming in a queue.
  • Q: When does the poet feel the presence of Allah?
    Ans: The poet feels the presence of Allah when she needs a lot of care. She also feels that Allah is with her when she smiles or when she weeps, and when no one else can hear her or support her.
  • Q: Why does the poet want more love from Allah?
    Ans: The poet wants more love from Allah because no one else can support her smile or hear her when she bitterly sheds her tears; she has judged this from far off miles. She asks Allah to enlighten her core, that is, to fill her heart with His light and love, and prays, 'O Allah! Just love me more!'

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension ii. Read the picture story (The Lion and the Mouse)

  • Q: Read the given pictures and the story. Retell the story of the lion and the mouse in the correct sequence.
    Ans: Once there was a lion sleeping in a forest. Suddenly a mouse came and climbed on its body. The lion got disturbed and woke up from his sleep. The lion angrily took hold of the tiny mouse. The mouse pleaded with the lion to let him go, saying he would help him in need. The lion laughed at the mouse and let him go. One day a hunter came and spread a net to catch the lion. The lion did not see the net and got stuck in it. He roared and tried to escape but failed. The mouse heard the lion's roars and came there. He started cutting the net with his teeth. The lion got out of the net and thanked the mouse. The mouse fulfilled his promise and saved the lion's life.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension iii. Look at the given pictures and write a story (The Ant and the Dove)

  • Q: Look at the given pictures and write a story in your notebook.
    Ans: The Ant and the Dove: Once an ant fell into a river and was about to drown. A dove was sitting on a branch of a tree above the river. She saw the ant in trouble. She plucked a leaf and dropped it into the water. The ant climbed onto the leaf and came safely to the bank. The ant thanked the dove. After some days, a hunter came and aimed at the dove sitting on the branch. The ant saw him and bit his foot hard. The hunter cried with pain and missed his aim. The dove flew away safely. In this way the ant repaid the dove's kindness. Moral: Do good and have good.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension iv. Read the poem again and fill in the blanks with the correct options

  • Q: The poet sees Allah in the ______ at night.
    Options: moon / sun / stars / clouds
    Ans: stars
  • Q: The poet says that the flowers ______ in a queue.
    Options: dry up / bloom / wither / fade
    Ans: bloom
  • Q: The poet wants ______.
    Options: father's love / mother's love / a friend's love / Allah's love
    Ans: Allah's love
  • Q: Allah is always ______ the poet when she cries or smiles.
    Options: away from / near / far from / beyond
    Ans: near
  • Q: When the poet needs a lot of care, ______ is always there.
    Options: her mother / her father / Allah / her brother
    Ans: Allah

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 2. Analytical Reading

  • Q: Read the poem again and make a list of the blessings of Allah mentioned in the poem.
    Ans: Blessings of Allah mentioned in the poem are: stars, the night that glows with spark, trees, air, birds, flowers, dew, sleep, smiles and tears (feelings), and Allah's care and presence with us at all times.
  • Q: Write a few lines about what life would be like if Allah's blessings (trees, birds, air, sun, water, etc.) were not there.
    Ans: If Allah's blessings were not there, life would not be possible. Without air we could not breathe, without water we could not drink or grow food, without the sun there would be no light or heat, without trees there would be no shade, fruit or clean air, and without birds and flowers the world would be silent and colourless. We should thank Allah for these blessings.

lessons.title: Language Focus
lessons.notes_html:
C) Language Focus — 1. Vocabulary Building i. Words with their meanings

  • Q: Match: spark
    Ans: a small flash of light
  • Q: Match: sway
    Ans: to move slowly from side to side
  • Q: Match: bitterly
    Ans: in a way that shows that you feel sad or angry
  • Q: Match: support
    Ans: to help or encourage somebody
  • Q: Match: enlighten
    Ans: to give somebody information so that they understand something better

C) Language Focus — 1. Vocabulary Building ii. Create a Poem 'Popcorn': put the given rhyming words in the blank spaces

  • Q: Pop pop popcorn / Popping in the ______!
    Ans: pot
  • Q: Pop pop popcorn / Eat it while its ______!
    Ans: hot
  • Q: Pop pop popcorn / Butter on the ______!
    Ans: top
  • Q: When I eat popcorn / I can't ______!
    Ans: stop

C) Language Focus — 1. Vocabulary Building iii. Create your own poem by using rhyming words of your own

  • Q: Now create your own poem by using rhyming words of your own.
    Ans: Model poem: The sun is bright in the sky so high, / The birds are singing as they fly. / The flowers bloom in red and blue, / And sparkle softly with the dew. / I thank Allah for this day, / For all His blessings on my way.

C) Language Focus — 1. Vocabulary Building: Expressing an Opinion iv–v

  • Q: Read the given expressions carefully. Which expressions are used to express an opinion, and which are used to respond to an opinion?
    Ans: To express an opinion we say: 'In my opinion...', 'Personally, I think...', 'In my experience...' and 'As far as I am concerned...'. To respond to an opinion we say: 'You're absolutely right.', 'Yes, I agree.', 'I don't agree with you.' and 'Of course.'
  • Q: Read the given dialogue (Danish and Ali) and notice the use of these expressions. What opinion does Ali express about a good friend?
    Ans: Ali expresses the opinion that a friend is someone who is fun to be with. He says he likes friends who go out and have fun together. He explains that a friend does not have to like the same things; he should have a jolly personality and be fun to be with whatever they do.

C) Language Focus — 1. Vocabulary Building: Offering and Accepting an Apology vi–vii

  • Q: Read the given expressions of offering an apology. List them.
    Ans: Expressions for offering an apology are: 'Sorry. It was all my fault.', 'Pardon me.', 'Please accept my apology.' and 'I'm so sorry.'
  • Q: Read the given expressions of accepting an apology. List them.
    Ans: Expressions for accepting an apology are: 'It's okay.', 'Don't worry about this.', 'That's okay.' and 'No problem.'
  • Q: Read the given dialogue (Sara and Miss Amna) and notice the use of these expressions. How does Sara offer her apology, and how does Miss Amna respond?
    Ans: Sara offers her apology by saying, 'I'm sorry I didn't bring my English workbook. I was doing my homework last night. I left it on my table.' Miss Amna accepts it kindly and advises her, 'Be careful next time. Make sure that you bring it tomorrow.' Sara promises to be careful next time and thanks her.

C) Language Focus — 1. Vocabulary Building viii. Write a dialogue of your own using the expressions given above

  • Q: Write a dialogue of your own using the expressions of offering and accepting an apology in your notebook.
    Ans: Model dialogue: Usman: I'm so sorry, Ahmed. I have lost your pencil. It was all my fault. Please accept my apology. Ahmed: It's okay, Usman. Don't worry about this. Usman: Thank you. I will buy you a new pencil tomorrow. Ahmed: No problem. You are my friend.

C) Language Focus — 2. Learning to Spell: Fill in the missing letters to complete the words

  • Q: ju______ge
    Ans: judge
  • Q: qu______ue
    Ans: queue
  • Q: presen______e
    Ans: presence
  • Q: ______nlighten
    Ans: enlighten
  • Q: bitt______rly
    Ans: bitterly

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar: Regular and Irregular Nouns i. Read the given regular and irregular nouns

  • Q: Give the plural of the regular noun 'day'.
    Ans: days
  • Q: Give the plural of the regular noun 'bag'.
    Ans: bags
  • Q: Give the plural of the regular noun 'bench'.
    Ans: benches
  • Q: Give the plural of the regular noun 'fox'.
    Ans: foxes
  • Q: Give the plural of the irregular noun 'man'.
    Ans: men
  • Q: Give the plural of the irregular noun 'foot'.
    Ans: feet
  • Q: Give the plural of the irregular noun 'mouse'.
    Ans: mice
  • Q: Give the plural of the irregular noun 'tooth'.
    Ans: teeth

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar ii. Write plurals of the given regular and irregular nouns

  • Q: Write the plural of the regular noun 'tree'.
    Ans: trees
  • Q: Write the plural of the regular noun 'table'.
    Ans: tables
  • Q: Write the plural of the regular noun 'bush'.
    Ans: bushes
  • Q: Write the plural of the regular noun 'page'.
    Ans: pages
  • Q: Write the plural of the irregular noun 'woman'.
    Ans: women
  • Q: Write the plural of the irregular noun 'goose'.
    Ans: geese
  • Q: Write the plural of the irregular noun 'ox'.
    Ans: oxen
  • Q: Write the plural of the irregular noun 'child'.
    Ans: children

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar iii. Rewrite the sentences using the correct plural forms of the underlined nouns and write the underlined words in the correct columns

  • Q: Rewrite using plurals: 'This cat is chasing the mouse.' Also write the underlined words in the correct columns.
    Ans: Rewritten: These cats are chasing the mice. Columns — Regular nouns: cat; Irregular nouns: mouse.
  • Q: Rewrite using plurals: 'There was a man and a woman at the party.' Also write the underlined words in the correct columns.
    Ans: Rewritten: There were men and women at the party. Columns — Regular nouns: none; Irregular nouns: man, woman.
  • Q: Rewrite using plurals: 'The dentist will examine my tooth.' Also write the underlined words in the correct columns.
    Ans: Rewritten: The dentists will examine my teeth. Columns — Regular nouns: dentist; Irregular nouns: tooth.
  • Q: Rewrite using plurals: 'The girls put a glass and a plate on the table.' Also write the underlined words in the correct columns.
    Ans: Rewritten: The girls put glasses and plates on the tables. Columns — Regular nouns: girls, glass, plate, table; Irregular nouns: none.
  • Q: Rewrite using plurals: 'My mother bought a book.' Also write the underlined words in the correct columns.
    Ans: Rewritten: My mothers bought books. Columns — Regular nouns: mother, book; Irregular nouns: none.

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar: Definite Article (the) iv. Notice the use of the definite article 'the'

  • Q: When do we use 'the' for something already known or previously mentioned? Give the book's examples.
    Ans: We use 'the' when we talk about something already known or previously mentioned. Examples: 'I have a parrot. The parrot is green.' and 'Do you know where I left the keys?'
  • Q: When do we use 'the' to define or identify a particular person or object? Give the book's examples.
    Ans: Examples: 'Can you see the boy in the red shirt?' and 'The man who wrote this book is famous.'
  • Q: When do we use 'the' for people or objects that are unique? Give the book's examples.
    Ans: Examples: 'Clouds drifted across the sky.', 'The sun sets at 7 o'clock in the evening.'
  • Q: When do we use 'the' before superlatives and ordinal numbers? Give the book's examples.
    Ans: Examples: 'This is the highest building in Lahore.' and 'This is the third time I have called you today.'
  • Q: When do we use 'the' with nouns to refer to a whole group of people? Give the book's examples.
    Ans: Examples: 'The giraffe is the tallest animal.' and 'She has given a lot of money to the poor.'
  • Q: When do we use 'the' with the names of rivers, mountain ranges, groups of islands, canals and oceans? Give the book's examples.
    Ans: Examples: 'Their ship crossed the Atlantic in three days.', 'They caught fish from the Ravi.' and 'Hiking across the Himalayas would be difficult.'
  • Q: When do we use 'the' with the names of famous buildings, museums or monuments? Give the book's examples.
    Ans: Examples: 'We went to the Lahore Museum.' and 'Sara visited the Faisal Mosque.'

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar v. Fill in the blanks with the correct articles (a / an / the)

  • Q: Asia is ______ largest continent in the world.
    Ans: the
  • Q: My cousin is ______ doctor.
    Ans: a
  • Q: There is ______ orange on the table.
    Ans: an
  • Q: Bring me ______ bottle of water.
    Ans: a
  • Q: Sadia is ______ honest girl.
    Ans: an
  • Q: He quickly ate ______ cake.
    Ans: the

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar vi. Rewrite each sentence using the correct articles

  • Q: Rewrite using the correct articles: 'Indus is longest river in Pakistan.'
    Ans: The Indus is the longest river in Pakistan.
  • Q: Rewrite using the correct articles: 'He is MA.' (printed in the book as 'BHe is MA.')
    Ans: He is an M.A.
  • Q: Rewrite using the correct articles: 'He lives in house next to ours.'
    Ans: He lives in the house next to ours.
  • Q: Rewrite using the correct articles: 'His father likes to read Daily News.'
    Ans: His father likes to read the Daily News.
  • Q: Rewrite using the correct articles: 'You can go anywhere in world.'
    Ans: You can go anywhere in the world.
  • Q: Note: misprint in the book (printed page 22, exercise vi)
    Ans: The second sentence of this exercise is printed in the book as 'BHe is MA.' The extra letter 'B' at the start is a printing mistake; the sentence should read 'He is MA.' It has been solved above in that corrected form.

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar: 'A' and 'an' with mute consonant letters vii. Notice the use of 'a' and 'an' with mute consonant letters

  • Q: In 'Sara had returned after an hour', why is 'an' used before 'hour'?
    Ans: 'an' is used because the 'h' in 'hour' is mute (not pronounced), so the word begins with a vowel sound. We choose 'a' or 'an' by focusing on the second letter's sound.
  • Q: In 'Yousaf is an honourable citizen', why is 'an' used before 'honourable'?
    Ans: 'an' is used because the 'h' in 'honourable' is mute and the word begins with a vowel sound.
  • Q: In 'His father is an honest businessman', why is 'an' used before 'honest'?
    Ans: 'an' is used because the 'h' in 'honest' is mute and the word begins with a vowel sound.
  • Q: In 'He gave him a wrapped gift box', why is 'a' used before 'wrapped'?
    Ans: 'a' is used because the 'w' in 'wrapped' is mute and the word begins with the consonant sound 'r'.
  • Q: In 'My mother bought a wrist watch', why is 'a' used before 'wrist'?
    Ans: 'a' is used because the 'w' in 'wrist' is mute and the word begins with the consonant sound 'r'.
  • Q: In 'Bring a knife from the kitchen', why is 'a' used before 'knife'?
    Ans: 'a' is used because the 'k' in 'knife' is mute and the word begins with the consonant sound 'n'.
  • Q: In 'The teacher has shown the diagram of a knee', why is 'a' used before 'knee'?
    Ans: 'a' is used because the 'k' in 'knee' is mute and the word begins with the consonant sound 'n'.

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar: Degrees of Regular Adjectives viii. Read the given degrees of regular adjectives with their sentences

  • Q: Give the comparative and superlative degrees of 'long' with the book's sentences.
    Ans: Positive: long — 'This path is long.' Comparative: longer — 'This path is longer than that.' Superlative: longest — 'This path is the longest.'
  • Q: Give the comparative and superlative degrees of 'heavy' with the book's sentences.
    Ans: Positive: heavy — 'My bag is heavy.' Comparative: heavier — 'My bag is heavier than yours.' Superlative: heaviest — 'My bag is the heaviest.'
  • Q: Give the comparative and superlative degrees of 'small' with the book's sentences.
    Ans: Positive: small — 'This is a small box.' Comparative: smaller — 'This box is smaller than yours.' Superlative: smallest — 'It is the smallest box in this room.'
  • Q: Give the comparative and superlative degrees of 'tall' with the book's sentences.
    Ans: Positive: tall — 'Her brother is tall.' Comparative: taller — 'Her brother is taller than mine.' Superlative: tallest — 'Her brother is the tallest boy in our school.'
  • Q: Give the comparative and superlative degrees of 'big' with the book's sentences.
    Ans: Positive: big — 'My house is big.' Comparative: bigger — 'My house is bigger than yours.' Superlative: biggest — 'My house is the biggest house in the town.'

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar ix. Write the degrees of the given regular adjectives and use them in your own sentences

  • Q: Write the degrees of 'large' and use them in your own sentences.
    Ans: large — larger — largest. Sentences: Our school has a large playground. His house is larger than mine. This is the largest city of our country.
  • Q: Write the degrees of 'young' and use them in your own sentences.
    Ans: young — younger — youngest. Sentences: Ali is a young boy. He is younger than his brother. She is the youngest girl in the class.
  • Q: Write the degrees of 'great' and use them in your own sentences.
    Ans: great — greater — greatest. Sentences: Quaid-e-Azam was a great leader. His courage was greater than others'. He is the greatest leader of our nation.
  • Q: Write the degrees of 'old' and use them in your own sentences.
    Ans: old — older — oldest. Sentences: My grandfather is an old man. He is older than my father. He is the oldest man in our village.
  • Q: Write the degrees of 'fast' and use them in your own sentences.
    Ans: fast — faster — fastest. Sentences: The horse runs fast. A car is faster than a bicycle. The train is the fastest of them all.

lessons.title: Writing
lessons.notes_html:
D) Writing — 1. Learning to Write i. Notice the use of conjunctions in the given sentences

  • Q: Read the given sentences about Ali and Ahmad and list the conjunctions used in them.
    Ans: The conjunctions used are 'and', 'because', 'so' and 'or'. 'and' joins 'Ali and Ahmad' and 'played and jumped'; 'because' gives the reason ('because it was raining outside'); 'so' shows the result ('Ali was hungry so he went to the kitchen'); 'or' shows a choice ('Do you like to take chips or biscuits?'). Conjunctions are words that join words, phrases or sentences.

D) Writing — 1. Learning to Write ii. Write a few sentences using the above conjunctions

  • Q: Write a few sentences using the conjunctions 'and', 'but', 'or', 'because' and 'so' in your notebook.
    Ans: Model sentences: (1) and — Sana and Fatima are good friends. (2) but — He is poor but honest. (3) or — Do you want tea or juice? (4) because — I stayed at home because I was ill. (5) so — It was raining, so we did not go to the park.

D) Writing — 1. Learning to Write iii. Notice the use of transitional words in the given sentences

  • Q: Read the given sentences and notice the use of the transitional words 'for example', 'for instance' and 'therefore'. What is each used for?
    Ans: 'For example' and 'for instance' are used to illustrate what has been said: 'We eat healthy food; for example eggs, milk, fruit and vegetables.' and 'For instance, delight is the opposite of sorrow.' 'Therefore' is used to show the result of an action: 'She came first therefore she got admission to a good college.' and 'I'm sleepy therefore I'm going to bed.' Transitional words carry a thought from one sentence to another.

D) Writing — 1. Learning to Write iv. Make two sentences each using the transitional words

  • Q: Make two sentences using the transitional word 'for example'.
    Ans: (1) We should eat healthy food; for example, fruit and vegetables. (2) Many animals live in the forest; for example, lions and deer.
  • Q: Make two sentences using the transitional word 'for instance'.
    Ans: (1) For instance, patience is a good quality for students. (2) We can save water in many ways; for instance, by closing the tap while brushing our teeth.
  • Q: Make two sentences using the transitional word 'therefore'.
    Ans: (1) He worked hard; therefore he passed the exam. (2) It is very hot today; therefore we should drink a lot of water.

D) Writing — 1. Learning to Write v. Circle those things from the given items that you need for making a card

  • Q: From the given items (plain paper, football, colour pencil, scissors, a pencil), circle those things that you need for making a card.
    Ans: Things needed for making a card: plain paper, colour pencil, scissors and a pencil. A football is not needed for making a card.

D) Writing — 1. Learning to Write vi. Use the given pictures for writing the procedure of card making in correct sequence

  • Q: Use the given pictures for writing the procedure of card making in correct sequence.
    Ans: How to make a card: First, collect all the things you need: plain paper, scissors, glue, colour pencils and a pencil. Next, fold the paper in half to make the card. Then, cut small flowers and shapes from the coloured paper. After that, paste the flowers and shapes on the front of the card with glue. Finally, write a sweet message inside the card with a pencil and colour it beautifully. Your card is ready.

D) Writing — 2. Creative Writing: The Memorable Incident

  • Q: Write any incident of your life when you treated somebody with kindness.
    Ans: The Memorable Incident: One day I was coming home from school. I saw an old man standing at the roadside. He wanted to cross the busy road but he could not walk fast. I held his hand and helped him cross the road safely. He thanked me and prayed for me. I felt very happy. That day I learnt that treating others with kindness gives us real joy.

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Getting Started — Let's Talk

  • Q: Do you like seeing women in any of the above mentioned professions? Why?
    Ans: Yes, I like seeing women in these professions, such as nurse, teacher, cook and police officer. The lesson says that whenever females get suitable circumstances, they perform well and achieve their goals, so women should be encouraged to work in every profession.

Pre-reading

  • Q: Read the title and guess what the text can be about. Share the names of some notable women of Pakistan.
    Ans: The title 'Women as Role Models' tells us that the text is about women who inspire us by their good work. Some notable women of Pakistan discussed in the lesson are Miss Fatima Jinnah, Dr. Ruth Pfau, Arfa Abdul Karim Randhawa and Samina Khayal Baig.

While-reading

  • Q: Which committee did Fatima Jinnah form for women?
    Ans: Fatima Jinnah formed the Women's Relief Committee, which was later renamed as All Pakistan Women's Association.

Post-reading

  • Q: Which award did Arfa get at the age of nine?
    Ans: At the age of nine, Arfa Abdul Karim Randhawa achieved the world's youngest Microsoft Certified Professional award.
  • Q: Why should we respect our national heroes? Discuss it in five lines.
    Ans: We should respect our national heroes because they worked hard for our country. They served the people selflessly and made Pakistan proud in the whole world. Their lives teach us honesty, courage and hard work. By following their example, we can also become successful and useful citizens. Respecting them keeps their great work alive in our hearts.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension — i. Answer these questions

  • Q: Why did the people of Pakistan give the title of 'Madar-e-Millat' to Fatima Jinnah?
    Ans: The people of Pakistan gave Fatima Jinnah the title of 'Madar-e-Millat', or 'Mother of the Nation', because of her un-tiring efforts. She was an inspiration to many Muslim women, especially during the Pakistan Movement, and she formed the Women's Relief Committee for women.
  • Q: What is the role of Ruth Pfau in controlling leprosy in Pakistan?
    Ans: Dr. Ruth Pfau devoted her life to fighting leprosy in Pakistan. She travelled across Pakistan to rescue patients suffering from leprosy and set up 150 leprosy clinics throughout the country. Because of her efforts, the disease came under control in 1996.
  • Q: Write a few sentences about how females contribute in the development of a society.
    Ans: Females contribute to the development of a society in many ways. They work as teachers, doctors, nurses and officers and serve the people. Educated women educate their children and build a better future generation. As the lesson shows, whenever females get suitable circumstances, they perform well and achieve their goals.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension — ii. Read the given paragraph. Notice the use of transitional devices

  • Q: Which transitional devices are used in the paragraph about John and the wheelchair race?
    Ans: The transitional devices used are 'whereas' (John loves playing games, whereas his sister likes to read storybooks), 'First', 'then' and 'Finally'. Transitional devices connect sentences or paragraphs and carry a thought from one sentence to another to create flow and coherence.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension — iii. Write a short paragraph using the words first, then, next, finally and however (beginning: 'First, we boil some water to make a cup of tea.')

  • Q: Write the short paragraph about making a cup of tea using first, then, next, finally and however.
    Ans: First, we boil some water to make a cup of tea. Then, we pour the hot water into a teapot and add tea leaves. Next, we let the tea brew for a few minutes and add milk and sugar. However, if the tea becomes too strong, we can add a little more milk. Finally, we pour the tea into cups and serve it hot.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension — iv. Look at the picture and answer the following questions using position words in complete sentences

  • Q: Where is the cow standing?
    Ans: The cow is standing in the green field on the other side of the stream.
  • Q: Where is the boy sitting?
    Ans: The boy is sitting on the grass near the stream.
  • Q: Where is the sun?
    Ans: The sun is shining in the sky above the hills.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension — v. Read the lesson again and fill in the blanks with the correct options

  • Q: Arfa flew her first aircraft at the age of ______.
    Ans: ten
  • Q: Ruth Pfau was a ______ doctor.
    Ans: German
  • Q: Fatima Jinnah was a ______ by profession.
    Ans: dentist
  • Q: Samina Baig is the first Pakistani ______ to climb The Mount Everest.
    Ans: woman

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 2. Analytical Reading

  • Q: Use the internet and read why education is important for women. Write five benefits of woman education.
    Ans: Five benefits of women's education are: 1) An educated woman can get a good job and support her family. 2) She can educate her children well. 3) She can take better care of her family's health. 4) She can take part in the development of society like the role models in this lesson. 5) She becomes confident and can achieve her goals in life.

    Ans: The nouns 'sheep' and 'goldfish' do not change: 'The sheep is running fast / The sheep are running fast' and 'There is a goldfish in the pond / There are goldfish in the pond.' Other such nouns given in the book are deer, fish and sheep.

D) Writing — 1. Learning to Write — i. Read the speech bubbles / ii. Fill in the speech bubbles

    Ans: Girl: Look at that tall green tree! Girl (second bubble): Many birds live in its branches and rest in its shade.

D) Writing — 2. Creative Writing: Write a biography of your favourite personality in your notebook

  • Q: Write a biography of your favourite personality, covering date/place of birth, education, career, reason for fame and major achievements. (Model: Fatima Jinnah)
    Ans: Fatima Jinnah was born in 1893. She was the younger sister of Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah. Her keen interest in education helped her complete her studies, and she became a dentist by profession. Later she gave up her profession to help her brother in the Pakistan Movement, which made her famous as a great leader of Muslim women. Her major achievement was forming the Women's Relief Committee, later renamed the All Pakistan Women's Association. Due to her un-tiring efforts, she got the title of 'Madar-e-Millat', or 'Mother of the Nation'. She died in Karachi on July 8, 1967.

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension: Answer the given questions

  • Q: Write four to five sentences on your favourite female personality.
    Ans: My favourite female personality is Samina Khayal Baig. She is the first Pakistani woman to climb Mount Everest and the first Muslim lady to climb all Seven Summits. She was born on September 19, 1990, in Shimshal village in Hunza Gojal, Gilgit-Baltistan. She loved climbing mountains, and her brother supported and guided her in her mountaineering career. Her hard work and courage make her a true role model for girls.
  • Q: How do we show our love to Allah?
    Ans: We show our love to Allah by obeying His commands and following the teachings of Islam. We pray five times a day, keep fasts, give charity and speak the truth. We also thank Him for His blessings and help His creatures. Loving Allah means doing good deeds and staying away from sins.
  • Q: Why was our last Rasoolullah called Saadiq and Ameen?
    Ans: Our last Rasoolullah was called Saadiq because he always spoke the truth and never told a lie. He was called Ameen because he was completely trustworthy and honest; people kept their precious things with him as a trust and he always returned them safely.

lessons.notes_html:
C) Language Focus — 1. Vocabulary Building: Read the given words and write their meanings

  • Q: What is the meaning of 'inspiration'?

  • Q: What is the meaning of 'support'?
    Ans: Help or encouragement given to someone.
  • Q: What is the meaning of 'fascinating'?
    Ans: Very interesting and attractive.
  • Q: What is the meaning of 'bitterly'?
    Ans: In a very unhappy, angry or painful way; for example, crying bitterly means crying with deep pain.
  • Q: What is the meaning of 'courage'?
    Ans: Bravery; the strength to face danger or difficulty without fear.

    Ans: A herd of cattle is grazing in the field.

    Ans: A flock of birds is flying in the sky.

D) Writing — 1. Creative Writing: Write a paragraph on the topic 'health is wealth'. Also underline its topic sentence

  • Q: Write a paragraph on 'health is wealth' and underline its topic sentence.
    Ans: Topic sentence (to be underlined): Health is wealth, because a healthy person can enjoy every blessing of life. A person who is healthy can work hard, study well and play happily. Money cannot buy good health, and a sick rich man cannot enjoy his wealth. We should eat simple and clean food, exercise daily and keep ourselves clean. In this way, we can stay healthy and live a happy life.

mcqs.why: The paragraph clearly says: 'Money cannot buy good health', however rich a person may be.

chapters.title: Unit 4: Unforgettable Moments of My Life

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Getting Started — Let's Talk

  • Q: What would happen if there were no trees in the world?
    Ans: If there were no trees in the world, animals would lose their homes, because trees are home to many animals. Humans would not get enough oxygen, and carbon dioxide would increase air pollution. The world would become hot, dry and unpleasant for all living things.
  • Q: Have you ever planted a seedling or asked anyone to help you plant one?
    Ans: Model answer: Yes, I have planted a seedling in my school garden. My teacher helped me dig a small hole, put the seedling in it and water it. Now I take care of it every day.
  • Q: What steps would you take to reduce deforestation?
    Ans: To reduce deforestation, I would plant more trees and take care of them. I would stop people from cutting trees without need and tell others about the importance of trees. I would also take part in tree-plantation activities at my school.

Pre-reading

  • Q: Look at the pictures and read the title of the lesson. Guess five words related to it.
    Ans: Five words related to the title 'Unforgettable Moments of My Life' are: visit, farmhouse, trees, garden and trip. The lesson is about a memorable visit to a grandparents' farmhouse in Swat.
  • Q: Have you ever visited a farm or any other place surrounded by natural beauty?
    Ans: Model answer: Yes, I have visited a farm surrounded by natural beauty. It had tall green trees, colourful flowers and feathery birds all around, which made the surroundings pleasant and vivid.

While-reading

  • Q: Why was the writer shocked to see the farmhouse?
    Ans: The writer was shocked to see the poor condition of the farmhouse. There was nothing but burnt yellow grass with bushes everywhere, and the plants had wilted, although the farmhouse used to have tall dense trees and a lush grassy floor.
  • Q: How do you take care of your plants?
    Ans: Model answer: I take care of my plants by watering them regularly. I keep them in sunlight, remove dry leaves and protect them from insects. I also add fertilizer so that they grow healthy and green.
  • Q: Can you tell the names of two places you have visited in Pakistan?
    Ans: Model answer: I have visited Swat and Hunza in Pakistan. Both places are famous for their natural beauty, tall trees and pleasant surroundings.

Post-reading

  • Q: What were the writer's feelings when he saw the burnt grass and wilted plants?
    Ans: The writer was shocked and sad when he saw the burnt grass and wilted plants. He murmured, 'Oh my God! What happened to them?' and ran in to ask his grandparents the reason behind it.
  • Q: What did you feel when you read this story?
    Ans: Model answer: I felt sad when I read about the poor condition of the farmhouse, but I felt happy and inspired at the end. The writer and his family worked together with full energy and restored the farmhouse to its original condition within a month.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension — i. Answer these questions

  • Q: What happened to the grandfather's farmhouse?
    Ans: The farmhouse fell into a poor condition. Its gardener, who used to take care of the garden, had passed away due to illness, and the grandparents were not able to pay as much attention as required. So there was nothing but burnt yellow grass with bushes everywhere, and the plants had wilted.
  • Q: How did the writer restore his grandparent's farmhouse?
    Ans: The writer decided to bring the same scenery back with the help of his father, sister and brothers. He requested his father to assign different responsibilities to them: his elder brothers took charge of bringing fertilizer from the market and planting new plants, his sister was to water plants in the afternoon, and he himself took care of the nests. Working with full energy, they got everything back to the way it used to be within a month's time.
  • Q: How can you restore a garden in your surroundings?
    Ans: I can restore a garden in my surroundings by working together with my family and friends. We can divide the responsibilities: some can bring fertilizer and plant new plants, some can water the plants daily, and some can clean the garden and take care of the nests. With regular care and full energy, the garden will become green again.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension — ii. Look at the picture and notice the use of positions and directions in the sentences given below

  • Q: Read the sentences under the picture and name the position words used.
    Ans: The position words used are: 'in' (The birds are flying in the air), 'above' (The girl is ziplining above the pond), 'on' (The frog is sitting on a lotus leaf), 'under' (The rabbit is sitting under the tree), 'in front of' (The boy is standing in front of the pond) and 'between' (The sun is between the clouds).

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension — iii. Look at the given picture and write five sentences about it using the position words above

  • Q: Write five sentences about the picture of the kennel and the pond using position words.
    Ans: 1) The dog is sitting in the kennel. 2) A bird is sitting on the roof of the kennel. 3) The fish are swimming in the pond. 4) A duck is swimming on the pond. 5) The butterflies are flying above the pond.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension — iv. Write a sentence to describe each picture

  • Q: Write a sentence to describe the first picture (a boy with a watering can).
    Ans: The boy is watering a small potted plant with a watering can.
  • Q: Write a sentence to describe the second picture (a man in a field).
    Ans: The man is planting a seedling in the field.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension — v. Read the lesson again and fill in the blanks with the correct options

  • Q: His grandparents' farmhouse had ______ dense trees.
    Options: short / green / tall / yellow
    Ans: tall
  • Q: The writer's family decided to visit ______.
    Options: Multan / Kashmir / Swat / Hunza
    Ans: Swat
  • Q: The writer was shocked to see the condition of the ______.
    Options: swing / farmhouse / the Jhelum river / zip lines
    Ans: farmhouse
  • Q: The writer decided to restore ______ of the farmhouse.
    Options: greenery / electricity / gas / animals
    Ans: greenery
  • Q: The writer had ______ siblings.
    Options: five / three / two / four
    Ans: three

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 2. Analytical Reading

  • Q: Find and read information about any two famous hill stations of Pakistan on the internet and write their comparison in your notebook.
    Ans: Model comparison: Swat and Hunza are two famous hill stations of Pakistan. Swat is a green valley with a river, tall dense trees and pleasant surroundings, and visitors enjoy zip lines there. Hunza is also famous for its natural beauty, with very high mountains and fresh air. Both places have cool weather and beautiful scenery, but Swat is greener with more forests, while Hunza has higher and drier mountains.

mcqs.why: The writer visited his grandparents in Swat, and the family later visited Swat Valley and rode the zip lines there.

mcqs.why: The writer says, 'I was shocked to see the poor condition of the farmhouse', with burnt yellow grass and wilted plants.

mcqs.why: He decided to bring the same scenery back and restore the greenery of the farmhouse with his family's help.

mcqs.why: The writer worked with his sister and his elder brothers — three siblings in all, as the book's correct option shows.

mcqs.why: The solved answer says his elder brothers took charge of bringing fertilizer from the market and planting new plants.

mcqs.why: The solved answer says: 'I had the responsibility of taking care of the nests', where he saw many frightening insects.

lessons.title: Sounds and Speaking
lessons.notes_html:
A) Oral Communication — 1. Learning the Sounds: Diphthongs — i. Read the given sentences and pronounce the diphthongs

  • Q: In August, I'm going to Hunza with my family. — Which word has a diphthong?
    Ans: 'going' — the diphthong letters are 'oi' in 'going'. A diphthong is a combination of two vowel sounds in a single syllable.
  • Q: They arrived in the town. — Which word has a diphthong?
    Ans: 'town' — the diphthong is 'ow' in 'town'.
  • Q: We dared each other to try the zip lines. — Which word has a diphthong?
    Ans: 'dared' — the diphthong is 'are' in 'dared'.
  • Q: We love to see birds flying in the sky. — Which word has a diphthong?
    Ans: 'flying' — the diphthong is 'y' in 'flying' (also in 'sky').
  • Q: His grandparents' farmhouse had tall, dense trees. — Which word has a diphthong?
    Ans: 'house' in 'farmhouse' — the diphthong is 'ou' in 'house'.

A) Oral Communication — 1. Learning the Sounds: Diphthongs — ii. Read the lesson again and circle five words with diphthongs. Make sentences with the words in your notebook

  • Q: Circle a word with a diphthong from the lesson and make a sentence with it: farmhouse
    Ans: Sentence: His grandparents' farmhouse had tall, dense trees.
  • Q: Circle a word with a diphthong from the lesson and make a sentence with it: around
    Ans: Sentence: Feathery birds were all around the farmhouse.
  • Q: Circle a word with a diphthong from the lesson and make a sentence with it: excited
    Ans: Sentence: My family and I were very excited about this visit.
  • Q: Circle a word with a diphthong from the lesson and make a sentence with it: decided
    Ans: Sentence: We decided to ride zip lines in Swat Valley.
  • Q: Circle a word with a diphthong from the lesson and make a sentence with it: time
    Ans: Sentence: We got everything back to the way it used to be within a month's time.

A) Oral Communication — 2. Learning to Speak — i. Read and practise the given dialogue / ii. Get students into pairs and ask them to share some information and instructions from a tourist guide

  • Q: In the dialogue, why do we need to plant trees, according to Miss Rabia?
    Ans: Miss Rabia says we need to plant trees because trees help us in many ways. They provide oxygen, control levels of carbon dioxide in the air, help to maintain the ecological balance, provide home to birds and prevent soil erosion.
  • Q: Work in pairs and share some information and instructions from a tourist guide.
    Ans: Model answer — Tourist guide: Welcome to Swat Valley. Please stay on the marked paths and do not throw litter in the river. You may ride the zip lines one by one, and please hold the rope firmly. Do not cut any tree or flower during your visit.

mcqs.q: What is a diphthong?
options: A combination of two vowel sounds or letters in a single syllable
A combination of two consonant sounds in a word
A letter that is not pronounced in a word
A group of three consonant letters
mcqs.why: The book's Read Me says a diphthong is a combination of two vowel sounds or letters in a single syllable, e.g. soil, plain, cow.

mcqs.why: The solved answer says the diphthong in 'house' is 'ou', as in 'His grandparents' farmhouse had tall, dense trees'.

mcqs.why: The solved answer marks 'flying' for its diphthong, and the same sound is also heard in 'sky' at the end of the sentence.

mcqs.q: Which letters make the diphthong in the word 'around' from the lesson?
mcqs.why: In 'Feathery birds were all around the farmhouse', the word 'around' carries the 'ou' diphthong, like 'house'.

mcqs.why: The solved answer uses 'time' from 'within a month's time' as a lesson word with a diphthong sound.

mcqs.q: In 'We dared each other to try the zip lines', the book marks the diphthong in 'dared' as:
mcqs.why: The solved answer says the diphthong in 'dared' is 'are', the vowel sound in the middle of the word.

mcqs.q: In 'His grandparents' farmhouse had tall, dense trees', the diphthong is in the word:
mcqs.why: The solved answer points to 'house' in 'farmhouse', whose 'ou' makes the diphthong in this sentence.

mcqs.q: According to Miss Rabia in the dialogue, trees provide home to:
mcqs.why: Miss Rabia says trees provide oxygen, control carbon dioxide, maintain the ecological balance, provide home to birds and prevent soil erosion.

mcqs.q: What does the tourist guide in the pair-work model answer ask visitors to do?
options: Cut any tree or flower during the visit
Throw litter in the river to feed fish
Stay on the marked paths and do not throw litter in the river
Ride the zip lines together at the same time

lessons.title: Language Focus
lessons.notes_html:
C) Language Focus — 1. Vocabulary Building — i. Read the given words with their meanings and practise them in your conversation

  • Q: What is the meaning of 'exotic'?
    Ans: brightly-coloured / exciting and unusual / foreign
  • Q: What is the meaning of 'vivid'?
    Ans: bright / clear
  • Q: What is the meaning of 'shocked'?
    Ans: very surprised
  • Q: What is the meaning of 'opt'?
    Ans: choose

C) Language Focus — 1. Vocabulary Building: Anagrams — ii. Read the given anagrams / iii. Make anagrams from the given words

  • Q: Read the given anagrams: what words are made by rearranging the letters of 'nest', 'silent', 'flow' and 'team'?
    Ans: nest — sent, tens; silent — enlist, listen; flow — fowl, wolf; team — mate, meat. An anagram is a word made by rearranging the letters of another word.
  • Q: Make an anagram from the word 'felt'.
    Ans: left
  • Q: Make an anagram from the word 'care'.
    Ans: race
  • Q: Make an anagram from the word 'taste'.
    Ans: state
  • Q: Make an anagram from the word 'heart'.
    Ans: earth
  • Q: Make an anagram from the word 'thing'.
    Ans: night
  • Q: Make an anagram from the word 'hear'.
    Ans: hare

C) Language Focus — 2. Learning to Spell: Fill in the missing letters to complete the words and learn their spelling

  • Q: Fill in the missing letters: ex__tic
    Ans: exotic — the missing letter is 'o'.
  • Q: Fill in the missing letters: e__perien__e
    Ans: experience — the missing letters are 'x' and 'c'.
  • Q: Fill in the missing letters: cree__y
    Ans: creepy — the missing letter is 'p'.
  • Q: Fill in the missing letters: v__vid
    Ans: vivid — the missing letter is 'i'.
  • Q: Fill in the missing letters: hung__y
    Ans: hungry — the missing letter is 'r'.

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar: Gender Nouns — i. Read the following use of gender nouns / ii. Classify the given gender nouns and write them in their respective columns

  • Q: Classify the given nouns in the Masculine column.
    Ans: Masculine: king, uncle, lion, prince. Masculine nouns are used for men, boys and male animals.
  • Q: Classify the given nouns in the Feminine column.
    Ans: Feminine: lioness, milkmaid, niece, goose. Feminine nouns are used for women, girls and female animals.
  • Q: Classify the given nouns in the Neuter column.
    Ans: Neuter: tree, chair, pencil, desk. Neuter refers to things that have no gender.

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar: Sentence Structures — iii. Read the given sentences and notice their structures

  • Q: Notice the structure: 'Toqeer planted a tree.' Name the subject, verb and direct object.
    Ans: Subject: Toqeer; verb: planted; direct object: a tree. Structure: Subject + verb + direct object.
  • Q: Notice the structure: 'Grandmother told the children a story.' Name the subject, verb, indirect object and direct object.
    Ans: Subject: Grandmother; verb: told; indirect object: the children; direct object: a story. Structure: Subject + verb + indirect object + direct object.

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar — iv. Write five sentences with direct and indirect objects each in your notebook

  • Q: Write a sentence with a direct and an indirect object (1 of 5).
    Ans: My father gave me an old watch. (Indirect object: me; direct object: an old watch.)
  • Q: Write a sentence with a direct and an indirect object (2 of 5).
    Ans: Mother told the children an old story. (Indirect object: the children; direct object: an old story.)
  • Q: Write a sentence with a direct and an indirect object (3 of 5).
    Ans: Ayesha bought her son a new car. (Indirect object: her son; direct object: a new car.)
  • Q: Write a sentence with a direct and an indirect object (4 of 5).
    Ans: The teacher gave the students a new lesson. (Indirect object: the students; direct object: a new lesson.)
  • Q: Write a sentence with a direct and an indirect object (5 of 5).
    Ans: Ali gave Ahmad a book. (Indirect object: Ahmad; direct object: a book.)

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar: Capitalisation — v. Read the following titles of books and the story to observe the use of capital letters / vi. Rewrite the following sentences in your notebook using correct capitalization

  • Q: Observe the use of capital letters in the given titles.
    Ans: The titles are written as: 'Two Little Kittens', 'Honesty is the Best Policy' and 'Colours of Pakistan'. The names of stories and books are proper nouns, and the keywords in their titles are written with capital letters.
  • Q: Rewrite using correct capitalization: 'toqeer is reading lifecycle of a plant'.
    Ans: Toqeer is reading 'Lifecycle of a Plant'.
  • Q: Rewrite using correct capitalization: 'the title of this book is my favourite memories'.
    Ans: The title of this book is 'My Favourite Memories'.
  • Q: Rewrite using correct capitalization: 'the zip line in malam jabba is 2,000 feet long and 1,000 feet high'.
    Ans: The zip line in Malam Jabba is 2,000 feet long and 1,000 feet high.
  • Q: Rewrite using correct capitalization: 'swat is famous for its natural beauty'.
    Ans: Swat is famous for its natural beauty.
  • Q: Rewrite using correct capitalization: 'an ant and a dove is a story with a moral'.
    Ans: 'An Ant and a Dove' is a story with a moral.
  • Q: Rewrite using correct capitalization: 'i bought a guide to travel in swat before visiting swat'.
    Ans: I bought 'A Guide to Travel in Swat' before visiting Swat.

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar: Capitalisation — vii. Make three sentences using the names of stories and books in your notebook. Remember to capitalise properly

  • Q: Make a sentence using the name of a story or book, capitalised properly (1 of 3).
    Ans: I have read the story 'An Ant and a Dove' in my English book.
  • Q: Make a sentence using the name of a story or book, capitalised properly (2 of 3).
    Ans: 'Honesty is the Best Policy' is my favourite story.
  • Q: Make a sentence using the name of a story or book, capitalised properly (3 of 3).
    Ans: Our teacher told us the story 'Two Little Kittens' in the class.

lessons.title: Writing
lessons.notes_html:
D) Writing — 1. Learning to Write — i. Read the given dialogue in the speech bubbles / ii. Fill in the speech bubbles to make your own dialogue

  • Q: Read the dialogue in the speech bubbles between the boy and his grandfather.
    Ans: Boy: Assalaamu Alaikum, grandfather! Grandfather: Wa Alaikum Assalaam! Boy: Can I get some red roses from your garden? Grandfather: Yes, you can. Boy: Thank you, grandfather! Grandfather: Welcome, dear! Speech bubbles tell us about the thoughts or words of characters.
  • Q: Fill in the speech bubbles to continue the dialogue that begins: 'What have you planned for the holidays?' — 'I am going to plant trees.'
    Ans: Boy: What have you planned for the holidays? Friend: I am going to plant trees. Boy: That is a great idea. Trees give us oxygen and shade. Friend: Yes, and they provide a home to birds. Boy: I will also join you and plant a tree. Friend: Sure! We will plant trees together in the holidays.

D) Writing — 1. Learning to Write — iii. Write a short paragraph in your notebook about the 'Benefits of Trees'. Remember to use correct capitalization and spelling

  • Q: Write a short paragraph about the 'Benefits of Trees'.
    Ans: Trees are very useful for us and for all living things. They provide us oxygen and control the levels of carbon dioxide in the air, which reduces air pollution. Trees are home to many animals and birds. They help to maintain the ecological balance and prevent soil erosion. We should plant more trees and take care of them.

D) Writing — 2. Creative Writing: Imagine you are experiencing zip lines. Write your feelings about it

  • Q: Imagine you are experiencing zip lines. Write your feelings about it.
    Ans: When I first stood on the hill to ride the zip line, I felt a little frightened but very excited. As I started moving from one hill to another, the cool wind touched my face and I could see the green trees and the pond below me. I dared myself to keep my eyes open, and soon my fear turned into joy. It was an exciting and memorable experience, and I will never forget those moments of my life.

mcqs.q: How did the writer feel when he first stood on the hill to ride the zip line?
options: A little frightened but very excited

options: The green trees and the pond
