lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Getting Started — Let's Talk

  • Q: Where do you live and what type of climate does your area have?
    Ans: Model answer: I live in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. My area has a varied climate. It is very hot in summer and cold in winter, and it rains in the monsoon season.
  • Q: Which season do you like the most? Why?
    Ans: Model answer: I like spring the most because the weather is pleasant, flowers bloom everywhere, the grass becomes soft and green, and birds sing in the trees.
  • Q: Do you go on vacation in summer? Is it the right season to stay home?
    Ans: Model answer: Yes, we usually go on vacation in the summer holidays. Summer is very hot, so it is a good season to visit cool hilly places, but staying home in the heat is not pleasant.
  • Q: Do you want to shift vacations to any other season? Why?
    Ans: Model answer: Yes, I would like some holidays in spring because the weather is mild and pleasant in spring, so we can enjoy travelling and outdoor activities more.

Reading Text 'I am the Earth' — Pre-reading, While-reading and Post-reading

  • Q: Pre-reading: What is pollution?
    Ans: Pollution is the dirt and harmful substances that make our air, water and land dirty and unsafe, for example smoke, plastic and waste thrown on the ground.
  • Q: Pre-reading: Do you keep your school and home clean?
    Ans: Model answer: Yes, I keep my school and home clean. I throw waste in the dustbin, do not use plastic bags, and help in cleaning my classroom and home.
  • Q: While-reading: Can you guess the meanings of the words 'regret' and 'fading'?
    Ans: 'Regret' means to feel sad and sorry about something. 'Fading' means becoming weaker, less bright and slowly coming to an end.
  • Q: Post-reading: What is climate change? Discuss.
    Ans: Climate change is a long-term change in the weather and climate of an area. Because of pollution, deforestation and rising temperature, seasons are changing and the Earth is getting warmer.
  • Q: Post-reading: What are reasons of climate change? Share your opinions.
    Ans: The main reasons of climate change are pollution from factories, power plants and vehicles, cutting down of trees (deforestation), and rising temperature. The mind map in the book also shows loss of fresh water resources as a result of climate change.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension: i. Answer these questions

  • Q: Explain the feelings of the Earth in your own words.
    Ans: The Earth feels sad and hurt because people destroy its skin and bone, throw plastic and waste, and pollute its air. Yet the Earth forgives people, forgets their mistakes and lets them live, but it regrets their behaviour and asks them to save it with love and care.
  • Q: Which problems are being faced by our Earth? Write some of them.
    Ans: Our Earth is facing pollution of air, water and land, too much plastic and waste, climate change and global warming. The Earth is fading at a fast pace because people are polluting its air.
  • Q: How can we keep our environment neat and clean? Discuss.
    Ans: We can keep our environment neat and clean by not throwing waste and plastic on the ground, putting rubbish in dustbins, planting more trees, keeping our homes, schools and streets clean, and not polluting the air and water.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension: ii. Read the given paragraph aloud and notice the use of punctuation marks

  • Q: Read the paragraph about the tour of the city aloud. Which punctuation marks are used in it?
    Ans: The paragraph uses capital letters at the start of sentences, full stops (.) at the end of sentences, commas (,) in the list 'a power plant, a factory and a workshop', and an exclamation mark (!) at the end of 'Time to think!' to show strong feeling.
  • Q: What did the children see on the tour of the city in the paragraph?
    Ans: They saw a power plant, a factory and a workshop with lots of smoke coming out of their chimneys, which made the sky look dark. They also saw a canal with dark water full of rubbish and dirty soil around it. There was a lot of pollution all around.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension: iii. Read the given affixes with their examples

  • Q: What is an affix? What are its two main types?
    Ans: An affix is added to the base form of a word to change its meaning. There are two main types of affixes: prefixes and suffixes. We add a prefix at the beginning and a suffix at the end of a word.
  • Q: Give the examples of prefixes given in the book.
    Ans: dis- in 'dislike', re- in 'recover', un- in 'unfriendly', and 'incorrect' (prefix in-).
  • Q: Give the examples of suffixes given in the book.
    Ans: -less in 'spotless', -ness in 'happiness', -al in 'logical', and -ship in 'friendship'.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension: iv. Make words with the given affixes

  • Q: Make a word with the prefix 'mis-'
    Ans: misunderstand (also: misbehave, misuse).
  • Q: Make a word with the prefix 'over-'
    Ans: overcome (also: overtake, overflow).
  • Q: Make a word with the prefix 'pre-'
    Ans: preview (also: preheat, prepaid).
  • Q: Make a word with the prefix 'im-'
    Ans: impossible (also: improper, impure).
  • Q: Make a word with the suffix '-wise'
    Ans: clockwise (also: likewise).
  • Q: Make a word with the suffix '-ful'
    Ans: beautiful (also: careful, helpful).
  • Q: Make a word with the suffix '-ly'
    Ans: quickly (also: happily, slowly).
  • Q: Make a word with the suffix '-ist'
    Ans: artist (also: dentist, scientist).

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension: v. Read the poem again and fill in the blanks

  • Q: The Earth is our ______.
    Ans: home
  • Q: We are destroying the Earth's skin and ______.
    Ans: bone
  • Q: We are polluting ______ of the Earth.
    Ans: air
  • Q: The Earth needs love and ______.
    Ans: care

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 2. Analytical Reading

  • Q: Visit your school library. Read some information about climate change. Note down some information in your notebook.
    Ans: Model notes: Climate change means the long-term change in weather patterns. It is caused by pollution, smoke from factories and vehicles, and cutting down trees. It makes the temperature rise, melts ice, and causes loss of fresh water. We can stop it by planting trees and reducing pollution.

A long-term change in the weather of an area
Clean water stored in a canal
A word part added to a base word

  • Q: Identify the common noun and the proper noun: 'I have two cats.' / 'My cat's name is Toffy.'

  • Q: Identify the common noun and the proper noun: 'There are many fish in this lake.' / 'Lake Saif-ul-Maluk gives a splendid sight.'

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar (Common Gender Nouns): iii. Read the given sentences and notice the use of common gender

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar (Punctuation and Capitalisation): v. Rewrite the given sentences by adding correct punctuation and capitalisation

lessons.title: Writing
lessons.notes_html:
D) Writing — 1. Learning to Write: i. Read the given mind map and write a paragraph about climate change

  • Q: Write a paragraph about climate change using the mind map (pollution, deforestation, rising temperature, loss of fresh water resources).
    Ans: Climate change is a big problem for our Earth. It is caused by pollution from factories, vehicles and power plants. Deforestation, that is cutting down trees, also makes it worse. Because of climate change, the temperature of the Earth is rising day by day. It also causes loss of fresh water resources. We should plant more trees and reduce pollution to save our planet.

D) Writing — 1. Learning to Write: ii. Make a mind map about your favourite season and write a few sentences using this mind map

  • Q: Make a mind map about your favourite season and write a few sentences using it.
    Ans: Model mind map — Favourite Season: Spring: pleasant weather, flowers bloom, green grass, birds sing, new leaves on trees. Sentences: Spring is my favourite season. The weather is pleasant in spring. Flowers bloom everywhere and the grass becomes soft and green. Birds sing sweet songs and the garden presents a beautiful sight.

D) Writing — 2. Creative Writing: Write a paragraph about the 'importance of natural environment' (word bank: Earth, plant, water, air)

  • Q: Write a paragraph about the 'importance of natural environment' using the word bank: Earth, plant, water, air.
    Ans: The natural environment is very important for life on Earth. We get fresh air to breathe from trees and plants. We need clean water for drinking and for growing food. Plants give us food, shade and homes for birds and animals. If we destroy our environment, we cannot live a healthy life. So we must protect our Earth, plant more trees and keep our air and water clean.

mcqs.q: Which four points are shown in the mind map about climate change?
options: Pollution, deforestation, rising temperature and loss of fresh water resources
Pollution, heavy rainfall, snowfall and fresh water
Deforestation, snowfall, cold weather and fresh water
Rising temperature, plastic, smoke and holidays
mcqs.why: The mind map in the book shows pollution, deforestation, rising temperature and loss of fresh water resources around climate change.

mcqs.q: According to the paragraph, climate change is caused by pollution from:
mcqs.why: The paragraph says climate change 'is caused by pollution from factories, vehicles and power plants'.

mcqs.q: In the paragraph, deforestation means:
mcqs.why: The paragraph explains deforestation in its own words: 'Deforestation, that is cutting down trees, also makes it worse.'

mcqs.q: According to the paragraph, the temperature of the Earth is:
mcqs.why: The paragraph says: 'Because of climate change, the temperature of the Earth is rising day by day.'

mcqs.q: Climate change also causes loss of which resource, according to the paragraph?
mcqs.why: The paragraph says climate change 'also causes loss of fresh water resources', one of the four mind-map points.

mcqs.q: What should we do to save our planet, according to the paragraph?
options: Throw more waste on the ground
Plant more trees and reduce pollution
mcqs.why: The paragraph ends: 'We should plant more trees and reduce pollution to save our planet.'

mcqs.q: The mind map about the favourite season in the solved answer is about which season?
mcqs.why: The model mind map is 'Favourite Season: Spring', with pleasant weather, flowers blooming, green grass and birds singing.

mcqs.q: In the spring mind-map sentences, what do the birds do?
mcqs.why: The model sentences say: 'Birds sing sweet songs and the garden presents a beautiful sight' in the spring season.

mcqs.q: According to the paragraph on the importance of natural environment, we get fresh air to breathe from:
mcqs.why: The paragraph says: 'We get fresh air to breathe from trees and plants', and we need clean water for drinking and growing food.

mcqs.q: Which word bank is given for the paragraph on the 'importance of natural environment'?
mcqs.why: The creative writing task gives the word bank Earth, plant, water, air for the paragraph on the importance of natural environment.

chapters.title: Unit 6: A Fit and Healthy Life

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Getting Started — Look at the pictures and guess the action words

  • Q: Look at the pictures and guess the action words.
    Ans: The action words shown in the pictures are: playing (boys are playing football), washing / working in the kitchen (a girl is washing dishes), and eating (a boy is eating food).

Getting Started — Let's Talk

  • Q: Why is a sound sleep important for good health?
    Ans: Model answer: A sound sleep is important for good health because it gives rest to our body and mind. It makes us fresh, strong and active for the next day.
  • Q: What do you eat to keep yourself healthy?
    Ans: Model answer: I eat healthy food like fruits, vegetables, milk, eggs and clean home-cooked food to keep myself healthy. I avoid eating too much junk food.
  • Q: How do you keep yourself fit, healthy and clean?
    Ans: Model answer: I keep myself fit, healthy and clean by washing my hands with soap, taking a bath daily, brushing my teeth, eating healthy food, drinking clean water, playing games and doing exercise.

Reading Text 'A Fit and Healthy Life' — Pre-reading, While-reading and Post-reading

  • Q: Pre-reading: Do you think personal hygiene is important?
    Ans: Yes, personal hygiene is very important. Keeping ourselves clean keeps us safe from germs and diseases and helps us stay fit and healthy.
  • Q: While-reading: Do you think washing hands can keep us safe from germs?
    Ans: Yes, washing hands with soap can keep us safe from germs. Germs from our hands can go into our mouth, nose, eyes and even ears and make us ill, so washing hands for at least 20 seconds removes the germs.
  • Q: Post-reading: How can we keep ourselves safe from Covid-19?
    Ans: We can keep ourselves safe from Covid-19 by washing our hands with soap for at least 20 seconds, wearing a mask, maintaining physical distancing, covering our face while sneezing, and being careful about the food we eat and the water we drink.
  • Q: Post-reading: How do you maintain your personal hygiene?
    Ans: Model answer: I maintain my personal hygiene by washing my hands with soap before eating and after using the toilet, taking a bath daily, brushing my teeth, wearing clean clothes and keeping my surroundings clean.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension: i. Answer these questions

  • Q: Why did the school invite Dr. Haroon?
    Ans: The school invited Dr. Haroon to talk about personal hygiene matters and raise awareness about COVID-19 among the children.
  • Q: What did Dr. Haroon tell the children about keeping personal hygiene?
    Ans: Dr. Haroon told the children to wash their hands with soap for at least 20 seconds before eating and after using the toilet, to cover their face while sneezing, to wear a mask and maintain physical distancing, to be careful about the food they eat and the water they drink, and to avoid eating too much junk food.
  • Q: Why is junk food unhealthy?
    Ans: Junk food is unhealthy because it does not give us the strength and nutrition our body needs. Eating too much junk food can make us weak and ill, while healthy food and clean water keep us strong and fit.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension: ii. Read the given sentences and notice the use of inflectional endings

  • Q: Identify the inflectional ending: 'Lubna and her classmates were very excited about Dr. Haroon's visit.'
    Ans: The inflectional ending is '-ed' in 'excited'. An inflectional ending is a letter or a group of letters added to the end of a word to change its form.
  • Q: Identify the inflectional ending: 'The children were wearing masks.'
    Ans: The inflectional ending is '-ing' in 'wearing'.
  • Q: Identify the inflectional ending: 'Sana always eats healthy food.'
    Ans: The inflectional ending is '-s' in 'eats'.
  • Q: Identify the inflectional ending: 'Sara always washes her hands with soap.'
    Ans: The inflectional ending is '-es' in 'washes'.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension: iii. Make three words with the given inflectional endings

  • Q: Make three words with the inflectional ending '-s'.
    Ans: eats, plays, reads.
  • Q: Make three words with the inflectional ending '-es'.
    Ans: washes, goes, watches.
  • Q: Make three words with the inflectional ending '-ing'.
    Ans: wearing, playing, washing.
  • Q: Make three words with the inflectional ending '-ed'.
    Ans: excited, played, washed.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension: iv. Read the given compound words

  • Q: Make the compound word: sun + light
    Ans: sunlight
  • Q: Make the compound word: head + ache
    Ans: headache
  • Q: Make the compound word: bed + room
    Ans: bedroom
  • Q: Make the compound word: tooth + brush
    Ans: toothbrush
  • Q: Make the compound word: play + ground
    Ans: playground
  • Q: What is a compound word?
    Ans: A compound word is a combination of two or more words that produce a word with a new meaning.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension: v. Match the given words to make compound words

  • Q: Match: butter
    Ans: butter + fly = butterfly
  • Q: Match: straw
    Ans: straw + berry = strawberry
  • Q: Match: extra
    Ans: extra + ordinary = extraordinary
  • Q: Match: rain
    Ans: rain + bow = rainbow

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension: vi. Read the lesson again and fill in the blanks with the correct options

  • Q: The school invited a ______.
    Options: carpenter / judge / lawyer / doctor
    Ans: doctor
  • Q: The students were wearing ______ during the doctor's visit.
    Options: gloves / masks / karate suits / colourful dresses
    Ans: masks
  • Q: We should wash our ______ with soap for twenty seconds.
    Options: feet / head / face / hands
    Ans: hands
  • Q: Never take medicine on an empty ______.
    Options: hand / head / mouth / stomach
    Ans: stomach
  • Q: ______ food keeps us strong and fit.
    Options: Junk / Healthy / Dirty / Unclean
    Ans: Healthy

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 2. Analytical Reading

  • Q: Surf the internet and read about how sports keep us healthy and fit and note down some details in your notebook.
    Ans: Model notes: Sports and games keep us healthy and fit. Playing sports makes our body strong, improves our blood flow and keeps our weight balanced. Sports also keep our mind fresh, teach us teamwork and discipline, and protect us from many diseases.

mcqs.q: Why did the school invite Dr. Haroon?
options: To check the school building and classrooms
To talk about personal hygiene and raise awareness about COVID-19
To teach the children a new sports game
To give the children their exam results
mcqs.why: The solved answer says the school invited Dr. Haroon to talk about personal hygiene matters and raise awareness about COVID-19 among the children.

mcqs.q: For at least how long should we wash our hands with soap to remove germs?
mcqs.why: The lesson says washing hands for at least 20 seconds removes the germs, and Dr. Haroon gave the children the same advice.

mcqs.q: Why is junk food unhealthy?
options: It is always served cold in a packet
It can only be eaten outside the home
It does not give us the strength and nutrition our body needs
It makes our hands dirty when we eat it
mcqs.why: The solved answer explains that junk food does not give the strength and nutrition our body needs, and eating too much can make us weak and ill.

mcqs.q: What is the inflectional ending in the word 'excited'?
mcqs.why: In 'Lubna and her classmates were very excited', the inflectional ending is '-ed' in 'excited', as the solved item shows.

mcqs.q: Which action words are shown in the Getting Started pictures?
mcqs.why: The solved answer lists the picture action words as playing (football), washing (dishes in the kitchen) and eating (food).

mcqs.q: sun + light makes which compound word?
mcqs.why: Joining 'sun' and 'light' gives the compound word 'sunlight', one of the compound words read in this unit.

mcqs.q: Match: butter + ______ = butterfly. Which word completes it?
mcqs.why: The matching exercise joins 'butter' with 'fly' to make the compound word 'butterfly'.

mcqs.q: The school invited a ______. (Book question)
mcqs.why: The book's own fill-in item gives 'doctor': the school invited a doctor, Dr. Haroon, to talk to the children.

mcqs.q: ______ food keeps us strong and fit. (Book question)
mcqs.why: The book's own item gives 'Healthy': healthy food keeps us strong and fit, while junk food makes us weak and ill.

mcqs.q: According to the Analytical Reading notes, what do sports teach us besides keeping us fit?
mcqs.why: The model notes say sports keep the mind fresh and teach us teamwork and discipline, and protect us from many diseases.

lessons.title: Sounds and Speaking
lessons.notes_html:
A) Oral Communication — 1. Learning the Sounds (Consonant Clusters): i. Read the given consonant clusters with their words

  • Q: Read the words with two-consonant clusters in initial position: br- and fl-
    Ans: br-: brush, bread, brain. fl-: flour, flower, fly.
  • Q: Read the words with three-consonant clusters in initial position: spl- and str-
    Ans: spl-: splash, splendid, split. str-: street, straw, stream.
  • Q: Read the words with two-consonant clusters in final position: -lp and -sk
    Ans: -lp: help, pulp, gulp. -sk: flask, ask, desk.
  • Q: Read the words with three-consonant clusters in final position: -fts and -mpt
    Ans: -fts: gifts, crafts, drafts. -mpt: attempt, prompt, contempt.
  • Q: What is a consonant cluster?
    Ans: A consonant cluster is a group of two or more consonants in a word. Each consonant keeps its own sound in the word. A consonant cluster can be in the initial or final position of a word.

A) Oral Communication — 1. Learning the Sounds: ii. Read the given sentences. Underline the words with consonant clusters and write them in their columns

  • Q: 'Brush your teeth before going to bed.' Write the word with a consonant cluster in its column.
    Ans: Brush — consonant cluster in initial position (br-).
  • Q: 'Sara showed me some splendid crafts.' Write the words with consonant clusters in their columns.
    Ans: Splendid — initial position (spl-). Crafts — final position (-fts).
  • Q: 'They attempted to cross the stream.' Write the words with consonant clusters in their columns.
    Ans: Stream — initial position (str-). Attempted (attempt) — final position (-mpt).
  • Q: 'He asked Dr. Haroon a question about germs.' Write the word with a consonant cluster in its column.
    Ans: Asked — consonant cluster in final position (-sk).
  • Q: 'You should help him in watering these flowers.' Write the words with consonant clusters in their columns.
    Ans: Flowers — initial position (fl-). Help — final position (-lp).

A) Oral Communication — 2. Learning to Speak: i. Read and practise the given dialogue

  • Q: Practise the dialogue between Maham and Sidra. Why was Sidra absent and what advice does Maham give her?
    Ans: Sidra was absent because she got fever two days ago. She has recovered now but still feels weakness. Maham advises her to take care of her health, eat a healthy diet and drink plenty of water, and asks if she saw a doctor. Sidra says the doctor gave her some medicines and she will be better soon.

A) Oral Communication — 2. Learning to Speak: ii. Arrange a debate competition about healthy and unhealthy food

  • Q: Give model points for a debate about healthy and unhealthy food.
    Ans: Model points: Healthy food like fruits, vegetables, milk and home-cooked food keeps us strong and fit and protects us from diseases. Unhealthy food like junk food makes us weak and ill, so we should avoid eating too much junk food and always eat healthy food and drink clean water.

mcqs.q: What is a consonant cluster?
options: A group of two or more consonants in a word, where each consonant keeps its own sound
A group of two vowel sounds in one syllable
A word that has no consonants at all
The silent letter at the end of a word
mcqs.why: The solved answer defines a consonant cluster as a group of two or more consonants in a word, and each consonant keeps its own sound.

mcqs.q: Which word begins with the two-consonant cluster 'br-'?
mcqs.why: The cluster list gives br-: brush, bread, brain, so 'brush' begins with the two-consonant cluster br-.

mcqs.q: Which word begins with the three-consonant cluster 'spl-'?
mcqs.why: The list of three-consonant clusters in initial position gives spl-: splash, splendid, split, so 'splendid' begins with spl-.

mcqs.q: In 'Sara showed me some splendid crafts', which word has a consonant cluster in final position?
mcqs.why: The solved answer puts 'crafts' in the final-position column because it ends with the three-consonant cluster -fts.

mcqs.q: In 'They attempted to cross the stream', which word begins with a consonant cluster?
mcqs.why: The solved answer puts 'stream' in the initial-position column because it begins with the three-consonant cluster str-.

mcqs.q: In 'He asked Dr. Haroon a question about germs', the word 'asked' has which final cluster?
mcqs.why: The solved answer shows 'asked' has a consonant cluster in final position, -sk, like flask, ask and desk.

mcqs.q: Why was Sidra absent from school in the dialogue?
options: She went on a trip with her family
She lost her school bag and books
She got fever two days ago
She was playing a football match
mcqs.why: In the dialogue Sidra tells Maham she was absent because she got fever two days ago, and she still feels weakness.

mcqs.q: What advice does Maham give Sidra in the dialogue?
options: Stop drinking water for a few days
Eat only junk food to get energy
Do not go to school for a month
Eat a healthy diet and drink plenty of water
mcqs.why: Maham advises Sidra to take care of her health, eat a healthy diet and drink plenty of water, and asks if she saw a doctor.

mcqs.q: Which pair of words shows the final cluster '-lp'?
mcqs.why: The cluster list gives two-consonant clusters in final position: -lp in help, pulp and gulp.

mcqs.q: In the debate about healthy and unhealthy food, which point supports healthy food?
options: Healthy food makes us weak and ill
Healthy food protects us from diseases
Junk food is better than home food
Clean water is not needed at all
mcqs.why: The model debate points say healthy food like fruits, vegetables, milk and home-cooked food keeps us strong and fit and protects us from diseases.

lessons.title: Language Focus
lessons.notes_html:
C) Language Focus — 1. Vocabulary Building: i. Read the given words with their meanings

  • Q: Match: hygiene
    Ans: to keep yourself and your environment clean
  • Q: Match: prevent
    Ans: to stop something from happening
  • Q: Match: viral
    Ans: caused by a virus
  • Q: Match: germs
    Ans: microbes that cause infection
  • Q: Match: plenty
    Ans: enough

C) Language Focus — 1. Vocabulary Building (Homophones): ii. Read the given homophones and their use

  • Q: Differentiate between the homophones 'right' and 'write' with their use.
    Ans: right: correct — 'You gave the right answer.' write: to put words on paper — 'He had to write a report on healthy food.'
  • Q: Differentiate between the homophones 'meet' and 'meat' with their use.
    Ans: meet: to come together — 'They will meet you soon.' meat: flesh used as food — 'Ali likes to eat red meat.'
  • Q: Differentiate between the homophones 'break' and 'brake' with their use.
    Ans: break: a rest or to separate into pieces — 'I need a break.' brake: the part that stops a vehicle — 'He should put on the brakes to avoid an accident.'
  • Q: Differentiate between the homophones 'ate' and 'eight' with their use.
    Ans: ate: past tense of eat — 'They ate a lot at dinner.' eight: the number 8 — 'Sara is eight years old.'
  • Q: Differentiate between the homophones 'week' and 'weak' with their use.
    Ans: week: seven days — 'There are seven days in a week.' weak: not strong — 'His child is getting weak.'
  • Q: What are homophones?
    Ans: Homophones are words that sound the same, but have different spellings and meanings.

C) Language Focus — 1. Vocabulary Building: iii. Fill in the blanks with the correct homophones

  • Q: Fill in the blanks with the correct homophones (sun, son): I saw ______ rise with my ______.
    Ans: I saw sun rise with my son. (sun, son)
  • Q: Fill in the blanks with the correct homophones (aloud, allowed): Am I ______ to read the given text ______.
    Ans: Am I allowed to read the given text aloud? (allowed, aloud)
  • Q: Fill in the blanks with the correct homophones (four, for): Maryam had bought ______ new dresses ______ her daughter.
    Ans: Maryam had bought four new dresses for her daughter. (four, for)
  • Q: Fill in the blanks with the correct homophones (won, one): ______ of my school teams ______ the cricket match.
    Ans: One of my school teams won the cricket match. (One, won)
  • Q: Fill in the blanks with the correct homophones (add, ad): I want to ______ more information in the newspaper ______.
    Ans: I want to add more information in the newspaper ad. (add, ad)

C) Language Focus — 1. Vocabulary Building: iv. Use the given homophones in your sentences

  • Q: Use the homophones 'fare' and 'fair' in your sentences.
    Ans: fare: The bus fare is twenty rupees. fair: Our teacher is fair with all students.
  • Q: Use the homophones 'wait' and 'weight' in your sentences.
    Ans: wait: Please wait for me at the gate. weight: The weight of this bag is five kilograms.
  • Q: Use the homophones 'sun' and 'son' in your sentences.
    Ans: sun: The sun rises in the east. son: He is the only son of his parents.
  • Q: Use the homophones 'whole' and 'hole' in your sentences.
    Ans: whole: She ate the whole apple. hole: There is a hole in my shoe.
  • Q: Use the homophones 'hear' and 'here' in your sentences.
    Ans: hear: I can hear the birds singing. here: Please come here and sit with me.

C) Language Focus — 2. Learning to Spell: Unscramble the words and learn their spelling

  • Q: Unscramble the word: kunj
    Ans: junk
  • Q: Unscramble the word: ealhth
    Ans: health
  • Q: Unscramble the word: isitv
    Ans: visit
  • Q: Unscramble the word: tafer
    Ans: after
  • Q: Unscramble the word: oaps
    Ans: soap
  • Q: Unscramble the word: hasw
    Ans: wash

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar (Pronoun): i. Read the given sentences and notice the use of pronouns

  • Q: Identify the pronouns: 'We should wash our hands with soap.'
    Ans: We, our.
  • Q: Identify the pronoun: 'They are planting new plants in their garden.'
    Ans: They, their.
  • Q: Identify the pronoun: 'Hira keeps her bedroom neat and clean.'
    Ans: her.
  • Q: Identify the pronoun: 'Always buy a juice in a can. It can be recycled easily.'
    Ans: It.
  • Q: Identify the pronoun: 'Yes, you are right.'
    Ans: you.
  • Q: What are pronouns?
    Ans: Pronouns are words that are used in place of nouns, for example I, you, we, they, us, our, etc.

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar: ii. Read the unit again and circle any five pronouns. Then use them in your own sentences

  • Q: Use the pronoun 'we' (from the unit) in your own sentence.
    Ans: We should wash our hands with soap.
  • Q: Use the pronoun 'you' (from the unit) in your own sentence.
    Ans: You should eat healthy food and drink clean water.
  • Q: Use the pronoun 'your' (from the unit) in your own sentence.
    Ans: Germs from your hands can make you ill.
  • Q: Use the pronoun 'it' (from the unit) in your own sentence.
    Ans: It is very important to look after yourself.
  • Q: Use the pronoun 'our' (from the unit) in your own sentence.
    Ans: We should keep our school clean.

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar (Pronouns as subject, object and possessive): iii. Read the given sentences and notice the use of pronouns as subject, object and possessive

  • Q: List the subject pronouns shown in the book with an example.
    Ans: I, You, He, She, It, We, They. Example: 'They are good students.' A subject pronoun is often the subject of a verb, who and what the sentence is about.
  • Q: List the object pronouns shown in the book with an example.
    Ans: me, you, him, her, it, us, them. Example: 'The teacher taught us nouns.' An object pronoun is often the object of the verb, who or what was acted upon.
  • Q: List the possessive pronouns shown in the book with an example.
    Ans: mine, hers, ours, yours, theirs, his, its. Example: 'This book is mine.' A pronoun that shows possession or ownership is called a possessive pronoun.

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar: iv. Use two subject, object and possessive pronouns each in your sentences

  • Q: Use the subject pronoun 'She' in a sentence.
    Ans: She went to the doctor for a check-up.
  • Q: Use the subject pronoun 'They' in a sentence.
    Ans: They are playing football in the ground.
  • Q: Use the object pronoun 'him' in a sentence.
    Ans: Dr. Haroon talked to him about hygiene.
  • Q: Use the object pronoun 'us' in a sentence.
    Ans: The teacher taught us about germs.
  • Q: Use the possessive pronoun 'mine' in a sentence.
    Ans: This toothbrush is mine.
  • Q: Use the possessive pronoun 'theirs' in a sentence.
    Ans: That house on the corner is theirs.

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar (Subject-Verb Agreement): v. Read the given sentences and notice the use of subject-verb agreement

  • Q: Notice the subject-verb agreement: 'Dr. Haroon is giving instructions to students.'
    Ans: Subject 'Dr. Haroon' is singular, so it takes the singular verb 'is'.
  • Q: Notice the subject-verb agreement: 'The students are washing their hands.'
    Ans: Subject 'students' is plural, so it takes the plural verb 'are'.
  • Q: Notice the subject-verb agreement: 'I don't understand this question.'
    Ans: Subject 'I' takes 'don't'.
  • Q: Notice the subject-verb agreement: 'You are my best friend.'
    Ans: 'You' always agrees with 'are' in both singular and plural cases.
  • Q: Notice the subject-verb agreement: 'I am fond of reading.'
    Ans: Subject 'I' takes the verb 'am'.
  • Q: What is the rule of subject-verb agreement?
    Ans: A singular subject always takes a singular verb and a plural subject always takes a plural verb. The form of a verb changes with the number and person of the subject.

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar: vi. Read the given sentences and tick the verbs that agree with the subjects

  • Q: My mother (likes, like) to eat vegetables.
    Options: likes / like
    Ans: likes
  • Q: Sports (keep, keeps) us healthy.
    Options: keep / keeps
    Ans: keep
  • Q: The bird (are, is) chirping in its nest.
    Options: are / is
    Ans: is
  • Q: They (do, does) not waste their time.
    Options: do / does
    Ans: do
  • Q: Pakistanis (is, are) brave people.
    Options: is / are
    Ans: are

mcqs.q: What does 'hygiene' mean?
options: To keep yourself and your environment clean
mcqs.why: The vocabulary list gives 'hygiene' as keeping yourself and your environment clean; the other options are the meanings of prevent, viral and germs.

mcqs.q: What does 'prevent' mean?
options: To keep yourself clean at all times
A feeling of happiness and joy
mcqs.why: The vocabulary list gives 'prevent' as to stop something from happening, for example preventing germs from making us ill.

mcqs.q: What are 'germs'?
options: Letters added to the end of a word
mcqs.why: The vocabulary list defines germs as microbes that cause infection, which is why washing hands keeps us safe from them.

mcqs.q: What are homophones?
options: Words that are spelled the same but sound different
Two words joined to make one new word
Words used in place of nouns in a sentence
Words that sound the same but have different spellings and meanings
mcqs.why: The solved answer defines homophones as words that sound the same, but have different spellings and meanings, like 'week' and 'weak'.

mcqs.q: Which homophone pair is used correctly in 'There are seven days in a ______'?
mcqs.why: The homophone list explains 'week' means seven days, while its homophone 'weak' means not strong.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blanks with the correct homophones (sun, son): 'I saw ______ rise with my ______.'
mcqs.why: The solved answer fills the sentence as 'I saw sun rise with my son', so the order is sun first and son second.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank with the correct homophone: 'Am I ______ to read the given text aloud?'
mcqs.why: The solved answer uses 'allowed', meaning permitted, in 'Am I allowed to read the given text aloud?', and 'aloud' is its homophone.

mcqs.q: Unscramble the letters 'kunj' to make a word from this unit.
mcqs.why: The spelling exercise unscrambles 'kunj' to make 'junk', as in the junk food discussed in this unit.

mcqs.q: What are pronouns?
options: Words that are used in place of nouns
Words that join two sentences together
Words that describe an action only
Words that name a place or a thing
mcqs.why: The grammar section defines pronouns as words used in place of nouns, for example I, you, we, they, us and our.

mcqs.q: Identify the pronouns in 'We should wash our hands with soap.'
mcqs.why: The solved answer identifies the pronouns in this sentence as 'We' and 'our', which stand in place of nouns.

mcqs.q: Which list gives the subject pronouns shown in the book?
options: me, you, him, her, it, us, them
I, You, He, She, It, We, They
my, your, his, her, its, our
mcqs.why: The book's table lists the subject pronouns as I, You, He, She, It, We and They, with the example 'They are good students.'

mcqs.q: In 'The teacher taught us nouns', what kind of pronoun is 'us'?
mcqs.why: The book uses 'The teacher taught us nouns' as its object pronoun example, because 'us' is who was acted upon by the verb.

mcqs.q: Which pronoun shows possession in 'This book is mine'?
mcqs.why: The book gives 'This book is mine' as the possessive pronoun example, because 'mine' shows possession or ownership.

mcqs.q: What is the rule of subject-verb agreement?
options: Every subject takes the verb 'are' with it
A singular subject takes a singular verb and a plural subject takes a plural verb
The verb never changes with the subject
A plural subject takes a singular verb
mcqs.why: The grammar section states that a singular subject always takes a singular verb and a plural subject always takes a plural verb.

mcqs.q: Choose the verb that agrees with the subject: 'My mother ______ to eat vegetables.'
mcqs.why: The book's own item gives 'likes', because the subject 'My mother' is singular and takes the singular verb 'likes'.

lessons.title: Writing
lessons.notes_html:
D) Writing — 1. Learning to Write: i. Read the given narrative paragraph

  • Q: Read the narrative paragraph about Naveed. What happened in the beginning, middle and ending of the paragraph?
    Ans: Beginning: Naveed was not feeling well last night and his ear was aching, so his mother told him he needed a doctor. Middle: In the morning his mother took him to hospital, the doctor examined his ear with a torch, checked his temperature with a thermometer, found he had fever too, and gave him medicines. Ending: Naveed thanked the doctor, took the medicines at home and got well after a couple of days. A narrative paragraph retells an event and has a beginning, middle and ending.

D) Writing — 1. Learning to Write: ii. Write a narrative paragraph about any memorable incident of your school life

  • Q: Write a narrative paragraph about any memorable incident of your school life.
    Ans: Model paragraph: Last month, Dr. Haroon visited our school to talk about personal hygiene. In the morning, we all wore masks and sat with physical distancing. He told us how germs from our hands can make us ill and taught us to wash our hands with soap for twenty seconds. We asked him many questions and he answered them happily. I will always remember this day because I learnt how to keep myself fit and healthy.

D) Writing — 2. Creative Writing: Write a paragraph on how you spent your time at home during the Corona Virus lockdown

  • Q: Write a paragraph on how you spent your time at home during the Corona Virus lockdown. Mention any new skill you learnt during this lockdown.
    Ans: Model paragraph: During the Corona Virus lockdown, I stayed at home with my family. I studied my school books, helped my mother in the kitchen and played indoor games with my brother. I washed my hands again and again and wore a mask when I went outside. During this lockdown, I learnt a new skill — I learnt how to draw and paint pictures. I also learnt to make a mask at home. It was a difficult time, but I learnt many useful things.

mcqs.q: In the beginning of the narrative paragraph, why did Naveed need a doctor?
options: He was not feeling well and his ear was aching
He had broken his school bag strap
He wanted to ask about his homework
He was going to play a football match
mcqs.why: The solved summary says the paragraph begins with Naveed not feeling well last night, his ear aching, and his mother saying he needed a doctor.

mcqs.q: In the middle of the paragraph, how did the doctor examine Naveed's ear?
mcqs.why: The middle of the paragraph tells that the doctor examined Naveed's ear with a torch and checked his temperature with a thermometer.

mcqs.q: What did the doctor use to check Naveed's temperature?
mcqs.why: The solved summary says the doctor checked Naveed's temperature with a thermometer and found that he had fever too.

mcqs.q: How does the narrative paragraph about Naveed end?
options: Naveed stayed in hospital for a whole month
Naveed went straight back to school the same hour
Naveed stopped taking all of his medicines
Naveed took the medicines at home and got well after a couple of days
mcqs.why: The ending of the paragraph is that Naveed thanked the doctor, took the medicines at home and got well after a couple of days.

mcqs.q: What does a narrative paragraph do?
options: It retells an event and has a beginning, middle and ending
It only lists the meanings of new words
It gives instructions for a science experiment
It is a list of questions without any answers
mcqs.why: The writing section explains that a narrative paragraph retells an event and has a beginning, a middle and an ending.

mcqs.q: In the model paragraph about the school incident, who visited the school?
mcqs.why: The model paragraph begins with Dr. Haroon visiting the school last month to talk about personal hygiene.

mcqs.q: In the model school paragraph, how did the children sit during the visit?
options: Standing in a long line outside
Sitting on the roof of the school
Wearing masks and with physical distancing
Without masks in a crowded hall
mcqs.why: The model paragraph says that in the morning the children all wore masks and sat with physical distancing during Dr. Haroon's visit.

mcqs.q: Which new skill does the writer say he learnt during the Corona Virus lockdown?
options: How to ride a bicycle fast
How to swim in a deep pond
How to fly a big aeroplane
How to draw and paint pictures
mcqs.why: The model lockdown paragraph says the writer learnt a new skill during the lockdown: how to draw and paint pictures.

mcqs.q: What else did the writer learn to make at home during the lockdown?
mcqs.why: The model paragraph also says the writer learnt to make a mask at home during the Corona Virus lockdown.

mcqs.q: During the lockdown, how did the writer spend time with his family at home?
options: He travelled to many cities every week
He studied, helped his mother in the kitchen and played indoor games
He went to school parties every day
He watched the rain from a hill station
mcqs.why: The model paragraph says the writer studied his school books, helped his mother in the kitchen and played indoor games with his brother.

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension: Answer the given questions

  • Q: How do you spend your summer holidays? Mention some activities.
    Ans: Model answer: I spend my summer holidays at home and sometimes visit my grandparents. I read story books, play games with my friends, help my parents at home, learn new things and sometimes go on a trip to a cool place like Murree.
  • Q: Why should we take care of our personal hygiene?
    Ans: We should take care of our personal hygiene because keeping ourselves and our environment clean keeps us safe from germs and diseases. Germs can make us ill, so personal hygiene helps us stay fit and healthy.
  • Q: How can germs make us ill?
    Ans: Germs are microbes that cause infection. Germs from our hands can go into our mouth, nose, eyes and even ears and make us ill. Germs also spread through dirty food, unclean water and viral diseases.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension: Make compound words with the given words

  • Q: Match: sun
    Ans: sun + flower = sunflower
  • Q: Match: wheel
    Ans: wheel + chair = wheelchair
  • Q: Match: tooth
    Ans: tooth + brush = toothbrush
  • Q: Match: cup
    Ans: cup + cake = cupcake
  • Q: Match: star
    Ans: star + fish = starfish

mcqs.q: In the model answer, where does the writer sometimes go during the summer holidays?
options: To a big city office every day
To a hospital for a check-up
mcqs.why: The model answer says the writer spends summer holidays at home and sometimes visits his grandparents during the holidays.

mcqs.q: Which activity is mentioned in the model answer about summer holidays?
options: Flying kites on the school roof
mcqs.why: The model answer lists reading story books, playing games with friends and helping parents at home as holiday activities.

options: It helps us finish our homework faster
It makes our school bags look new
Keeping clean keeps us safe from germs and diseases
It is only needed during the holidays

options: They can change the colour of our clothes
They can make our books wet and torn
They can stop us from playing games

mcqs.why: The solved answer adds that germs also spread through dirty food, unclean water and viral diseases.

mcqs.why: The matching exercise joins 'cup' with 'cake' to make the compound word 'cupcake'.

mcqs.q: star + fish makes which compound word?
mcqs.why: The matching exercise joins 'star' with 'fish' to make the compound word 'starfish'.

mcqs.why: The model answer says the writer sometimes goes on a trip to a cool place like Murree during the summer holidays.

lessons.title: Sounds and Speaking
lessons.notes_html:
A) Oral Communication — 1. Learning the Sounds: Read the given text and circle the words with diphthongs

  • Q: Read the given text and circle the words with diphthongs: 'It was a Monday morning. I reached the sports ground with my family. All my school friends and teachers were there to support me. I was a bit nervous but, somehow, I managed to keep myself together. I looked at the sky and asked Allah for help.'
    Ans: The words with diphthongs are: Monday, I, ground, my, somehow, sky. A diphthong is a sound made by joining two vowel sounds in one syllable, for example 'sky', 'my' and 'somehow'.

A) Oral Communication — 1. Learning the Sounds: Write two words for each given consonant cluster

  • Q: Write two words for the initial consonant cluster 'str-'
    Ans: street, strong (also: straw, stream).
  • Q: Write two words for the initial consonant cluster 'spr-'
    Ans: spring, spray (also: spread).
  • Q: Write two words for the initial consonant cluster 'thr-'
    Ans: three, throw (also: thread).
  • Q: Write two words for the final consonant cluster '-nts'
    Ans: plants, accounts (also: agents, paints).
  • Q: Write two words for the final consonant cluster '-rst'
    Ans: first, worst (also: burst).
  • Q: Write two words for the final consonant cluster '-mpt'
    Ans: attempt, prompt (also: contempt).

A) Oral Communication — Arrange a discussion in class about healthy habits

  • Q: Arrange a discussion in class about healthy habits. Give model points for the discussion.
    Ans: Model points: Healthy habits keep us fit and strong. We should wash our hands with soap, eat healthy food, drink clean water, take a bath daily, brush our teeth, sleep on time and play sports. We should avoid junk food and keep our surroundings clean.

mcqs.q: What is a diphthong?
options: A sound made by joining two vowel sounds in one syllable
A group of three consonants at the end of a word
A letter that is never pronounced in a word
Two words joined to make a compound word
mcqs.why: The solved answer defines a diphthong as a sound made by joining two vowel sounds in one syllable, as in 'sky', 'my' and 'somehow'.

mcqs.q: Which word from the given text contains a diphthong?
mcqs.why: The solved answer circles 'sky' among the diphthong words in the text, along with Monday, I, ground, my and somehow.

mcqs.q: Which word from the given text contains a diphthong?
mcqs.why: The solved answer lists 'somehow' as one of the words with a diphthong in the Monday morning text about the sports ground.

mcqs.q: Write two words for the initial consonant cluster 'str-'. Which pair is correct?
mcqs.why: The solved answer gives street and strong for the initial cluster str-, with straw and stream as further examples.

mcqs.q: Write two words for the initial consonant cluster 'spr-'. Which pair is correct?
mcqs.why: The solved answer gives spring and spray for the initial cluster spr-, with spread as a further example.

mcqs.q: Write two words for the initial consonant cluster 'thr-'. Which pair is correct?

mcqs.q: Write two words for the final consonant cluster '-nts'. Which pair is correct?
mcqs.why: The solved answer gives plants and accounts for the final cluster -nts, with agents and paints as further examples.

mcqs.q: Write two words for the final consonant cluster '-rst'. Which pair is correct?
mcqs.why: The solved answer gives first and worst for the final cluster -rst, with burst as a further example.

mcqs.q: Write two words for the final consonant cluster '-mpt'. Which pair is correct?
mcqs.why: The solved answer gives attempt and prompt for the final cluster -mpt, with contempt as a further example.

mcqs.q: Which healthy habit is named in the class discussion points?
options: Sleep on time and play sports
mcqs.why: The model discussion points say we should sleep on time and play sports, wash hands with soap, eat healthy food and drink clean water.

lessons.title: Language Focus
lessons.notes_html:
C) Language Focus — 1. Vocabulary Building: Read the given words and write their meanings

  • Q: Write the meaning of 'pandemic'.
    Ans: A disease that spreads over a whole country or the whole world.
  • Q: Write the meaning of 'cheer'.
    Ans: Delight; a feeling of happiness and joy.
  • Q: Write the meaning of 'prevent'.
    Ans: To stop something from happening.
  • Q: Write the meaning of 'hygiene'.
    Ans: To keep yourself and your environment clean.
  • Q: Write the meaning of 'precautionary'.
    Ans: Done to stop something bad from happening; taken as a precaution to stay safe.

C) Language Focus — 1. Vocabulary Building: Write two nouns in each of the given columns of gender nouns

  • Q: Write two masculine gender nouns.
    Ans: king, father (also: man, brother).
  • Q: Write two feminine gender nouns.
    Ans: queen, mother (also: woman, sister).
  • Q: Write two neuter gender nouns.
    Ans: table, book (also: chair, pen). Things that are neither male nor female are neuter gender.
  • Q: Write two common gender nouns.
    Ans: teacher, doctor (also: student, friend). Common gender nouns can be male or female.

C) Language Focus — Read the given text. Circle the common nouns and underline the proper nouns

  • Q: 'Abid and his family went to Murree during the last summer holidays.' Circle the common nouns and underline the proper nouns.
    Ans: Common nouns: family, holidays. Proper nouns: Abid, Murree.
  • Q: 'They stayed at Uncle Salim's house.' Circle the common nouns and underline the proper nouns.
    Ans: Common noun: house. Proper noun: Salim (Uncle Salim).
  • Q: 'They visited many beautiful places in Murree.' Circle the common nouns and underline the proper nouns.
    Ans: Common noun: places. Proper noun: Murree.
  • Q: 'They went to Nathia Gali, Patriata, Pindi Point and Kashmir Point.' Circle the common nouns and underline the proper nouns.
    Ans: Common noun: none in this sentence except the names of places. Proper nouns: Nathia Gali, Patriata, Pindi Point, Kashmir Point.
  • Q: 'They also bought Kashmiri shawls and embroidered bags from the Mall Road.' Circle the common nouns and underline the proper nouns.
    Ans: Common nouns: shawls, bags. Proper nouns: Kashmiri, Mall Road.
  • Q: 'They enjoyed their trip a lot.' Circle the common nouns and underline the proper nouns.
    Ans: Common noun: trip. Proper noun: none.

C) Language Focus — Rewrite the given paragraph using the correct subject-verb agreement

  • Q: Rewrite the paragraph using the correct subject-verb agreement: 'Next month we is going to the Clifton beach. My sister like this idea because she like the natural beauty of seas. My brother and I wants to go fishing. My father say he are going to take us fishing this time. I hopes the weather is good so we can go out in the sea. My mother will cooks the fish.'
    Ans: Next month we are going to the Clifton beach. My sister likes this idea because she likes the natural beauty of seas. My brother and I want to go fishing. My father says he is going to take us fishing this time. I hope the weather is good so we can go out in the sea. My mother will cook the fish.

C) Language Focus — Rewrite the given paragraph by using correct punctuation and capitalisation

  • Q: Rewrite the paragraph by using correct punctuation and capitalisation: 'dr haroon told them that germs from our hands can go into our mouth, nose, eyes and even ears and make us ill we should also be careful about our food junk food is not good for us so we should eat healthy food'
    Ans: Dr Haroon told them that germs from our hands can go into our mouth, nose, eyes and even ears and make us ill. We should also be careful about our food. Junk food is not good for us, so we should eat healthy food.

mcqs.q: What does 'pandemic' mean?
options: A disease that spreads over a whole country or the whole world
A feeling of happiness and joy
Something done to stop a bad thing happening
Keeping yourself and your environment clean
mcqs.why: The vocabulary exercise gives 'pandemic' as a disease that spreads over a whole country or the whole world.

mcqs.q: What does 'cheer' mean?
options: A disease that spreads over the whole world
Delight; a feeling of happiness and joy
A thing that is neither male nor female
mcqs.why: The vocabulary exercise gives 'cheer' as delight, a feeling of happiness and joy.

mcqs.q: What does 'precautionary' mean?
options: A disease that spreads over a whole country
Delight and a feeling of happiness
Done to stop something bad from happening; taken as a precaution to stay safe
A noun that can be male or female
mcqs.why: The vocabulary exercise explains 'precautionary' as done to stop something bad from happening, taken as a precaution to stay safe.

mcqs.q: Which pair gives two masculine gender nouns?
mcqs.why: The gender nouns exercise lists king and father as masculine gender nouns, with man and brother as further examples.

mcqs.q: Which pair gives two feminine gender nouns?
mcqs.why: The gender nouns exercise lists queen and mother as feminine gender nouns, with woman and sister as further examples.

mcqs.q: Things that are neither male nor female belong to which gender?
mcqs.why: The solved answer explains that things that are neither male nor female, like table and book, are neuter gender.

mcqs.q: Which pair gives two common gender nouns?
mcqs.why: The exercise lists teacher and doctor as common gender nouns, because common gender nouns can be male or female.

mcqs.q: In 'Abid and his family went to Murree', which words are proper nouns?
mcqs.why: The solved answer underlines Abid and Murree as the proper nouns, while family and holidays are the common nouns in that sentence.

mcqs.q: In 'They also bought Kashmiri shawls and embroidered bags from the Mall Road', which words are common nouns?
mcqs.why: The solved answer circles shawls and bags as the common nouns, while Kashmiri and Mall Road are the proper nouns.

mcqs.q: Which places are proper nouns in 'They went to Nathia Gali, Patriata, Pindi Point and Kashmir Point'?
options: Nathia Gali, Patriata, Pindi Point and Kashmir Point
mcqs.why: The solved answer lists Nathia Gali, Patriata, Pindi Point and Kashmir Point as the proper nouns, the names of the places visited.

mcqs.q: Choose the corrected sentence with the right subject-verb agreement.
options: My sister like this idea because she like the natural beauty of seas.
My sister liking this idea because she like the natural beauty of seas.
My sister likes this idea because she likes the natural beauty of seas.
My sister are liking this idea because she are liking the seas.
mcqs.why: The corrected paragraph uses 'likes' with the singular subject 'sister' and with 'she': 'My sister likes this idea because she likes...'

mcqs.q: Choose the corrected sentence with the right subject-verb agreement.
options: My father say he are going to take us fishing this time.
My father says he are going to take us fishing this time.
My father say he is going to take us fishing this times.
My father says he is going to take us fishing this time.
mcqs.why: The corrected paragraph reads 'My father says he is going to take us fishing this time', with 'says' and 'is' agreeing with their subjects.

mcqs.q: How does the corrected paragraph about Dr Haroon begin?
options: Dr Haroon told them that germs from our hands can go into our mouth, nose, eyes and even ears and make us ill.
Dr Haroon told them that germs from our hands can go into our mouth nose eyes and even ears and make us ill
dr haroon told them, that germs from our hands can go into our mouth, nose, eyes and even ears and make us ill.
Dr Haroon told them that germs from our hands can go into our mouth, nose, eyes and even ears and make us ill!
mcqs.why: The rewritten paragraph capitalises the name as 'Dr Haroon' at the start of the sentence, with correct punctuation and capitalisation.

mcqs.q: What punctuation ends the corrected sentence 'We should also be careful about our food'?
mcqs.why: In the rewritten paragraph this statement ends with a full stop before the next sentence about junk food begins.

mcqs.q: In the corrected paragraph, why should we eat healthy food?
options: Because healthy food is hard to find
Because germs cannot touch any food
Because junk food is not good for us
mcqs.why: The corrected paragraph ends: 'Junk food is not good for us, so we should eat healthy food', giving the reason for eating healthy food.

lessons.title: Writing
lessons.notes_html:
