chapters.title: Unit 7: What Goes Around, Comes Around

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Getting Started — Let's Talk

  • Q: What are the friends doing in the pictures?
    Ans: In one picture two friends are studying and reading a book together at a table. In the other picture a boy is helping his friend who has fallen off his bicycle to get up.
  • Q: Can you share other things that friends do for one another?
    Ans: Friends help each other in studies, share their lunch and books, play together, visit each other when one is ill, and stand by each other in difficult times.
  • Q: How can you be a good friend to someone?
    Ans: I can be a good friend by being honest and kind, helping my friend in need, listening to him, sharing with him, and never making fun of him or leaving him alone in trouble.
  • Q: Are you a good friend? Analyse yourself.
    Ans: Yes, I try to be a good friend. I help my friends with their lessons, share my things with them and help them when they are in trouble. I still need to improve by always speaking the truth and never hurting anyone's feelings.

Pre-reading

  • Q: Look at the given pictures and guess what is happening.
    Ans: In the pictures a frog is talking to a mouse near a pond. The frog seems to be inviting the mouse to go with him, and in another picture the frog and the mouse are tied together near the water.
  • Q: Share good qualities of your best friend.
    Ans: My best friend is honest, kind and helpful. He always speaks the truth, helps me in my studies, shares his lunch with me and never leaves me alone when I am in trouble.

While-reading — Tell meanings of 'underwater' and 'pounced'

  • Q: What is the meaning of 'underwater'?
    Ans: Underwater means below the surface of the water.
  • Q: What is the meaning of 'pounced'?
    Ans: Pounced means sprang forward suddenly so as to catch something.

Post-reading

  • Q: Can you think of a different moral for the fable?
    Ans: A different moral for the fable can be: 'What goes around, comes around,' or 'Never harm others, because the same harm can come back to you.'
  • Q: Read the story again and think of another ending for this story and discuss.
    Ans: Another ending: When the mouse begged to be taken out of the water, the frog felt sorry, untied the thread and helped the mouse back to the bank. The mouse thanked him, and the frog learnt that a true friend never puts his friend in danger for his own fun.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension (i) Answer these questions

  • Q: Why does the frog tie his foot to the mouse's foot?
    Ans: The frog ties the mouse's foot to his own foot with a piece of thread so that he can pull the mouse along in the water, because the mouse cannot swim.
  • Q: What happened at the end of the story?
    Ans: At the end, the poor mouse drowned in the pond. A hawk pounced on the mouse and flew away with it, dragging the frog out of the water too because he was still tied to the mouse. The hawk ate both the selfish frog and the poor mouse for his supper.
  • Q: Write a summary of the fable you have just read.
    Ans: A mouse who lived on land became friends with a frog who lived in water. The mouse showed the frog his little hole, and the frog invited the mouse to see the underwater world. As the mouse could not swim, the frog tied the mouse's foot to his own with a piece of thread. In the pond the frog swam happily while the poor mouse was frightened and soon drowned. A hawk pounced on the dead mouse and flew away with it, dragging the frog out of the water too, because he was still tied to the mouse. The hawk ate both of them. Moral: As you sow, so shall you reap.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension (ii) Elements of a fable

  • Q: What is 'Character' in a story?
    Ans: Characters are the people and animals in a story. In this fable the characters are the mouse, the frog and the hawk.
  • Q: What is 'Setting' in a story?
    Ans: Setting is where and when the action in the story takes place. In this fable the setting is the mouse's little hole on land, the meadow and the frog's pond.
  • Q: What is 'Plot' in a story?
    Ans: Plot is the theme of the story around which events are planned. It is the beginning, middle and end of the story.
  • Q: What is 'Conflict' in a fable?
    Ans: Every fable has a problem that makes the characters work and resolve it. In this fable the conflict is that the mouse cannot swim, yet the cruel frog pulls him into the water and does not take him out.
  • Q: What is 'Resolution' in a fable?
    Ans: Resolution is the solution to the conflict. It has a moral. In this fable the frog gets the result of his own cruelty when the hawk eats him along with the mouse, and the moral is: As you sow, so shall you reap.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension (iii) Which is your favourite character of the story? Discuss why

  • Q: Which is your favourite character of the story? Why?
    Ans: My favourite character is the mouse. He is friendly and trusting. He showed the frog his home and all the beautiful things in it, and he went with the frog because he trusted his friend. I feel sorry for him because the unkind frog did not care for him.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension (iv) Read the given story and fill in the blanks with the correct words given below

  • Q: Once there lived a hare and a tortoise in a forest. The ______ was very proud of his speed.
    Ans: hare
  • Q: He used to make fun of the ______ for being too slow.
    Ans: tortoise
  • Q: One day, the hare ______ the tortoise to a race.
    Ans: challenged
  • Q: The race started. The hare ran very ______.
    Ans: fast
  • Q: The tortoise was ______ much behind.
    Ans: left
  • Q: The hare got tired and stopped to have some rest under ______ tree.
    Ans: a
  • Q: ______ tortoise passed him and reached the winning post.
    Ans: The
  • Q: The hare ______ up and ran as fast as he could.
    Ans: woke
  • Q: He saw that the tortoise was already there at ______ winning post.
    Ans: the
  • Q: The tortoise had ______ the race.
    Ans: won
  • Q: Give the complete filled story in order.
    Ans: Once there lived a hare and a tortoise in a forest. The hare was very proud of his speed. He used to make fun of the tortoise for being too slow. One day, the hare challenged the tortoise to a race. The tortoise accepted the challenge. The race started. The hare ran very fast. The tortoise was left much behind. The hare got tired and stopped to have some rest under a tree. He fell asleep. The tortoise passed him and reached the winning post. The hare woke up and ran as fast as he could. He saw that the tortoise was already there at the winning post. The tortoise had won the race.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension (v) Read the story again and write its summary in your own words

  • Q: Write the summary of 'What Goes Around, Comes Around' in your own words.
    Ans: A mouse who lived on land became friends with a frog who lived in water. The mouse showed the frog his little hole, and the frog invited the mouse to see the underwater world. As the mouse could not swim, the frog tied the mouse's foot to his own with a piece of thread. In the pond the frog swam happily while the poor mouse was frightened and soon drowned. A hawk pounced on the dead mouse and flew away with it, dragging the frog out of the water too, because he was still tied to the mouse. The hawk ate both of them. Moral: As you sow, so shall you reap.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension (vi) Read the lesson again and fill in the blanks with the correct options

  • Q: The frog lived in ______ for most of his life.
    Options: a stable / a nest / soil / water
    Ans: water
  • Q: The frog tied the mouse's foot to his own with a piece of ______.
    Options: cloth / thread / rope / string
    Ans: thread
  • Q: The poor ______ drowned and his body floated on the surface of the water.
    Options: hawk / hen / mouse / crow
    Ans: mouse
  • Q: As you sow, so shall you ______.
    Options: cook / reap / eat / enjoy
    Ans: reap
  • Q: The hawk had a good ______.
    Options: lunch / dinner / supper / breakfast
    Ans: supper

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 2. Analytical Reading: Read a fable. Write its elements and moral in your notebook

  • Q: Write the elements and moral of the fable 'What Goes Around, Comes Around'.
    Ans: Characters: the mouse, the frog and the hawk. Setting: the mouse's hole on land, the meadow and the pond. Plot: a land mouse befriends a water frog; the frog ties their feet together, pulls the mouse into the pond and lets him drown; a hawk carries off the mouse and the tied frog and eats both. Conflict: the mouse cannot swim and the cruel frog refuses to take him out of the water. Resolution: the frog suffers the result of his own bad deed. Moral: As you sow, so shall you reap.

mcqs.q: Why does the frog tie his foot to the mouse's foot?
options: So that the mouse can teach him to run fast
So that he can pull the mouse along in the water, because the mouse cannot swim
So that they can climb a tree together
So that the hawk cannot see them at all
mcqs.why: The solved answer says the frog tied the mouse's foot to his own with a piece of thread so he could pull the mouse along in the water.

mcqs.q: What happened at the end of the story?
options: A hawk pounced on the drowned mouse and flew away with it, dragging the tied frog out too, and ate both
The frog untied the mouse and they went home together
The mouse learnt to swim and thanked the frog
The hawk helped the mouse back to the bank
mcqs.why: The solved answer tells that the mouse drowned, a hawk pounced on it and flew away dragging the tied frog, and ate both for his supper.

mcqs.q: What does 'underwater' mean?
options: Above the clouds in the sky
Inside a hole in the ground
Below the surface of the water
On the top of a tall tree
mcqs.why: The while-reading item gives 'underwater' as below the surface of the water, the world the frog invited the mouse to see.

mcqs.q: What does 'pounced' mean?
options: Sprang forward suddenly so as to catch something
mcqs.why: The while-reading item gives 'pounced' as sprang forward suddenly so as to catch something, which is what the hawk did.

mcqs.q: Who are the characters in the fable?
options: The mouse, the frog and the hawk
The hare, the tortoise and the lion
The sparrow, the cat and the deer
The hen, the crow and the fox
mcqs.why: The elements section says the characters are the people and animals in a story, and in this fable they are the mouse, the frog and the hawk.

mcqs.q: What is the setting of the fable?
options: A school classroom and its playground
The mouse's little hole on land, the meadow and the frog's pond
A big city market and a railway station
A snow-covered mountain and a deep cave
mcqs.why: The elements section gives the setting as where and when the action takes place: the mouse's hole on land, the meadow and the frog's pond.

mcqs.q: What is the conflict in the fable?
options: The hare challenges the tortoise to a race in the forest
The hawk cannot find any food for his supper
The mouse cannot swim, yet the cruel frog pulls him into the water and does not take him out
The frog loses his way back to the pond
mcqs.why: The elements section states the conflict: the mouse cannot swim, yet the cruel frog pulls him into the water and does not take him out.

mcqs.q: What is the moral of the fable?
options: Slow and steady wins the race
A friend in need is a friend indeed
As you sow, so shall you reap
mcqs.why: The resolution of the fable carries the moral 'As you sow, so shall you reap', the same idea as the title 'What Goes Around, Comes Around'.

mcqs.q: In the hare and tortoise story, why was the hare proud?
options: He was very proud of his speed
He was proud of his beautiful house
He was proud of winning every race
He was proud of his loud voice
mcqs.why: The fill-in story begins that the hare was very proud of his speed and used to make fun of the tortoise for being too slow.

mcqs.q: Who won the race in the hare and tortoise story?
mcqs.why: The completed story says the tortoise passed the sleeping hare, reached the winning post and had won the race.

lessons.title: Sounds and Speaking
lessons.notes_html:
A) Oral Communication — 1. Learning the Sounds: Vowels and Consonants (i) Read the given sentences and notice the use of words starting with consonant and vowel sounds

  • Q: In 'The frog splashed around and swam, croaking about as if he had done a good feat,' which words start with a vowel sound and which with a consonant sound?
    Ans: Vowel sounds: around, and, about, as, if. Consonant sounds: The, frog, splashed, swam, croaking, he, had, done, good, feat.
  • Q: In 'The frog intended to get into mischief,' which words start with a vowel sound and which with a consonant sound?
    Ans: Vowel sounds: intended, into. Consonant sounds: The, frog, to, get, mischief.
  • Q: In 'Maryam likes to eat eggs and bread for breakfast,' which words start with a vowel sound and which with a consonant sound?
    Ans: Vowel sounds: eat, eggs, and. Consonant sounds: Maryam, likes, to, bread, for, breakfast.
  • Q: In 'Only eight apples were left in this basket,' which words start with a vowel sound and which with a consonant sound?
    Ans: Vowel sounds: Only, eight, apples, in. Consonant sounds: were, left, this, basket.
  • Q: In 'Naeema is a bright student of our university,' which words start with a vowel sound and which with a consonant sound?
    Ans: Vowel sounds: is, a, of, our. Consonant sounds: Naeema, bright, student, university (university begins with a consonant 'y' sound).

A) Oral Communication — 1. Learning the Sounds (ii) Write five words starting with consonant and vowel sounds each

  • Q: Write five words starting with a consonant sound.
    Ans: Frog, mouse, water, thread, pond.
  • Q: Write five words starting with a vowel sound.
    Ans: Apple, egg, underwater, only, eight.

A) Oral Communication — 2. Learning to Speak (i) Read and practise the given dialogue

  • Q: Read and practise the given dialogue between Hen, Mouse and Crow. What does the dialogue show?
    Ans: Hen greets Mouse and asks where he is going in a hurry. Mouse says he is going with a frog to see the underwater world. Crow joins them and warns Mouse that it can be dangerous because the frog is naughty, so he should be aware of him. Mouse thanks Crow for the advice and says he will take care of himself, and they say goodbye to each other. The dialogue shows that good friends warn us about danger.

A) Oral Communication — 2. Learning to Speak (ii) Discuss your favourite stories

  • Q: Discuss your favourite story. (Model response)
    Ans: My favourite story is 'The Hare and the Tortoise.' I like it because it teaches us that slow and steady wins the race. The proud hare slept during the race, but the tortoise kept walking and won. We should never be proud and should keep working hard.

mcqs.q: In 'The frog splashed around and swam', which word starts with a vowel sound?
mcqs.why: The solved answer lists the vowel-sound words in this sentence as around, and, about, as and if, while frog and splashed start with consonant sounds.

mcqs.q: In 'The frog intended to get into mischief', which words start with vowel sounds?
mcqs.why: The solved answer lists 'intended' and 'into' as the vowel-sound words, and The, frog, to, get and mischief as consonant-sound words.

mcqs.q: In 'Maryam likes to eat eggs and bread for breakfast', which word starts with a vowel sound?
mcqs.why: The solved answer lists eat, eggs and and as the vowel-sound words in this sentence, while Maryam, likes and bread start with consonant sounds.

mcqs.q: In 'Only eight apples were left in this basket', which word starts with a consonant sound?
mcqs.why: The solved answer lists Only, eight, apples and in as vowel-sound words, and were, left, this and basket as consonant-sound words.

mcqs.q: In 'Naeema is a bright student of our university', the word 'university' begins with which sound?
mcqs.why: The solved answer notes that 'university' begins with a consonant 'y' sound, so it is counted with the consonant-sound words in that sentence.

mcqs.q: Which list gives five words starting with a consonant sound?
mcqs.why: The solved answer gives frog, mouse, water, thread and pond as five words starting with a consonant sound.

mcqs.q: Which list gives five words starting with a vowel sound?
mcqs.why: The solved answer gives apple, egg, underwater, only and eight as five words starting with a vowel sound.

mcqs.q: In the dialogue, where does Mouse say he is going with the frog?
options: To buy food from the market
To visit the hare in the forest
To build a nest in a tree
mcqs.why: In the dialogue Mouse tells Hen he is going with a frog to see the underwater world, and he is in a hurry.

mcqs.q: What warning does Crow give Mouse in the dialogue?
options: The pond water is too cold for swimming
The hawk is waiting near his hole today
It can be dangerous because the frog is naughty, so he should be aware of him
He should carry food for the long journey
mcqs.why: Crow joins the dialogue and warns Mouse that it can be dangerous because the frog is naughty, so he should be aware of him.

mcqs.q: What lesson does the writer's favourite story 'The Hare and the Tortoise' teach?
options: As you sow, so shall you reap
Always run as fast as you can
Slow and steady wins the race
mcqs.why: The model discussion says the writer likes 'The Hare and the Tortoise' because it teaches that slow and steady wins the race.

lessons.title: Language Focus
lessons.notes_html:
C) Language Focus — 1. Vocabulary Building (i) Read the given words with their meanings

  • Q: Match: croaking
    Ans: a sound made by a frog
  • Q: Match: intent
    Ans: the purpose to do something
  • Q: Match: drag
    Ans: to pull somebody
  • Q: Match: frightened
    Ans: afraid
  • Q: Match: pounced
    Ans: sprang forward suddenly so as to catch something

C) Language Focus — 1. Vocabulary Building: Compound Words (ii) Read the given compound words

  • Q: Match: birth + day
    Ans: birthday
  • Q: Match: after + noon
    Ans: afternoon
  • Q: Match: back + bone
    Ans: backbone
  • Q: Match: chair + man
    Ans: chairman
  • Q: Match: air + port
    Ans: airport
  • Q: Match: milk + shake
    Ans: milkshake

C) Language Focus — 1. Vocabulary Building (iii) Make compound words by combining the words from the word bank. Also use any three of them in your sentences

  • Q: Match: table + spoon
    Ans: tablespoon
  • Q: Match: bed + room
    Ans: bedroom
  • Q: Match: sun + shine
    Ans: sunshine
  • Q: Match: air + port
    Ans: airport
  • Q: Match: tooth + brush
    Ans: toothbrush
  • Q: Match: moon + light
    Ans: moonlight
  • Q: Match: fire + fly
    Ans: firefly
  • Q: Use 'bedroom' in a sentence.
    Ans: My bedroom is neat and clean.
  • Q: Use 'sunshine' in a sentence.
    Ans: The children are playing in the bright sunshine.
  • Q: Use 'toothbrush' in a sentence.
    Ans: I clean my teeth with a toothbrush every morning.

C) Language Focus — 1. Vocabulary Building: Homonyms (iv) Read the given homonyms and their use

  • Q: Explain the two meanings of 'sink' with the given sentences.
    Ans: 'Sink' as a noun means the basin in a kitchen: 'There are some plates in the kitchen sink.' 'Sink' as a verb means to go down below the surface: 'The ship sinks to the bottom of the sea.'
  • Q: Explain the two meanings of 'tie' with the given sentences.
    Ans: 'Tie' as a verb means to fasten with a knot: 'Please tie a knot in this rope.' 'Tie' as a noun means the long narrow piece of cloth worn with a shirt: 'He likes to wear a tie and shirt.'
  • Q: Explain the two meanings of 'park' with the given sentences.
    Ans: 'Park' as a verb means to leave a vehicle somewhere: 'They usually park their cars outside their house.' 'Park' as a noun means a public garden for walking and playing: 'The children are playing in the park.'
  • Q: Explain the two meanings of 'bank' with the given sentences.
    Ans: 'Bank' in 'riverbank' means the land along the side of a river: 'Ali bought a house near the riverbank.' 'Bank' also means a place where money is kept: 'Sara opened an account in a bank.'
  • Q: Explain the two meanings of 'match' with the given sentences.
    Ans: 'Match' in 'matchsticks' means a small stick used to light a fire: 'Could you please, light a matchstick?' 'Match' also means a game or contest: 'They won the cricket match.'

C) Language Focus — 1. Vocabulary Building (v) Read the given sentences and circle the correct words from the given homonyms

  • Q: The apples are beginning to drop from the trees. Here 'drop' means:
    Options: drop (fall) / drop (a small quantity of a liquid)
    Ans: drop (fall)
  • Q: He held the bird gently in his palm. Here 'palm' means:
    Options: palm (a straight tree with long leaves at the top) / palm (the inner surface of the hand between the wrist and the fingers)
    Ans: palm (the inner surface of the hand between the wrist and the fingers)
  • Q: The key was hanging from a nail by the door. Here 'nail' means:
    Options: nail (the thin hard layer covering the outer tip of the fingers or toes) / nail (a small pointed piece of metal with a flat head)
    Ans: nail (a small pointed piece of metal with a flat head)

C) Language Focus — 1. Vocabulary Building (vi) Use the given homonyms in your own sentences

  • Q: Use 'right' (correct) in a sentence.
    Ans: Your answer to this question is right.
  • Q: Use 'right' (the side opposite to left) in a sentence.
    Ans: The school is on the right side of the road.
  • Q: Use 'fair' (just and honest) in a sentence.
    Ans: Our teacher is always fair with all the students.
  • Q: Use 'fair' (a funfair / exhibition) in a sentence.
    Ans: We enjoyed the rides at the village fair.
  • Q: Use 'glasses' (spectacles) in a sentence.
    Ans: My grandfather wears glasses for reading.
  • Q: Use 'glasses' (drinking glasses) in a sentence.
    Ans: She filled two glasses with cold water.
  • Q: Use 'well' (in good health / properly) in a sentence.
    Ans: He is not feeling well today.
  • Q: Use 'well' (a deep hole for water) in a sentence.
    Ans: The villagers take water from the well.

C) Language Focus — 2. Learning to Spell: Fill in the missing letters to complete the words

  • Q: Complete the word: wonde______ful
    Ans: wonderful
  • Q: Complete the word: th______ead
    Ans: thread
  • Q: Complete the word: s______rfa______e
    Ans: surface
  • Q: Complete the word: d______owned
    Ans: drowned
  • Q: Complete the word: su______p______r
    Ans: supper

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar: Personal Pronouns (Reflexive Pronoun) (i) Read the given sentences and notice the use of personal pronouns

  • Q: Identify the reflexive pronoun: 'The frog hurt itself while playing.'
    Ans: itself
  • Q: Identify the reflexive pronoun: 'Ali introduced himself to his new neighbour.'
    Ans: himself
  • Q: Identify the reflexive pronoun: 'God helps those who help themselves.'
    Ans: themselves
  • Q: Identify the reflexive pronoun: 'Sana bought a dress for herself.'
    Ans: herself
  • Q: Identify the reflexive pronoun: 'You should complete your assignment yourself.'
    Ans: yourself
  • Q: Identify the reflexive pronoun: 'We are enjoying ourselves.'
    Ans: ourselves
  • Q: Identify the reflexive pronoun: 'I prepare lunch myself.'
    Ans: myself

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar (ii) Use the personal pronouns in your own sentences

  • Q: Use 'myself' in a sentence.
    Ans: I did my homework myself.
  • Q: Use 'yourself' in a sentence.
    Ans: Please help yourself to the biscuits.
  • Q: Use 'himself' in a sentence.
    Ans: He cut himself while playing.
  • Q: Use 'herself' in a sentence.
    Ans: She made a cup of tea for herself.
  • Q: Use 'itself' in a sentence.
    Ans: The cat cleaned itself in the sun.
  • Q: Use 'ourselves' in a sentence.
    Ans: We enjoyed ourselves at the picnic.
  • Q: Use 'themselves' in a sentence.
    Ans: The children dressed themselves for school.

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar: Interrogative Sentence of 'Be' and 'Do' (iii) Read the given interrogative sentences and notice the use of different forms of 'be' and 'do'

  • Q: Which form of 'be' or 'do' is used in 'Is the hawk eating a frog?'
    Ans: 'Is' — present form of 'be', used at the beginning to make the question.
  • Q: Which form of 'be' or 'do' is used in 'Are the boys playing?'
    Ans: 'Are' — present form of 'be'.
  • Q: Which form of 'be' or 'do' is used in 'Am I reading a storybook?'
    Ans: 'Am' — present form of 'be'.
  • Q: Which form of 'be' or 'do' is used in 'Was Anum cooking pasta?'
    Ans: 'Was' — past form of 'be'.
  • Q: Which form of 'be' or 'do' is used in 'Were a frog and a mouse swimming in the pond?'
    Ans: 'Were' — past form of 'be'.
  • Q: Which form of 'be' or 'do' is used in 'Does Ali ride a bicycle?'
    Ans: 'Does' — present form of 'do'.
  • Q: Which form of 'be' or 'do' is used in 'Do we get up early?'
    Ans: 'Do' — present form of 'do'.
  • Q: Which form of 'be' or 'do' is used in 'Did they learn a lesson?'
    Ans: 'Did' — past form of 'do'.

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar (iv) Write interrogative sentences of the forms of 'be' and 'do'

  • Q: Write interrogative sentences using forms of 'be'. (Model)
    Ans: Is the frog swimming in the pond? Are the students reading the story? Am I late for school? Was the mouse frightened? Were the boys playing in the meadow?
  • Q: Write interrogative sentences using forms of 'do'. (Model)
    Ans: Do you like this fable? Does the frog live in water? Did the hawk eat the frog?

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar (v) Rewrite the given sentences by adding correct punctuation

  • Q: Rewrite with correct punctuation: 'sara is twenty two years old'
    Ans: Sara is twenty-two years old.
  • Q: Rewrite with correct punctuation: 'oh what a beautiful scene it is'
    Ans: Oh! What a beautiful scene it is!
  • Q: Rewrite with correct punctuation: 'the frog deceived the poor mouse'
    Ans: The frog deceived the poor mouse.
  • Q: Rewrite with correct punctuation: 'do you know the moral of this story'
    Ans: Do you know the moral of this story?
  • Q: Rewrite with correct punctuation: 'it is raining outside'
    Ans: It is raining outside.

mcqs.q: What does 'croaking' mean?
options: A sound made by a frog
mcqs.why: The vocabulary list gives 'croaking' as a sound made by a frog, matching the frog in the fable who croaked about.

mcqs.q: What does 'intent' mean?
options: A sound made by a frog
mcqs.why: The vocabulary list gives 'intent' as the purpose to do something, as in the frog's intent to get into mischief.

mcqs.q: What does 'frightened' mean?

A place where money is kept

mcqs.q: In 'They usually park their cars outside their house', what does 'park' mean?
options: A public garden for walking and playing
The land along the side of a river
A small stick used to light a fire

mcqs.q: In 'Sara opened an account in a bank', what does 'bank' mean?

A place where money is kept

A small pointed piece of metal

mcqs.q: Identify the reflexive pronoun: 'God helps those who help themselves.'
mcqs.why: The grammar exercise identifies 'themselves' as the reflexive pronoun in this sentence, referring back to 'those'.

lessons.title: Writing
lessons.notes_html:
D) Writing — 1. Learning to Write: Write a fable about your favourite animals. Also note the elements of the fable

  • Q: Write a fable about your favourite animals and note its elements.
    Ans: The Kind Sparrow and the Cat: Once a little sparrow lived in a tree near a house. One cold morning she saw a cat shivering under the tree. The sparrow dropped soft dry leaves and feathers for the cat to rest on. The cat thanked her. A few days later the sparrow's chick fell from the nest. The cat gently picked up the chick and placed it back near the tree, and called the sparrow. From that day they became good friends. Elements — Characters: the sparrow, her chick and the cat. Setting: a tree near a house on a cold morning. Plot: the sparrow helps the cat, and later the cat saves the sparrow's chick. Conflict: the chick falls from the nest. Resolution: the cat saves the chick. Moral: Do good and good will come back to you.

D) Writing — 2. Creative Writing: Write a fable with the moral 'A Friend in need is a Friend Indeed'

  • Q: Write a fable with the moral 'A Friend in need is a Friend Indeed'.
    Ans: Once a deer and a rabbit were close friends. One day hunters came to the forest and the deer got his leg caught in a net. He cried for help. Many animals ran away in fear, but the little rabbit came running. He bit the ropes of the net with his sharp teeth, one by one, until the deer was free. Both of them ran to a safe place before the hunters returned. The deer thanked the rabbit and said that he had proved to be a true friend. Moral: A friend in need is a friend indeed.

mcqs.q: In the model fable 'The Kind Sparrow and the Cat', who are the characters?
options: The deer, the rabbit and the hunters
The mouse, the frog and the hawk
The hen, the crow and the mouse
The sparrow, her chick and the cat
mcqs.why: The elements listed for the model fable name the characters as the sparrow, her chick and the cat.

mcqs.q: What is the setting of the model sparrow fable?
options: A tree near a house on a cold morning
A pond in a meadow in summer
A forest during a hunting season
mcqs.why: The elements listed for the model fable give the setting as a tree near a house on a cold morning.

mcqs.q: How did the sparrow help the cat in the model fable?
options: She brought the cat food from the house
She dropped soft dry leaves and feathers for the cat to rest on
She built the cat a nest in the tree
She chased away the dogs near the house
mcqs.why: The model fable says the sparrow saw the cat shivering and dropped soft dry leaves and feathers for the cat to rest on.

mcqs.q: What is the conflict in the model sparrow fable?
options: The cat cannot find any food to eat
The tree is cut down by the people
The sparrow's chick falls from the nest
The sparrow loses her way home
mcqs.why: The elements listed for the model fable give the conflict as the chick falling from the nest a few days later.

mcqs.q: How is the conflict resolved in the model sparrow fable?
options: The sparrow builds a new nest on the ground
The people of the house catch the chick
The chick learns to fly the same day
The cat gently picks up the chick and places it back near the tree
mcqs.why: The resolution listed for the model fable is that the cat gently picked up the chick, placed it back near the tree and called the sparrow.

mcqs.q: What is the moral of the model sparrow fable?
options: Do good and good will come back to you
A friend in need is a friend indeed
Slow and steady wins the race
mcqs.why: The model fable ends with the moral 'Do good and good will come back to you', because the cat returned the sparrow's kindness.

mcqs.q: In the creative fable, how did the deer get into trouble?
options: He fell into a deep river while drinking
His leg got caught in a net set by hunters
He was chased by a lion in the forest
He lost his way in the dark forest
mcqs.why: The creative fable says hunters came to the forest and the deer's leg got caught in a net, and he cried for help.

mcqs.q: How did the rabbit free the deer?
options: He pulled the net away with his paws
He called the other animals to lift it
He bit the ropes of the net with his sharp teeth, one by one
He dug a hole under the net
mcqs.why: The creative fable says the little rabbit came running and bit the ropes of the net with his sharp teeth, one by one, until the deer was free.

mcqs.q: What did the other animals do when the deer cried for help?
options: They all came to free the deer
They went to call the hunters back
They hid the deer under the leaves
Many animals ran away in fear
mcqs.why: The creative fable says many animals ran away in fear, but the little rabbit came running to help his friend.

mcqs.q: What is the moral of the creative fable about the deer and the rabbit?
options: A friend in need is a friend indeed
Do good and good will come back to you
As you sow, so shall you reap
Slow and steady wins the race
mcqs.why: The creative writing task and its fable carry the moral 'A Friend in need is a Friend Indeed', proved by the rabbit's help.

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Getting Started — Let's Talk

  • Q: What wrong are they doing?
    Ans: In the pictures the boys are teasing and making fun of a boy, fighting and pulling each other's hair, quarrelling angrily, and one boy is throwing litter into the pond and spoiling the water.
  • Q: What should they be doing instead?
    Ans: Instead of teasing, fighting and quarrelling, they should speak kindly, play together peacefully and help one another. Instead of throwing litter in the pond, they should keep the water and their surroundings clean and throw litter in a dustbin.

Pre-reading

  • Q: Read the title 'Do What's Right' and tell five words related to it.
    Ans: Honesty, truth, kindness, help, right.
  • Q: Why should we be thankful to Allah?
    Ans: We should be thankful to Allah all the time for all His blessings, such as our health, food, family and home, and for showing us the right path.

While-reading — Why do you think moral values are important for us?

  • Q: Why do you think moral values are important for us?
    Ans: Moral values are important for us because they teach us to do what is right. They stop us from telling lies and being greedy, and guide us to return things to their owners, to be honest, and to live peacefully and happily with others.

Post-reading — What would you do if you were Raffay?

  • Q: What would you do if you were Raffay?
    Ans: If I were Raffay, I would do the same as he did in the end. I would not keep the wallet or spend the money. I would go to Mohsin's house, tell him the whole story honestly and return his wallet to him.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension (i) Answer these questions

  • Q: What things did Raffay want to buy with the money?
    Ans: With the money in the wallet, Raffay wanted to buy sweets, toys and chocolates. He also thought of eating some chips and sweets.
  • Q: What two things had Raffay's teacher told him to do?
    Ans: Raffay's teacher had told him, first, never to tell a lie, and secondly, when you find something unattended, return it to whom it belongs.
  • Q: Why should we be honest?
    Ans: We should be honest because honesty is always praised and it makes us feel happy and peaceful. In the story Mohsin praised Raffay for his honesty, and Raffay felt happy after returning the wallet. A dishonest person feels sorry and restless, as Raffay did when he hid the wallet and told a lie.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension (ii) Arrange the words in alphabetical order according to the first letter: invitation, valley, camera, excited, jeep

  • Q: Arrange in alphabetical order according to the first letter: invitation, valley, camera, excited, jeep
    Ans: camera, excited, invitation, jeep, valley

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension (iii) Arrange the words in alphabetical order according to the second letter: accepted, after, arrival, always, award

  • Q: Arrange in alphabetical order according to the second letter: accepted, after, arrival, always, award
    Ans: accepted, after, always, arrival, award

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension (iv) Arrange the words in alphabetical order according to the third letter: they, thrilling, thing, thumb, thorn

  • Q: Arrange in alphabetical order according to the third letter: they, thrilling, thing, thumb, thorn
    Ans: they, thing, thorn, thrilling, thumb

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension (v) Read the lesson again and fill in the blanks with the correct options

  • Q: Raffay was feeling ______.
    Options: angry / thirsty / hungry / sleepy
    Ans: hungry
  • Q: Mohsin dropped his ______.
    Options: bag / wallet / book / bottle
    Ans: wallet
  • Q: Raffay feels ______ for his behaviour.
    Options: angry / happy / sorry / glad
    Ans: sorry
  • Q: Raffay thanked ______ for showing him the right path.
    Options: Allah / his teacher / his mother / his friend
    Ans: Allah

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 2. Analytical Reading: Look for the meanings and synonyms of the given words in a dictionary

  • Q: Give the meaning and a synonym of 'participate'.
    Ans: Meaning: to take part in an activity. Synonym: take part.
  • Q: Give the meaning and a synonym of 'remarkable'.
    Ans: Meaning: unusual or surprising in a good way, worth noticing. Synonym: amazing.
  • Q: Give the meaning and a synonym of 'improvement'.
    Ans: Meaning: the act of becoming better than before. Synonym: progress.
  • Q: Give the meaning and a synonym of 'hesitation'.
    Ans: Meaning: a pause before doing something because you are unsure or nervous. Synonym: doubt.
  • Q: Give the meaning and a synonym of 'overcome'.
    Ans: Meaning: to succeed in dealing with a problem or difficulty. Synonym: conquer.

mcqs.q: In the Getting Started pictures, what wrong is one boy doing at the pond?
options: He is throwing litter into the pond and spoiling the water
He is cleaning the pond water

He is swimming across the pond
mcqs.why: The solved answer says one boy is throwing litter into the pond and spoiling the water, while the other boys tease, fight and quarrel.

mcqs.q: What should the boys do instead of teasing, fighting and quarrelling?
options: Tease and make fun of others
Speak kindly, play together peacefully and help one another
mcqs.why: The solved answer says that instead of teasing and fighting, they should speak kindly, play together peacefully and help one another.

mcqs.q: Why should we be thankful to Allah?

mcqs.why: The lesson says moral values teach us to do what is right; they stop us from telling lies and being greedy and guide us to be honest.

options: Keep it hidden in his room
Return it to Mohsin at his house and tell him the whole story honestly

mcqs.q: What things did Raffay want to buy with the money in the wallet?
mcqs.why: The comprehension answer says Raffay wanted to buy sweets, toys and chocolates, and also thought of eating some chips and sweets.

mcqs.q: What was the second thing Raffay's teacher had told him to do?
options: Return a thing you find unattended to the person it belongs to
Hide the thing in your room
mcqs.why: The teacher told Raffay, first, never to tell a lie, and secondly, to return anything found unattended to the person it belongs to.

mcqs.q: Raffay was feeling ______.
mcqs.why: This is the book's own fill-in item from the lesson: Raffay was feeling hungry, and the correct option in the book is 'hungry'.

mcqs.q: Which word comes first when invitation, valley, camera, excited and jeep are arranged by their first letter?
mcqs.why: Arranged by first letter the order is camera, excited, invitation, jeep, valley, so 'camera' with the letter c comes first.

mcqs.q: What is a synonym of 'participate', as given in the Analytical Reading?
mcqs.why: The dictionary work in the lesson gives 'participate' the meaning 'to take part in an activity', and its synonym is 'take part'.

  • Q: Match: vowel 'e' — short and long sounds
    Ans: Short vowel sound: red. Long vowel sound: read.
  • Q: Match: vowel 'i' — short and long sounds
    Ans: Short vowel sound: sit. Long vowel sound: site.
  • Q: Match: vowel 'o' — short and long sounds
    Ans: Short vowel sound: hop. Long vowel sound: hope.
  • Q: Match: vowel 'u' — short and long sounds
    Ans: Short vowel sound: tub. Long vowel sound: tube.

A) Oral Communication — 1. Learning the Sounds (ii) Underline the short vowels and circle the long vowels from the given words

  • Q: Is the vowel sound in 'coin' short or long?
    Ans: Long vowel sound.
  • Q: Is the vowel sound in 'wave' short or long?
    Ans: Long vowel sound.
  • Q: Is the vowel sound in 'ride' short or long?
    Ans: Long vowel sound.
  • Q: Is the vowel sound in 'beg' short or long?
    Ans: Short vowel sound.
  • Q: Is the vowel sound in 'cake' short or long?
    Ans: Long vowel sound.
  • Q: Is the vowel sound in 'paint' short or long?
    Ans: Long vowel sound.
  • Q: Is the vowel sound in 'apple' short or long?
    Ans: Short vowel sound.
  • Q: Is the vowel sound in 'sun' short or long?

A) Oral Communication — 2. Learning to Speak (i) Read and practise the given dialogue

  • Q: Read and practise the given dialogue between the Teacher and Maryam. What does it teach?
    Ans: The teacher calls Raffay to bring his notebook first. Maryam asks if she should bring hers first, but the teacher says she will call the students one at a time. Maryam says she has also finished her work, and the teacher tells her to wait for her turn. Maryam agrees politely. The dialogue teaches us to take turns and wait patiently.

A) Oral Communication — 2. Learning to Speak (ii) Role-play activity on how to take turns using the words first, next, later, etc.

  • Q: Conduct a role-play on taking turns. (Model dialogue)
    Ans: Student 1: First, I will read the lesson aloud. Student 2: Next, I will answer the first question. Student 3: After that, I will write the answers on the board. Student 4: Later, we will check the work together. In this way everyone gets a turn and no one is left out.

C) Language Focus — 1. Vocabulary Building (i) Read the given words with their meanings

  • Q: In 'This is her dress. This is hers,' which words are the possessive adjective and the possessive pronoun?

  • Q: In 'This is his pencil box. This is his,' which words are the possessive adjective and the possessive pronoun?

  • Q: In 'This is our house. This is ours,' which words are the possessive adjective and the possessive pronoun?

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar (ii) Write five sentences of your own using some of these pronouns

  • Q: Write five sentences using personal and possessive pronouns. (Model)
    Ans: 1. This is my bag. It is mine. 2. That is your notebook. It is yours. 3. This is her pen. It is hers. 4. That is their classroom. It is theirs. 5. This is our garden. It is ours.

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar: Prepositions of Position and Time (iii) Read the following prepositions of position and time with their sentences

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar (iv) Use prepositions of position and time in sentences of your own

  • Q: Use prepositions of position in your own sentences. (Model)
    Ans: The students are sitting in front of the teacher. My bag is behind my chair. The library is next to our classroom.
  • Q: Use prepositions of time in your own sentences. (Model)
    Ans: We play in the evening. Our school starts at eight o'clock. We have a holiday on Sunday.

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar: Adverb of Manner (v) Read the following sentences

  • Q: Identify the adverb of manner: 'He swims well.'

  • Q: Identify the adverb of manner: 'He ran quickly.'

  • Q: Identify the adverb of manner: 'She spoke in a friendly way.'

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar (vi) Underline the adverbs of manner in the text 'Do What's Right'

  • Q: Find the adverbs of manner in the text 'Do What's Right'.
    Ans: The adverbs of manner in the text are: 'quietly' (he hid the wallet and stayed in his room quietly), 'accidentally' (Mohsin had accidentally dropped his wallet on the road) and 'quickly' (he quickly ran to Mohsin's house).

lessons.title: Writing
lessons.notes_html:
D) Writing — 1. Learning to Write (i) Write a short invitation to your friend to attend your birthday party

  • Q: Write a short invitation to your friend to attend your birthday party.
    Ans: Date, time and location: Sunday, 22 November 2026, at 4 p.m., at my home. Dear Ahmed, I am happy to invite you to my birthday party. We will cut the cake, play games and have snacks together. Please come on time and join the fun. I will be waiting for you. (Sender's Name) Ali

D) Writing — 1. Learning to Write (ii) Write a short note accepting the invitation above

  • Q: Write a short note accepting the invitation above.
    Ans: Dear Ali, Thank you for your invitation. That is so kind of you. I am very happy to accept it. I will surely come to your birthday party on Sunday at 4 p.m. I am looking forward to meeting you and all our friends there. Yours lovingly, Ahmed

D) Writing — 2. Creative Writing: Write about an incident of your life when you felt disappointed

  • Q: Write about an incident of your life when you felt disappointed and how you dealt with it.
    Ans: Last year I worked very hard for my class test, but I got fewer marks than I had expected. I felt very disappointed and sad. I did not lose heart. I told my teacher about it, found the topics in which I was weak, and studied them again every day. In the next test I got much better marks. This incident taught me that disappointment goes away when we keep trying and do what is right.

mcqs.why: The model invitation gives the party time as 4 p.m. on Sunday, 22 November 2026, at the sender's home.

mcqs.why: The model invitation gives the location of the birthday party as 'at my home', the home of the sender, Ali.

mcqs.why: The model invitation is signed with the sender's name Ali, and it invites his friend Ahmed to the birthday party.

mcqs.q: Who is invited to the birthday party in the model invitation?
mcqs.why: The model invitation begins 'Dear Ahmed' and invites Ahmed; Ahmed's reply note is signed 'Yours lovingly, Ahmed'.

mcqs.q: What will the children do at the party, according to the invitation?
options: Cut the cake, play games and have snacks together
Watch a film at the cinema
mcqs.why: The model invitation says: We will cut the cake, play games and have snacks together at the birthday party.

mcqs.q: How does Ahmed reply to the invitation?
options: He thanks Ali and happily accepts it
He asks to change the day
He does not reply at all
mcqs.why: Ahmed's note thanks Ali for the invitation, calls it kind, and says he is very happy to accept it and will surely come.

mcqs.q: In the model incident, why did the writer feel disappointed?
options: He got fewer marks in the class test than he had expected
mcqs.why: The creative writing answer says he worked hard for the class test but got fewer marks than expected, so he felt disappointed and sad.

mcqs.q: How did the writer deal with his disappointment?
options: He found his weak topics and studied them again every day
mcqs.why: The model answer says he told his teacher, found the topics in which he was weak, and studied them again every day.

mcqs.why: The model incident ends with the writer getting much better marks in the next test, learning that disappointment goes away when we keep trying.

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Getting Started — Let's Talk

  • Q: What is happening in these pictures? Describe it in your own words.
    Ans: In the first picture, children with school bags are going to a small village school. In the second picture, many students are standing in front of a big, beautiful school building. Both pictures show children getting education, which makes a nation strong.
  • Q: What can you do for the welfare of society?
    Ans: I can study hard, keep my surroundings clean, help poor and needy people, and obey the rules. In this way I can work for the welfare of my society.

A Nation's Strength — Pre-reading, While-reading and Post Reading

  • Q: Pre-reading: What do the colours of our national flag mean?
    Ans: The green colour of our flag stands for the Muslim majority of Pakistan and prosperity, the white stripe stands for the minorities and peace, and the crescent and star stand for progress and light.
  • Q: Pre-reading: How do you celebrate the Independence Day of Pakistan?
    Ans: We celebrate Independence Day on 14th August by hoisting the national flag, decorating our homes and schools with flags and buntings, singing national songs and remembering the sacrifices of our elders.
  • Q: While-reading: How do brave men make a nation strong?
    Ans: Brave men work while others sleep and dare while others fly away. They stand fast for truth and honour and build the nation's pillars deep, so they make the nation strong.
  • Q: Post Reading: How can we contribute to make our nation great and strong? Share your views.
    Ans: We can contribute by getting education, working hard and honestly, obeying the law, keeping our country clean and helping one another. Such good and selfless people make a nation great and strong.
  • Q: Post Reading: What is the main idea of the poem? Discuss it in your words.
    Ans: The main idea of the poem is that a nation is not made great by gold or wealth, but by its brave, truthful and hardworking men. Such men are the real strength of a nation.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension i. Answer these questions

  • Q: Who can make a nation strong?
    Ans: Only brave, truthful and hardworking men can make a nation strong. Not gold, but such men make a people great and strong.
  • Q: What is the message of the poem in your opinion?
    Ans: In my opinion, the message of the poem is that the real wealth of a nation is its good people. Brave men who work hard, stand for truth and honour, and face every challenge make their nation strong and great.
  • Q: Why is education important for our country?
    Ans: Education is important for our country because it makes people knowledgeable and skilful. It makes lives better for those who struggle for their survival, and educated people work hard for the welfare of society.

Reading Comprehension ii. Look and read the given table of contents of a book. Then answer the given questions

  • Q: What is the title of the first chapter of the book?
    Ans: The Thirsty Crow
  • Q: Which page does the third chapter start on?
    Ans: The third chapter, 'Love for the Country', starts on page 9.
  • Q: What is the title of the last chapter of the book?
    Ans: The Red Fat Hen

Reading Comprehension iii. Read the given glossary

  • Q: ability
    Ans: a special skill or talent
  • Q: altitude
    Ans: the height above the Earth's surface or sea level
  • Q: battle
    Ans: a fight or conflict with or without weapons
  • Q: bottom
    Ans: the lowest, last, or underside of something
  • Q: career
    Ans: what you do for a living
  • Q: choice
    Ans: the act of making a selection
  • Q: Look up the meaning of 'altitude' in the given glossary and write it.
    Ans: Altitude means the height above the Earth's surface or sea level.
  • Q: Why do we use a glossary?
    Ans: We use a glossary to find the meanings of words in a book that are newly introduced or uncommon. A glossary is given at the end of a book.

Reading Comprehension iv. Take any ten words from your textbook and make your own glossary

  • Q: Make your own glossary of ten words from the textbook.
    Ans: Model glossary: brave: not afraid, ready to face danger; dare: to be brave enough to do something; honour: great respect for somebody; nation: people of a country; pillar: a strong upright support of a building; sake: the reason or purpose of doing something; strength: the quality of being strong; suffer: to feel pain or undergo hardship; survive: to continue to live; welfare: health, comfort and happiness of people.

Reading Comprehension v–vi. Read the given map and its key / Look at the compass and answer the given questions

  • Q: Write the direction of the mountains from the forest.
    Ans: The mountains are to the east of the forest.
  • Q: Write the direction of the river from the forest.
    Ans: The river is to the north of the forest.
  • Q: Write the direction of the railroad from the river.
    Ans: The railroad is to the north of the river.

Reading Comprehension vii. Read the poem again and fill in the blanks with the correct options

  • Q: ______ cannot make people great and strong.
    Options: Money / Gold / Diamonds / Silver
    Ans: Gold
  • Q: ______ men work while others sleep.
    Options: Dull / Coward / Brave / Weak
    Ans: Brave
  • Q: The men who dare while others ______.
    Options: cook / smile / fly / cry
    Ans: fly
  • Q: Great men lift the nation to the ______.
    Options: park / clouds / sky / rainbow
    Ans: sky
  • Q: Only ______ can make a nation strong.
    Options: mountains / animals / men / hills
    Ans: men

2. Analytical Reading — Read the biography of the Quaid-e-Azam and list down his five qualities in your notebook

  • Q: List five qualities of the Quaid-e-Azam.
    Ans: Five qualities of the Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah were: 1) He was honest and truthful. 2) He was hardworking and disciplined. 3) He was determined and never gave up. 4) He was a man of principles who followed the law. 5) He was selfless and worked only for his nation. Note: the biography itself is not printed in this unit; the book asks students to read it from reference books.

lessons.title: Sounds and Speaking
lessons.notes_html:
A) Oral Communication — 1. Learning the Sounds: '-ed' Sounds i. Read the given sentences and pronounce the '-ed' sound endings correctly

  • Q: showed — 'Hina showed me her new dress.' The '-ed' sound is:
    Ans: /d/
  • Q: lived — 'They lived in Lahore.' The '-ed' sound is:
    Ans: /d/
  • Q: played — 'He played in the evening.' The '-ed' sound is:
    Ans: /d/
  • Q: wanted — 'Ali wanted to buy a new house.' The '-ed' sound is:
    Ans: /id/
  • Q: started — 'She started her new job.' The '-ed' sound is:
    Ans: /id/
  • Q: faded — 'These flowers had faded.' The '-ed' sound is:
    Ans: /id/
  • Q: worked — 'He worked hard for his test.' The '-ed' sound is:
    Ans: /t/
  • Q: walked — 'We walked in the morning.' The '-ed' sound is:
    Ans: /t/
  • Q: helped — 'They helped a poor man.' The '-ed' sound is:
    Ans: /t/

Learning the Sounds ii. Underline the words with the -ed ending and write them in their relevant columns

  • Q: It rained heavily last night. — 'rained' goes in the column:
    Ans: /d/ — rained
  • Q: The labourers had loaded the truck. — 'loaded' goes in the column:
    Ans: /id/ — loaded
  • Q: Ali asked his teacher a question. — 'asked' goes in the column:
    Ans: /t/ — asked
  • Q: She laughed aloud. — 'laughed' goes in the column:
    Ans: /t/ — laughed
  • Q: The children jumped on the bouncy castle. — 'jumped' goes in the column:
    Ans: /t/ — jumped
  • Q: They waited for him last night. — 'waited' goes in the column:
    Ans: /id/ — waited

2. Learning to Speak i. Read and practise the given dialogue

  • Q: What national event is coming on March 23?
    Ans: Pakistan Day is coming on March 23.
  • Q: Why do we celebrate Pakistan Day?
    Ans: We celebrate Pakistan Day to remember the Lahore Resolution of 1940. This resolution proposed the idea of an independent state for Muslims, so it is also called the Pakistan Resolution.
  • Q: Where was this event held?
    Ans: It was held at Manto Park, Lahore (Minar-e-Pakistan).
  • Q: What is Sir Yasir arranging about this day?
    Ans: Sir Yasir is arranging a speech competition about Pakistan Day, and he wants all the students to come and participate.

Learning to Speak ii. Conduct a dialogue on 'Benefits of Education'. Make sure students use polite expressions to seek attention

  • Q: Conduct a dialogue on 'Benefits of Education' using polite expressions to seek attention.
    Ans: Model dialogue: Student 1: 'Excuse me, may I say something? Education makes us knowledgeable and skilful.' Student 2: 'Sorry to interrupt, but I agree with you. Education also makes our lives better.' Student 1: 'May I add one more point, please? An educated nation always works hard for the welfare of society.' Student 2: 'Thank you for sharing your views. Education is truly the strength of a nation.'

lessons.title: Language Focus
lessons.notes_html:
C) Language Focus — 1. Vocabulary Building i. Read the given words with their meanings

  • Q: honour
    Ans: great respect for somebody
  • Q: suffer
    Ans: to feel pain, to undergo hardship
  • Q: dare
    Ans: to be brave enough to do something
  • Q: strength
    Ans: the quality or degree of being brave
  • Q: nation
    Ans: people of a country

Vocabulary Building ii. Writing a Poem — Write a poem on the topic 'My Country' with the help of the given rhyming words (land, stand / dream, stream / day, way)

  • Q: Write a poem on the topic 'My Country' using the rhyming words land–stand, dream–stream and day–way.
    Ans: My Country: Pakistan is my dear land, / For its honour I will always stand. / To see it progress is my dream, / May its happiness flow like a stream. / I will work hard every day, / And serve my country in every way.

Vocabulary Building iii. Entry Word — Look at the given page of a dictionary and notice the use of alphabetical arrangement of words. Also notice the use of the entry word

  • Q: What is an entry word?
    Ans: An entry word is a word that can be looked up in a dictionary. Entry words are usually printed in dark print.
  • Q: Write the entry words sake, sleep and stand in alphabetical order, with their parts of speech.
    Ans: sake (noun), sleep (verb), stand (verb). They are already in alphabetical order: sake comes first, then sleep, then stand.

2. Learning to Spell — Fill in the missing letters to complete the words

  • Q: ______onour
    Ans: honour
  • Q: pill______rs
    Ans: pillars
  • Q: bra______e
    Ans: brave
  • Q: s______ffer
    Ans: suffer
  • Q: bu______ld
    Ans: build

3. Grammar — Pronoun-antecedent Agreement i. Read the given sentences and notice the use of pronoun-antecedent agreement

  • Q: In 'I bought a book about Pakistan. It is very interesting', which pronoun is used for 'book' and why?
    Ans: The pronoun 'It' is used for 'book' because 'book' is a singular noun, and a singular pronoun replaces a singular noun.
  • Q: In 'Pakistani soldiers are brave. They protect us', which pronoun is used for 'soldiers' and why?
    Ans: The pronoun 'They' is used for 'soldiers' because 'soldiers' is a plural noun, and a plural pronoun replaces a plural noun.
  • Q: In 'Ahmed is my neighbour. He is a good man', which pronoun is used for 'Ahmed' and why?
    Ans: The pronoun 'He' is used for 'Ahmed' because Ahmed is masculine, and a masculine pronoun replaces a masculine noun.
  • Q: In 'My mother is very caring. She loves us', which pronoun is used for 'mother' and why?
    Ans: The pronoun 'She' is used for 'mother' because mother is feminine, and a feminine pronoun replaces a feminine noun.

Grammar ii. Fill in the blanks with correct pronouns to complete these sentences

  • Q: Sara completed ______ (his, her) work.
    Ans: her
  • Q: Ali left ______ (his, her) keys in his house.
    Ans: his
  • Q: They worked hard to make ______ (their, him) nation strong.
    Ans: their
  • Q: Look at the apples. Let's go pick ______. (her, them)
    Ans: them
  • Q: They drank coffee even though ______ (he, it) was cold.
    Ans: it

Grammar — Be, Do and Have as Helping Verbs (Negative Form) iii. Read the given sentences

  • Q: Give the negative 'be' form sentences from the table.
    Ans: Raffay is not studying. The ants are not eating. It was not raining.
  • Q: Give the negative 'do' form sentences from the table.
    Ans: He does not work. She did not like spicy food. We do not practise tennis.
  • Q: Give the negative 'have' form sentences from the table.
    Ans: He has not invited us. They have not decided to go out. We had not completed our work.

Grammar — Use of 'can', 'cannot', 'may' and 'may not' iv–v. Read the given sentences and notice the use of 'can', 'cannot', 'may' and 'may not'

  • Q: 'Ali can speak different languages.' What does 'can' show here?
    Ans: It shows the ability to do something.
  • Q: 'Can we go home now?' What does 'Can' show here?
    Ans: It is used to ask permission.
  • Q: 'This news can't be true.' What does 'can't' show here?
    Ans: It shows that something is impossible.
  • Q: 'He may join Pakistan Army.' What does 'may' show here?
    Ans: It shows possibility.
  • Q: 'May I come in, sir?' What does 'May' show here?
    Ans: It is used to ask permission.
  • Q: 'There may not be many people there.' What does 'may not' show here?
    Ans: It expresses doubt.
  • Q: 'You may not borrow the car until you learn driving.' What does 'may not' show here?
    Ans: It expresses prohibition.

Grammar vi. Write two sentences with 'can', 'cannot', 'may' and 'may not' each

  • Q: Write two sentences with 'can'.
    Ans: 1) I can ride a bicycle. 2) She can speak English well.
  • Q: Write two sentences with 'cannot'.
    Ans: 1) A baby cannot walk. 2) We cannot fly like birds.
  • Q: Write two sentences with 'may'.
    Ans: 1) May I drink water, please? 2) It may rain today.
  • Q: Write two sentences with 'may not'.
    Ans: 1) You may not play in the street. 2) He may not come to school today.

Grammar — Adverbs of Time and Place vii. Read the given sentences and notice the use of adverbs of time and place

  • Q: In 'Ali will call you later', identify the adverb and its type.
    Ans: 'later' — adverb of time.
  • Q: In 'He is putting his toys inside the box', identify the adverb and its type.
    Ans: 'inside' — adverb of place.
  • Q: In 'I saw Sana today', identify the adverb and its type.
    Ans: 'today' — adverb of time.
  • Q: In 'Hira lives near the school', identify the adverb and its type.
    Ans: 'near' — adverb of place.
  • Q: In 'Please, sit here', identify the adverb and its type.
    Ans: 'here' — adverb of place.

Grammar viii. Use the given adverbs of place in your sentences and write them in your notebook

  • Q: Use 'there' in a sentence.
    Ans: My school is over there.
  • Q: Use 'far' in a sentence.
    Ans: My village is far from the city.
  • Q: Use 'somewhere' in a sentence.
    Ans: I have kept my keys somewhere in this room.
  • Q: Use 'downstairs' in a sentence.
    Ans: Mother is waiting for us downstairs.
  • Q: Use 'away' in a sentence.
    Ans: The bird flew away.

Grammar — Full Stops with Abbreviations viii–ix. Read the given abbreviations with their full form and write five more abbreviations

  • Q: Capt.
    Ans: captain
  • Q: dept.
    Ans: department
  • Q: govt.
    Ans: government
  • Q: Ltd.
    Ans: limited
  • Q: What is the abbreviation of 'approximately'?
    Ans: approx. Note: in the printed table on page 94 the abbreviation cell for 'approximately' is blank; 'approx.' is the standard abbreviation written with a full stop.
  • Q: Write five more abbreviations with full stops.
    Ans: Dr. (doctor), Mr. (mister), Mrs. (mistress), e.g. (for example), etc. (and so on). We use a full stop to mark abbreviations.

lessons.title: Writing
lessons.notes_html:
D) Writing — 1. Learning to Write i. Read the central idea of the poem

  • Q: What is the central idea of the poem 'A Nation's Strength' as given in the book?
    Ans: The poet tells us about the secret of a nation's success, which is its manpower. Good people are more important than gold and jewels. The people who make their nation strong are great and selfless. They fight for the truth and honour of their nation. They are the brave people who face all challenges. If a nation has such people, then no one can stop this nation from making progress and getting strong.

Learning to Write ii. Read the given poem 'My Flag' and write its central idea in your own words

  • Q: Write the central idea of the poem 'My Flag' by Dr. Tafazzal in your own words.
    Ans: The central idea of the poem is that we must never forget the sacrifices of our mothers, sisters and great men who laid down their lives for a just cause. Because of their efforts, the flag of our country flies very high and Pakistan came into being. We should always remember their sacrifices with love and respect.

2. Creative Writing — Write what do you want to be when you grow up so you can serve your country, and why?

  • Q: Write what you want to be when you grow up so you can serve your country, and why.
    Ans: When I grow up, I want to be a teacher so that I can serve my country. Education makes a nation strong by making people knowledgeable and skilful. As a teacher, I will educate the children of my village, teach them honesty and hard work, and help them become good citizens. In this way, I will build the pillars of my nation deep and strong.

mcqs.q: What is the secret of a nation's success, according to the central idea given in the book?
options: Its manpower, that is, its good people
mcqs.why: The book's central idea says the secret of a nation's success is its manpower, and good people are more important than gold and jewels.

mcqs.q: According to the central idea, good people are more important than ______.
mcqs.why: The central idea given in the book says good people are more important than gold and jewels for the success of a nation.

mcqs.q: How are the people who make their nation strong described in the central idea?
mcqs.why: The central idea in the book says the people who make their nation strong are great and selfless and fight for the truth and honour of their nation.

mcqs.q: For what do these brave people fight, according to the central idea?
options: The truth and honour of their nation
mcqs.why: The central idea says these brave people fight for the truth and honour of their nation and face all challenges bravely.

mcqs.q: What happens if a nation has such brave people, according to the central idea?
options: No one can stop it from making progress and getting strong
mcqs.why: The central idea ends by saying that if a nation has such people, then no one can stop this nation from making progress and getting strong.

mcqs.q: In the poem 'My Flag', whose sacrifices must we never forget?
options: Our mothers, sisters and great men who laid down their lives
mcqs.why: The solved central idea of 'My Flag' says we must never forget the sacrifices of our mothers, sisters and great men who laid down their lives for a just cause.

mcqs.q: Because of their efforts, what happened, according to 'My Flag'?
options: The flag of our country flies very high and Pakistan came into being
mcqs.why: The solved central idea says that because of their efforts, the flag of our country flies very high and Pakistan came into being.

mcqs.q: Who wrote the poem 'My Flag'?
mcqs.why: The solved writing item names the poem as 'My Flag' by Dr. Tafazzal, and the book prints the poet's name below the poem.

mcqs.q: What does the writer want to be when he grows up, in the model creative writing?
mcqs.why: The model answer says: When I grow up, I want to be a teacher so that I can serve my country by educating its children.

mcqs.q: Why does the writer want to become a teacher?
options: To earn a lot of money
To educate the children and teach them honesty and hard work
To work in a big office
mcqs.why: The model answer says that as a teacher he will educate the children of his village, teach them honesty and hard work, and help them become good citizens.

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Getting Started — Let's Talk

  • Q: Think of more ideas to make others happy and share with your classmates.
    Ans: We can make others happy by sharing our things with friends and family, helping others in their difficult times, donating money and things to the poor, and protecting the rights of others. Sharing is caring.
  • Q: Have you ever helped a friend in difficulty?
    Ans: Yes, I once helped my friend when he had lost his books. I shared my books with him and helped him complete his work. He was very happy and thanked me.

Eid-ul-Azha — Pre-reading, While-reading and Post Reading

  • Q: While-reading: In which Islamic month do we celebrate Eid-ul-Adha?
    Ans: We celebrate Eid-ul-Azha on the 10th of Dhul-Hijjah, so it is celebrated in the Islamic month of Dhul-Hijjah.
  • Q: While-reading: How many family members are there in the picture?
    Ans: There are five family members in the picture, sitting together around the table.
  • Q: While-reading: What did Suleman want to have on Eid-ul-Azha?
    Ans: Suleman wanted to buy a goat for Eid-ul-Azha.
  • Q: Post Reading: How do you help the poor and needy on Eid?
    Ans: On Eid, we share the meat of the sacrificed animal among friends, relatives and the poor. We also give money and food to the poor and needy so that they can also enjoy the festival.
  • Q: Post Reading: What message does this religious festival convey?
    Ans: This festival conveys the message of sharing and sacrifice. It teaches us to obey Allah, to be thankful to Him for His blessings, and to share our happiness with the poor and needy.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension i. Answer these questions

  • Q: When do Muslims celebrate Eid-ul-Azha?
    Ans: Muslims celebrate Eid-ul-Azha on the 10th of Dhul-Hijjah every year.
  • Q: How do we celebrate Eid-ul-Azha?
    Ans: We dress up in the nicest clothes and say Eid prayers in the morning to thank Allah. We sacrifice animals — goats, cows and camels — on this Eid and share the meat among friends, relatives and the poor.
  • Q: What did Suleman buy for Eid-ul-Azha?
    Ans: Suleman bought a white goat for Eid-ul-Azha. His father took him to the cattle market on Sunday and they bought the goat there.

Reading Comprehension ii. Read the given chart about 'how to keep our environment safe and clean'

  • Q: What must we do to keep the environment clean?
    Ans: We must throw garbage in wastebins, sharpen pencils in wastebins, keep walls clean and keep streets clean.
  • Q: How can we save water?
    Ans: We can save water by turning off the water tap after use, turning off the tap while brushing teeth, and using bucket water for a bath.
  • Q: How can we save electricity?
    Ans: We can save electricity by turning off lights and fans when we leave a room vacant, turning off lights, and unplugging electronics when they are not in use.
  • Q: What are the 3R-Principles given in the chart?
    Ans: The 3R-Principles are Reduce, Reuse and Recycle. We should avoid the use of plastic bags and try to reuse and recycle used things.

Reading Comprehension iii. Read the given checklist and tick (✓) the measures you take to save the environment

  • Q: Plant new trees.
    Ans: ✓ — Yes, I plant new trees.
  • Q: Keep your house and rooms clean.
    Ans: ✓ — Yes, I keep my house and rooms clean.
  • Q: Turn off the tap while brushing.
    Ans: ✓ — Yes, I turn off the tap while brushing.
  • Q: Turn off the lights when they are not in use.
    Ans: ✓ — Yes, I turn off the lights when they are not in use.
  • Q: Use bucket water for a bath.
    Ans: ✓ — Yes, I use bucket water for a bath.
  • Q: Use less plastic bags.
    Ans: ✓ — Yes, I use fewer plastic bags.

Reading Comprehension iv. Read the lesson again and fill in the blanks with the correct options

  • Q: Suleman saw some banner about a ______.
    Options: clothes sale / cattle sale / food sale / mobile sale
    Ans: cattle sale
  • Q: Suleman wanted to buy a ______ for Eid.
    Options: cow / goat / camel / bull
    Ans: goat
  • Q: They are going to buy their animal for sacrifice on ______.
    Options: Tuesday / Sunday / Monday / Friday
    Ans: Sunday
  • Q: Prophet ______ had a dream about sacrificing his son.
    Options: Sulyeman / Ibrahim / Ishaq / Ismail
    Ans: Ibrahim

2. Analytical Reading — Read the story carefully. Compare your Eid day with Suleman's. Note down the differences and similarities

  • Q: Compare your Eid day with Suleman's Eid day. Note down the differences and similarities.
    Ans: Similarities: Like Suleman, I also wear new clothes on Eid, say Eid prayers with my family, sacrifice an animal and share its meat with the poor. Differences: Suleman bought a white goat from the cattle market on Sunday with his father, while my family buys a cow. Suleman also learnt about using a slaughterhouse to keep the environment clean, and I also try to keep my surroundings clean on Eid.

lessons.title: Sounds and Speaking
lessons.notes_html:
A) Oral Communication — 1. Learning the Sounds: Syllables i. Read the given words with their syllable division

  • Q: hoarding
    Ans: hoard-ing (2 syllables)
  • Q: excitement
    Ans: ex-cite-ment (3 syllables)
  • Q: conversation
    Ans: con-ver-sa-tion (4 syllables)
  • Q: sacrifice
    Ans: sac-ri-fice (3 syllables)
  • Q: remember
    Ans: re-mem-ber (3 syllables)

Learning the Sounds ii. Read the given words and divide them into their syllables. Also write their number of syllables

  • Q: impatiently
    Ans: im-pa-tient-ly — 4 syllables
  • Q: moment
    Ans: mo-ment — 2 syllables
  • Q: cattle
    Ans: cat-tle — 2 syllables
  • Q: fortnight
    Ans: fort-night — 2 syllables
  • Q: thankful
    Ans: thank-ful — 2 syllables

2. Learning to Speak i. Read and practise the given dialogue

  • Q: Why did Suleman's family decide to use a slaughterhouse to sacrifice their animals?
    Ans: They decided to use a slaughterhouse because a lot of animal waste is thrown out in the open these days, and a slaughterhouse throws all the animal waste out in a safe and clean way.
  • Q: What is environmental change, according to Suleman?
    Ans: According to Suleman, all the things we throw out or waste at home pollute the environment. This pollution causes environmental change.
  • Q: How can we save our environment, according to Suleman?
    Ans: We can save our environment by spreading awareness among people about the harmful effects of pollution, and by keeping our environment clean — disposing of garbage in a proper way and not throwing it in our streets.

Learning to Speak ii. Arrange a classroom discussion about how you celebrate your religious festivals

  • Q: How do you celebrate your religious festivals? Give a model response for the classroom discussion.
    Ans: We celebrate Eid-ul-Azha with great joy. We wear our nicest clothes, say Eid prayers in the morning to thank Allah, sacrifice an animal, and share its meat among friends, relatives and the poor. We visit our relatives and enjoy delicious food together.

mcqs.q: How many syllables are in 'hoarding' (hoard-ing)?
