lessons.title: Language Focus
lessons.notes_html:
C) Language Focus — 1. Vocabulary Building i. Read the given words with their meanings

  • Q: sacrifice
    Ans: to give away something that is dear to you
  • Q: rush
    Ans: to run hurriedly
  • Q: memorise
    Ans: to learn by heart
  • Q: enquire
    Ans: to ask for information

Vocabulary Building iii. Write synonyms and antonyms of the following words

  • Q: excited
    Ans: Synonym: thrilled / very happy. Antonym: calm / bored.
  • Q: buy
    Ans: Synonym: purchase. Antonym: sell.
  • Q: remember
    Ans: Synonym: recall. Antonym: forget.
  • Q: great
    Ans: Synonym: grand / large. Antonym: small / ordinary.

Vocabulary Building iv. Homonyms — Write the meanings of the given homonyms in your notebook. Also use them in sentences of your own

  • Q: watch, watch
    Ans: watch (noun): a small clock worn on the wrist — My father wears a watch. watch (verb): to look at something for some time — We watch television in the evening.
  • Q: fly, fly
    Ans: fly (noun): a small insect with wings — A fly is sitting on the wall. fly (verb): to move through the air — Birds fly in the sky.
  • Q: bat, bat
    Ans: bat (noun): a small animal that flies at night — A bat sleeps during the day. bat (noun): a piece of wood used in cricket — He hit the ball with his bat.
  • Q: fine, fine
    Ans: fine (adjective): good, satisfactory — I am fine, thank you. fine (noun): money paid as a punishment — He paid a fine for breaking the rule.
  • Q: park, park
    Ans: park (noun): a public garden where people walk and play — Children play in the park. park (verb): to leave a vehicle somewhere for a time — Father parked the car near the gate.

Vocabulary Building v. Homophones — Fill in the blanks with the correct homophones

  • Q: Please get a ______ of paper. (peace, piece)
    Ans: piece
  • Q: They can't ______ for you. (weight, wait)
    Ans: wait
  • Q: They are going ______ buy a goat. (too, to)
    Ans: to
  • Q: My uncle has a good ______ to tell. (tale, tell)
    Ans: tale
  • Q: Do you ______ this news. (no, know)
    Ans: know

Vocabulary Building vi. Compound Words — Choose the correct words from the given word bank and make compound words (hopper, light, time, book, cake, bird)

  • Q: grass + ______
    Ans: grasshopper
  • Q: life + ______
    Ans: lifetime
  • Q: pan + ______
    Ans: pancake
  • Q: lady + ______
    Ans: ladybird
  • Q: sun + ______
    Ans: sunlight
  • Q: note + ______
    Ans: notebook

2. Learning to Spell — Fill in the missing letters to complete the words

  • Q: s______crifice
    Ans: sacrifice
  • Q: th______ughtfully
    Ans: thoughtfully
  • Q: i______quire
    Ans: inquire
  • Q: e______citemen______
    Ans: excitement
  • Q: cele______rate
    Ans: celebrate
  • Q: m______morise
    Ans: memorise
  • Q: u______ite
    Ans: unite
  • Q: rus______
    Ans: rush

3. Grammar — Pointing Words i. Read the given sentences and notice the use of demonstrative pronouns (pointing words)

  • Q: In 'I love to eat apples and mangoes. These are my favourite', which pointing word is used and why?
    Ans: 'These' is used because apples and mangoes are plural and near.
  • Q: In 'I planted tomatoes and potatoes. These were easy to plant', which pointing word is used and why?
    Ans: 'These' is used because tomatoes and potatoes are plural and near.
  • Q: In 'We bought a new chair from the market. This is very comfortable', which pointing word is used and why?
    Ans: 'This' is used because the chair is singular and near.
  • Q: In 'I lost my book last year. That was about the history of Pakistan', which pointing word is used and why?
    Ans: 'That' is used because the book is singular and far (lost last year).

Grammar ii. Fill in the blanks with the correct demonstrative pronouns

  • Q: You will have to use your pen. ______ is mine.
    Ans: This
  • Q: Let me introduce you. Ali, ______ is Suleman.
    Ans: this
  • Q: I have five new dresses. Look ______ are very beautiful.
    Ans: These
  • Q: I made sandwiches yesterday. ______ were delicious.
    Ans: Those

Grammar — Use of 'should' and 'should not' v. Read the given sentences of 'should' and 'should not'

  • Q: What do we use 'should' for? Give examples from the book.
    Ans: We use 'should' to talk about an obligation or for things that are important for people to do. Examples: We should always follow traffic rules. You should speak the truth. We should always respect our elders.
  • Q: What do we use 'should not' for? Give examples from the book.
    Ans: We use 'should not' to advise against doing something because it is bad or wrong to do so. Examples: You should not throw garbage in the street. You should not go outside at night.

Grammar vi. Write two sentences using 'should' and 'should not' each in your notebook

  • Q: Write two sentences using 'should'.
    Ans: 1) We should keep our environment clean. 2) You should help the poor and needy.
  • Q: Write two sentences using 'should not'.
    Ans: 1) We should not waste water. 2) You should not throw garbage in the open.

Grammar — Use of Apostrophe vii. Read the given sentences and notice the use of the apostrophe

  • Q: We'll
    Ans: We will — the apostrophe marks the omitted letters in the contraction.
  • Q: didn't
    Ans: did not — the apostrophe marks the omitted letter 'o'.
  • Q: isn't
    Ans: is not — the apostrophe marks the omitted letter 'o'.
  • Q: I'm
    Ans: I am — the apostrophe marks the omitted letter 'a'.
  • Q: They're
    Ans: They are — the apostrophe marks the omitted letter 'a'.

Grammar viii. Make contractions of the following words using the apostrophe correctly in your notebook

  • Q: could not
    Ans: couldn't
  • Q: I have
    Ans: I've
  • Q: should not
    Ans: shouldn't
  • Q: you will
    Ans: you'll
  • Q: does not
    Ans: doesn't

Grammar — Adverbs of Frequency ix. Read the given sentences and notice the use of adverbs of frequency

  • Q: In 'She always sacrifices a camel on Eid-ul-Azha', identify the adverb of frequency.
    Ans: always
  • Q: In 'They often go to the park for jogging', identify the adverb of frequency.
    Ans: often
  • Q: In 'He rarely makes a mistake in the test', identify the adverb of frequency.
    Ans: rarely
  • Q: In 'They sometimes play cricket on the weekend', identify the adverb of frequency.
    Ans: sometimes
  • Q: In 'I never forget my keys in my room', identify the adverb of frequency.
    Ans: never

Grammar x. Read the given paragraph and underline the adverbs of frequency in it

  • Q: Underline the adverbs of frequency in the paragraph beginning 'I always get up early in the morning...'
    Ans: The adverbs of frequency in the paragraph are: always, often, Sometimes, rarely, usually and never.

mcqs.why: The homonyms exercise gives fly as a verb meaning to move through the air, as birds fly in the sky; as a noun it is a small insect with wings.

mcqs.q: Please get a ______ of paper. (peace, piece)
mcqs.why: The homophones exercise chooses 'piece' for a piece of paper; 'peace' sounds the same but means calm, so it does not fit here.

mcqs.q: My uncle has a good ______ to tell. Choose the correct homophone.
mcqs.why: The book prints this pair as (tale, tell), but 'tell' is not a homophone of 'tale'; the true homophone pair is tale and tail, and a story that someone tells is a 'tale'.

mcqs.q: Which compound word is made from 'grass' using the word bank?
mcqs.why: The compound words exercise joins grass with hopper from the word bank to make the compound word 'grasshopper'.

mcqs.q: Which compound word is made from 'sun' using the word bank?
mcqs.why: The compound words exercise joins sun with light from the word bank to make 'sunlight'; lady joins bird and note joins book.

mcqs.q: In 'I love to eat apples and mangoes. These are my favourite', why is 'These' used?
options: Because they are singular and near
Because apples and mangoes are plural and near
Because they are plural and far
Because they are singular and far
mcqs.why: The pointing words lesson says 'These' is used because apples and mangoes are plural and near; 'this' is singular and near, and 'those' is plural and far.

mcqs.q: What do we use 'should' for?
options: To talk about an obligation or things that are important to do
To tell how often an action happens
mcqs.why: The lesson says we use 'should' to talk about an obligation or for things that are important for people to do, like following traffic rules and speaking the truth.

mcqs.q: What is the contraction of 'could not'?
mcqs.why: The apostrophe exercise makes contractions by omitting letters: could not becomes couldn't, with the apostrophe marking the omitted letter 'o'.

lessons.title: Writing
lessons.notes_html:
D) Writing — 1. Learning to Write i. Suleman and his sister made a dessert for an Eid party. Read the recipe they followed for making 'Chocolate Banana Pops'

  • Q: Write the recipe of 'Chocolate Banana Pops' with the things needed.
    Ans: Things we need: 1 large banana, a bar of chocolate, a few toothpicks. Recipe: Cut the banana into slices. Slide each slice onto the top of a toothpick. Put the bar of chocolate in a bowl. Melt the chocolate. Dip the banana slices into the melted chocolate. Place the chocolate banana pops in a tray. Freeze them. Serve frozen.

Learning to Write ii. Find the recipe of your favourite dish on the internet and write it in your notebook

  • Q: Write the recipe of your favourite dish.
    Ans: Model recipe — Fruit Chaat: Things we need: 2 bananas, 1 apple, 1 orange, a few grapes, sugar and chaat masala. Recipe: Wash all the fruits. Peel the bananas and orange. Cut the fruits into small pieces. Put them in a bowl. Add sugar and chaat masala. Mix well. Serve fresh.

2. Creative Writing — Write a paragraph on the topic 'A Good Day with my Family' in your notebook

  • Q: Write a paragraph on the topic 'A Good Day with my Family'.
    Ans: Last Sunday, I spent a good day with my family. We got up early and had breakfast together. Then we went to a park near our home. We played games, ate delicious food and took pictures. In the evening, we visited our grandparents and shared the meat of Eid with our neighbours. I felt very happy because I spent the whole day with the people I love.

mcqs.q: Which of these is needed to make 'Chocolate Banana Pops'?
mcqs.why: The recipe's 'Things we need' list gives 1 large banana, a bar of chocolate and a few toothpicks for making Chocolate Banana Pops.

mcqs.q: What is the first step of the 'Chocolate Banana Pops' recipe?
mcqs.why: The recipe begins: Cut the banana into slices, then slide each slice onto the top of a toothpick before melting the chocolate.

mcqs.q: After cutting, each banana slice is slid onto ______.
mcqs.why: The recipe says: Slide each slice onto the top of a toothpick, then dip the banana slices into the melted chocolate.

mcqs.q: How are the Chocolate Banana Pops served?
mcqs.why: The recipe ends: Place the chocolate banana pops in a tray, freeze them, and serve them frozen.

mcqs.q: In the model Fruit Chaat recipe, what is added to the cut fruits?
mcqs.why: The model recipe for Fruit Chaat says: Put the cut fruits in a bowl, add sugar and chaat masala, mix well and serve fresh.

mcqs.q: How is the model Fruit Chaat served?
mcqs.why: The model Fruit Chaat recipe ends with 'Serve fresh', after mixing the cut fruits with sugar and chaat masala in a bowl.

mcqs.q: In 'A Good Day with my Family', where did the family go after breakfast?
options: To a park near their home
mcqs.why: The model paragraph says that after breakfast together, the family went to a park near their home, played games, ate delicious food and took pictures.

mcqs.q: In the evening, in the model paragraph, the family ______.
options: visited their grandparents and shared the meat of Eid with neighbours
mcqs.why: The model paragraph says that in the evening they visited their grandparents and shared the meat of Eid with their neighbours.

mcqs.q: What did the family do at the park, in the model paragraph?
options: Played games, ate delicious food and took pictures
mcqs.why: The model paragraph says that at the park they played games, ate delicious food and took pictures together.

mcqs.q: Why did the writer feel happy at the end of the paragraph?
options: Because he spent the whole day with the people he loves
mcqs.why: The paragraph ends: I felt very happy because I spent the whole day with the people I love, that is, with my family.

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension: Write the elements of the story 'A Mouse and the Lion'

  • Q: Characters:
    Ans: A lion and a small mouse.
  • Q: Setting:
    Ans: A jungle (forest), where the lion lived.
  • Q: Plot:
    Ans: A mouse ran over a sleeping lion and woke him up. The lion caught the mouse but let it go when it promised to help him one day. Later, the lion was caught in a hunter's net.
  • Q: Conflict:
    Ans: The lion was trapped in the hunter's net and could not free himself.
  • Q: Resolution:
    Ans: The little mouse came and gnawed the ropes of the net with its sharp teeth and set the lion free. In this way, the mouse kept its promise.

mcqs.q: Who are the characters in the story 'A Mouse and the Lion'?
options: A lion and a small mouse
A lion and a big elephant
mcqs.why: The solved story elements name the characters clearly: a lion and a small mouse are the two characters of the story.

mcqs.q: Where is the story 'A Mouse and the Lion' set?
options: In a village near a river
A jungle (forest), where the lion lived
In a zoo in a big city
On a farm with other animals
mcqs.why: The solved setting answer says the story takes place in a jungle, that is a forest, where the lion lived.

mcqs.q: How does the plot of the story begin?
options: A lion chased a mouse through the forest
A hunter set a net for the lion
A mouse ran over a sleeping lion and woke him up
A mouse brought food for the lion
mcqs.why: The solved plot says a mouse ran over a sleeping lion and woke him up, and that is how the story begins.

mcqs.q: What did the lion do after he caught the mouse?
options: He kept it in a cage
He asked it to bring him food
He let it go when it promised to help him one day
mcqs.why: The solved plot says the lion caught the mouse but let it go when the mouse promised to help him one day.

mcqs.q: What happened to the lion later in the story?
options: He was caught in a hunter's net
He fell into a deep river
He was chased away by hunters
He got lost in the jungle
mcqs.why: The solved plot says that later the lion was caught in a hunter's net and could not get out by himself.

mcqs.q: What is the conflict in the story?
options: The mouse could not find its home
The lion was trapped in the hunter's net and could not free himself
The lion and the mouse fought over food
The hunter lost his net in the jungle
mcqs.why: The solved conflict is that the lion was trapped in the hunter's net and could not free himself from it.

mcqs.q: How did the little mouse free the lion?
options: It pulled the net away with its tail
It called other animals for help
It gnawed the ropes of the net with its sharp teeth
It cut the net with a knife
mcqs.why: The solved resolution says the little mouse gnawed the ropes of the net with its sharp teeth and set the lion free.

mcqs.q: How does the story end?
options: The lion caught the mouse again
The hunter freed the lion himself
The mouse ran away from the jungle
The mouse set the lion free and kept its promise
mcqs.why: The solved resolution says the mouse set the lion free, and in this way the mouse kept the promise it had made.

mcqs.q: What did the mouse use to gnaw the ropes of the net?
mcqs.why: The solved resolution states that the mouse gnawed the ropes of the net with its sharp teeth to free the lion.

mcqs.q: Whose net had trapped the lion?
mcqs.why: Both the solved plot and the conflict say the lion was caught and trapped in a hunter's net in the jungle.

lessons.title: Sounds and Speaking
lessons.notes_html:
A) Oral Communication — 1. Learning the Sounds: Read the given sentences. Circle the words with long vowel sounds and underline the words with short vowel sounds

  • Q: 'My mother baked a red velvet cake.' — long and short vowel words
    Ans: Long vowel sounds: baked, cake. Short vowel sounds: red, velvet.
  • Q: 'She had drawn some trees and a sun in her drawing notebook.' — long and short vowel words
    Ans: Long vowel sounds: trees, notebook. Short vowel sounds: had, sun.
  • Q: 'Ali had written a note that he could not participate in the school function.' — long and short vowel words
    Ans: Long vowel sounds: note, school. Short vowel sounds: had, written.
  • Q: 'He bought a new tub and water tube from the shop.' — long and short vowel words
    Ans: Long vowel sounds: new, tube. Short vowel sounds: tub, shop.
  • Q: 'They made a plan to travel by aeroplane.' — long and short vowel words
    Ans: Long vowel sounds: made, aeroplane. Short vowel sounds: plan, travel.

Learning the Sounds — Write two words with the given -ed sounds

  • Q: Write two words with the /d/ -ed sound.
    Ans: played, lived
  • Q: Write two words with the /id/ -ed sound.
    Ans: wanted, waited
  • Q: Write two words with the /t/ -ed sound.
    Ans: worked, helped

mcqs.q: Which words have long vowel sounds in 'My mother baked a red velvet cake.'?
mcqs.why: The solved answer circles baked and cake as the long vowel words in this sentence, while red and velvet are short.

mcqs.q: Which words have short vowel sounds in 'My mother baked a red velvet cake.'?
mcqs.why: The solved answer underlines red and velvet as the short vowel words, while baked and cake have long vowel sounds.

mcqs.q: Which words have long vowel sounds in 'She had drawn some trees and a sun in her drawing notebook.'?
mcqs.why: The solved answer gives trees and notebook as the long vowel words in this sentence, and had and sun as the short ones.

mcqs.q: Which words have short vowel sounds in 'Ali had written a note that he could not participate in the school function.'?
mcqs.why: The solved answer gives had and written as the short vowel words here, while note and school have long vowel sounds.

mcqs.q: Which words have long vowel sounds in 'He bought a new tub and water tube from the shop.'?
mcqs.why: The solved answer gives new and tube as the long vowel words in this sentence, and tub and shop as the short ones.

mcqs.q: Which words have short vowel sounds in 'They made a plan to travel by aeroplane.'?
mcqs.why: The solved answer gives plan and travel as the short vowel words, while made and aeroplane have long vowel sounds.

mcqs.q: Which pair of words has the /d/ sound for -ed?
mcqs.why: The solved answer lists played and lived as the two words with the /d/ -ed sound in this review exercise.

mcqs.q: Which pair of words has the /id/ sound for -ed?
mcqs.why: The solved answer lists wanted and waited as the two words with the /id/ -ed sound in this review exercise.

mcqs.q: Which pair of words has the /t/ sound for -ed?
mcqs.why: The solved answer lists worked and helped as the two words with the /t/ -ed sound in this review exercise.

mcqs.q: Which words have long vowel sounds in 'Ali had written a note that he could not participate in the school function.'?
mcqs.why: The solved answer gives note and school as the long vowel words in this sentence, and had and written as the short ones.

lessons.title: Language Focus
lessons.notes_html:
C) Language Focus — Make as many words as you can using the given letters (s, t, n, a, e, i, o, u, r)

  • Q: Make as many words as you can using the letters s, t, n, a, e, i, o, u, r.
    Ans: sun, run, eat, tea, ten, net, rat, sat, sea, ear, air, nut, out, our, rain, train, stone, nature, station, reason, senator, routine, tourist, nourish, tension, earnest.

Language Focus — Fill in the given paragraph with personal pronouns

  • Q: I bought ______ a stuffed penguin at the gift shop.
    Ans: myself
  • Q: Then, Hamna took a picture of ______ next to a giant octopus.
    Ans: me
  • Q: An aquarium worker, named Tariq, introduced ______ and briefed us about different kinds of fish.
    Ans: himself
  • Q: We enjoyed ______ a lot.
    Ans: ourselves

Language Focus — Read the given text carefully. Circle the adverbs and write their types above them

  • Q: In 'Umair wakes up before 6 o'clock in the morning. He always goes to school on time', identify the adverb 'always' and its type.
    Ans: always — adverb of frequency.
  • Q: In 'He daily goes to the park with his father for jogging', identify the adverb 'daily' and its type.
    Ans: daily — adverb of frequency (time).
  • Q: In 'He completes his homework quickly', identify the adverb 'quickly' and its type.
    Ans: quickly — adverb of manner.
  • Q: In 'He treats his friends kindly', identify the adverb 'kindly' and its type.
    Ans: kindly — adverb of manner.

Language Focus — Rewrite the given text by adding correct punctuation. Use capitalisation where required

  • Q: Rewrite with correct punctuation and capitalisation: 'sulemans mother came from the kitchen after listening to their conversation Yes we will buy a goat he said to his mother do you know what the other name for Bakra Eid is Mother asked'
    Ans: Suleman's mother came from the kitchen after listening to their conversation. "Yes, we will buy a goat," he said to his mother. "Do you know what the other name for Bakra Eid is?" Mother asked.

mcqs.q: Which of these words appears in the solved list of words made from the letters s, t, n, a, e, i, o, u, r?
mcqs.why: The solved word list made from these letters includes tourist, along with words like train, station, nature and routine.

mcqs.q: Which of these words also appears in the solved list made from the letters s, t, n, a, e, i, o, u, r?
mcqs.why: The solved word list ends with earnest; window, pencil and garden use letters that are not in the given set at all.

mcqs.q: Complete the sentence: 'I bought ______ a stuffed penguin at the gift shop.'
mcqs.why: The solved paragraph fills this blank with myself, because the buyer is I and the penguin was bought for the speaker himself.

mcqs.q: Complete the sentence: 'Then, Hamna took a picture of ______ next to a giant octopus.'
mcqs.why: The solved paragraph fills this blank with me, because Hamna took a picture of the speaker next to the giant octopus.

mcqs.q: Complete the sentence: 'An aquarium worker, named Tariq, introduced ______ and briefed us about different kinds of fish.'
mcqs.why: The solved paragraph fills this blank with himself, because Tariq, the aquarium worker, introduced his own self to the visitors.

mcqs.q: Complete the sentence: 'We enjoyed ______ a lot.'
mcqs.why: The solved paragraph fills this blank with ourselves, because the subject is we and the enjoyment was their own.

mcqs.q: What type of adverb is 'always' in 'He always goes to school on time'?
mcqs.why: The solved answer identifies always as an adverb of frequency, because it tells how often Umair goes to school on time.

mcqs.q: What type of adverb is 'daily' in 'He daily goes to the park with his father for jogging'?
mcqs.why: The solved answer identifies daily as an adverb of frequency, because it tells how often he goes to the park with his father.

mcqs.q: What type of adverb is 'quickly' in 'He completes his homework quickly'?
mcqs.why: The solved answer identifies quickly as an adverb of manner, because it tells how or in what manner he completes his homework.

mcqs.q: What type of adverb is 'kindly' in 'He treats his friends kindly'?
mcqs.why: The solved answer identifies kindly as an adverb of manner, because it tells how or in what manner he treats his friends.

mcqs.q: Which word is the adverb in 'He completes his homework quickly'?
mcqs.why: In the solved adverb exercise, quickly is the word circled as the adverb in this sentence from the text about Umair.

mcqs.q: According to the text about Umair, when does Umair wake up?
mcqs.why: The text given in the solved exercise begins by saying that Umair wakes up before 6 o'clock in the morning every day.

mcqs.q: Which is the correctly punctuated and capitalised opening sentence?
options: Sulemans mother came from the kitchen after listening to their conversation
Suleman's mother came from the kitchen, after listening to their conversation
Suleman's mother came from the kitchen after listening to their conversation.
Suleman's mother came from the kitchen, after listening, to their conversation
mcqs.why: The solved rewrite begins with a capital S, uses an apostrophe in Suleman's, and ends the sentence with a full stop.

mcqs.q: Which line is written correctly in the solved rewrite?
options: 'Yes we will buy a goat' he said to his mother
Yes, we will buy a goat he said to his mother.
'Yes we will buy a goat,' he said to his mother?
'Yes, we will buy a goat,' he said to his mother.
mcqs.why: The solved rewrite puts the spoken words in quotation marks with a comma before the closing mark, as direct speech needs.

mcqs.q: Which line is written correctly in the solved rewrite?
options: 'Do you know what the other name for Bakra Eid is?' Mother asked.
Do you know what the other name for Bakra Eid is Mother asked
'Do you know what the other name for Bakra Eid is.' Mother asked.
'do you know what the other name for Bakra Eid is?' mother asked
mcqs.why: The solved rewrite makes Mother's words a proper question, with a capital D, quotation marks and a question mark at the end.

lessons.title: Writing
lessons.notes_html:
D) Writing — 1. Learning to Write: Write the fable on the topic 'A Lion and the Mouse' with a moral

  • Q: Write the fable 'A Lion and the Mouse' with a moral.
    Ans: Once a lion was sleeping in a jungle. A little mouse ran over his body and woke him up. The lion caught the mouse and was about to kill it. The mouse begged, 'Please let me go. One day I will surely help you.' The lion laughed but let it go. After some days, the lion was caught in a hunter's net. He roared loudly. The mouse heard him, came quickly and gnawed the ropes with its sharp teeth. Soon the lion was free. He thanked the little mouse. Moral: Kindness is never wasted. Even a small and weak creature can help a great one.

mcqs.q: In the fable 'A Lion and the Mouse', where was the lion sleeping?
mcqs.why: The solved fable begins by saying that once a lion was sleeping in a jungle when the little mouse ran over his body.

mcqs.q: What woke the lion up in the fable?
options: A little mouse ran over his body
mcqs.why: The solved fable says a little mouse ran over the sleeping lion's body, and that is what woke the lion up.

mcqs.q: What was the lion about to do when he caught the mouse?
options: He was about to feed it
He was about to run away
He was about to kill it
He was about to climb a tree
mcqs.why: The solved fable says the lion caught the mouse and was about to kill it, but the mouse begged him to let it go.

mcqs.q: What did the mouse beg the lion to do?
options: Give it some food to eat
Let it live inside the jungle
Take it back to its home
Let it go, promising to help the lion one day
mcqs.why: The solved fable gives the mouse's own words: please let me go, and one day I will surely help you in return.

mcqs.q: How did the lion react before he let the mouse go?
options: He laughed but let it go
He roared and chased it away
He called the hunter at once
He went back to sleep angrily
mcqs.why: The solved fable says the lion laughed at the mouse's promise but still let the little mouse go free.

mcqs.q: What happened to the lion after some days?
options: He fell sick in the jungle
He was caught in a hunter's net
He left the jungle for good
He was chased by other lions
mcqs.why: The solved fable says that after some days the lion was caught in a hunter's net and could not free himself.

mcqs.q: What did the trapped lion do in the net?
options: He dug a hole under the net
mcqs.why: The solved fable says the trapped lion roared loudly, and the little mouse heard his roar and came quickly to help.

mcqs.q: How did the mouse free the lion in the fable?
options: It pulled the net with its tail
It brought a knife from the village
It called the hunter to open the net
It gnawed the ropes with its sharp teeth
mcqs.why: The solved fable says the mouse gnawed the ropes of the net with its sharp teeth, and soon the lion was free.

mcqs.q: What did the lion do when he was free?
options: He gave the mouse a gift
He left the jungle at once
He went to catch the hunter
mcqs.why: The solved fable ends this part by saying that the freed lion thanked the little mouse for saving his life.

mcqs.q: What is the moral of the fable 'A Lion and the Mouse'?
options: Might is always right in the jungle
Kindness is never wasted; even a small and weak creature can help a great one
We should never help anyone at all
The strong never need any help
mcqs.why: The solved fable gives this moral: kindness is never wasted, and even a small and weak creature can help a great one.

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Getting Started — Let's Talk

  • Q: Have you ever tried to make someone happy? How?
    Ans: Yes. I once shared my lunch with a classmate who had forgotten his. He became happy and thanked me. Making others happy also makes us happy.
  • Q: How do you spend your savings?
    Ans: I spend my savings carefully. I buy only the things I really need, like books and stationery, and I keep the rest saved for a useful purpose.
  • Q: Why should we help a needy person?
    Ans: We should help a needy person because helping others brings happiness to them and to us. It shows that we care for others, and we should take care of each other.

Pre-reading

  • Q: Do you share your things with others?
    Ans: Yes, I share my things, such as my books, pencils and lunch, with my friends. Sharing brings happiness and shows that we care for others.
  • Q: Do you help your friends?
    Ans: Yes, I help my friends in their studies and in times of need, just as Abdullah, Tahir and Maheen helped their friend Sara in the lesson.

While-reading

  • Q: Why was Sara sad?
    Ans: Sara was sad because her father had lost his job last month and could not buy her a new dress for the fun fair.

Post-reading

  • Q: Share some ways by which we can help our friends.
    Ans: We can help our friends by sharing our things with them, helping them in their studies, saving our pocket money to buy something they need, and standing by them when they are sad or in trouble.
  • Q: How do you spend your pocket money?
    Ans: I spend my pocket money carefully. I do not waste it on extra things. I save a part of it in my money box and spend the rest only on things I need.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension (i) Answer these questions

  • Q: Why was Sara not happy?
    Ans: Sara was not happy because her father had lost his job last month and could not buy her a new dress.
  • Q: What is a fun fair?
    Ans: A fun fair is a fair held for enjoyment, with rides, games and stalls. In the lesson, Sara's school was going to arrange a fun fair the next month.
  • Q: Why should we always help others?
    Ans: We should always help others because sharing brings happiness to us and to them. It shows how much we care for our friends and loved ones, and we should take care of each other.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension (ii) Main idea of the paragraph

  • Q: Read the paragraph about money and write its main idea.
    Ans: The main idea is that money is an essential need for life, so people work hard to earn it. To earn and save money, we must set a specific goal, make smart spending decisions, and not waste money on extravagant things.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension (iii) Summarise the paragraph in 2-3 sentences

  • Q: Summarise the paragraph about money in 2-3 sentences.
    Ans: Money is an essential need, and people work hard to earn it so that they can fulfil their dreams. To earn and save money, we need to set a specific goal for ourselves. We should make smart spending decisions and not waste money buying extravagant things.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension (iv) Fill in the blanks correctly

  • Q: Their school was arranging a ______.
    Ans: fun fair
  • Q: Sara's father could not buy her a new ______.
    Ans: dress
  • Q: Note: 'They went with Maheen's ______ to the market.'
    Ans: This printed blank cannot be completed from the lesson text. In the lesson the children do not go to the market with Maheen; they save their pocket money for a whole month, buy Sara a new dress, pack it in colourful wrapping paper and take it to Sara's house. No word from the text fits this blank, so it has not been guessed.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 2. Analytical Reading

  • Q: Write the advantages and disadvantages of using the internet.

lessons.title: Sounds and Speaking
lessons.notes_html:
A) Oral Communication — 1. Learning the Sounds: Use of Dictionary (i)

  • Q: What is a dictionary?
    Ans: A dictionary is a reference book which lists the words of a language in alphabetical order and gives their meanings. It also provides the pronunciation and the number of syllables of words.
  • Q: In the dictionary entry for 'company', what is its part of speech and how many syllables does it have?
    Ans: 'Company' is a noun. It has 3 syllables: com-pa-ny. The entry also gives its meaning: a business organization that makes money by providing or selling goods or services.

A) Oral Communication — 1. Learning the Sounds: Use of Dictionary (ii) Find the words in a dictionary

  • Q: Write the meaning and number of syllables of 'investment', and use it in a sentence.
    Ans: Investment means money put into something to make a profit, or the act of putting money in. It has 3 syllables: in-vest-ment. Sentence: His father made an investment in a small shop.
  • Q: Write the meaning and number of syllables of 'measure', and use it in a sentence.
    Ans: Measure means to find the size, length or amount of something. It has 2 syllables: meas-ure. Sentence: We measure the cloth before buying it.
  • Q: Write the meaning and number of syllables of 'recommend', and use it in a sentence.
    Ans: Recommend means to suggest something as being good or suitable. It has 3 syllables: rec-om-mend. Sentence: I recommend this book to my friends.
  • Q: Write the meaning and number of syllables of 'provide', and use it in a sentence.
    Ans: Provide means to give or supply something that is needed. It has 2 syllables: pro-vide. Sentence: Our school provides us with books.

A) Oral Communication — 2. Learning to Speak (i) Dialogue: Adam and his father

  • Q: What rules does Adam's father give him to save money?
    Ans: Adam's father tells him to set a goal that he will not spend money on extra things and will only buy the things he needs. Adam promises to follow these instructions and save money.

A) Oral Communication — 2. Learning to Speak (ii) Complete the dialogue

  • Q: Complete the dialogue between Adam and Saad about the way to the library.
    Ans: Adam: Can you tell me the way to the library? Saad: I am also going there; just follow me. Adam: Thank you, Saad. That is very kind of you. Saad: You are welcome. The library is near our school. Adam: Good, let us go together.

mcqs.q: What is a dictionary?
options: A reference book that lists the words of a language in alphabetical order and gives their meanings
A story book full of pictures
A book used for writing essays
mcqs.why: The solved answer defines a dictionary as a reference book listing words in alphabetical order with their meanings.

mcqs.q: What else does a dictionary provide, besides meanings?
options: The pronunciation and the number of syllables of words
mcqs.why: The solved answer says a dictionary also provides the pronunciation of words and the number of their syllables.

mcqs.q: What is the part of speech of 'company' in the dictionary entry?
mcqs.why: The solved dictionary entry for company clearly labels the word company as a noun with three syllables.

mcqs.q: How many syllables does the word 'company' have?
mcqs.why: The solved dictionary entry divides company into three syllables, com-pa-ny, and marks the number of syllables as three.

mcqs.q: What does 'company' mean in the dictionary entry?
options: A business organization that makes money by providing or selling goods or services
A group of friends sitting in a park
A box used for saving money
mcqs.why: The solved entry gives this meaning of company: a business organization that makes money by providing or selling goods or services.

mcqs.q: What does 'investment' mean?
options: Finding the size or length of something
Money put into something to make a profit
mcqs.why: The solved dictionary answer says investment means money put into something to make a profit, or the act of putting money in.

mcqs.q: How many syllables does the word 'measure' have?
mcqs.why: The solved dictionary answer divides measure into two syllables, meas-ure, so the word has two syllables in total.

mcqs.q: What does 'recommend' mean?
options: To find the size of something
To give something that is needed
Money put in to make a profit
To suggest something as being good or suitable
mcqs.why: The solved dictionary answer says recommend means to suggest something as being good or suitable for someone.

mcqs.q: What does 'provide' mean?
options: To give or supply something that is needed
To find the length of something
Money put in to make a profit
mcqs.why: The solved dictionary answer says provide means to give or supply something that is needed by someone.

mcqs.q: What rule does Adam's father give him for saving money?
options: Spend all your money as soon as you get it
Set a goal: do not spend money on extra things, and buy only the things you need
Buy everything that you like to see
Never save any money for the future
mcqs.why: The solved dialogue answer says Adam's father tells him to set a goal, avoid extra things and buy only what he needs.

lessons.title: Language Focus
lessons.notes_html:
C) Language Focus — 1. Vocabulary Building (i) Words with their meanings

  • Q: What does 'participation' mean? Use it in a sentence.
    Ans: Participation means taking part in an activity or event. Sentence: Sara's participation in the fun fair made her friends happy.
  • Q: What does 'speechless' mean? Use it in a sentence.
    Ans: Speechless means not able to speak out of emotions. Sentence: They were speechless as Sara walked away sadly.
  • Q: What does 'collect' mean? Use it in a sentence.
    Ans: Collect means to bring things together. Sentence: After a month, they collected their money to buy a new dress for Sara.
  • Q: What does 'gratitude' mean? Use it in a sentence.
    Ans: Gratitude means being grateful. Sentence: When Sara opened the gift, her eyes filled with delight and gratitude.
  • Q: What does 'care' mean? Use it in a sentence.
    Ans: Care means to look after. Sentence: We should take care of each other.

C) Language Focus — 1. Vocabulary Building (ii) Parts of speech from the lesson

  • Q: Read the lesson again and write examples of each part of speech from it.
    Ans: Nouns: school, park, dress. Verbs: gather, save, buy. Pronouns: I, we, she. Adjectives: new, beautiful, colourful. Prepositions: in, to, for. Adverbs: sadly, away, then.

C) Language Focus — 2. Learning to Spell

  • Q: Fill in the missing letters to complete the word: st__ck
    Ans: stick
  • Q: Fill in the missing letters to complete the word: in__ormatio__
    Ans: information
  • Q: Fill in the missing letters to complete the word: st__al
    Ans: steal
  • Q: Fill in the missing letters to complete the word: ex__pert
    Ans: expert
  • Q: Fill in the missing letters to complete the word: amoun__
    Ans: amount
  • Q: Note: spelling patterns in this exercise
    Ans: The pattern 'st__ck' can be completed with different vowels (stick, stock, stuck); 'stick' is given here as the most common school word. The pattern 'ex__pert' also has one extra letter space; the intended word is 'expert'.

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar: Question Words (i) Use of question words

  • Q: What is the question word 'Why' used for?
    Ans: 'Why' is used to ask for a reason, e.g. 'Why do you save your money?'
  • Q: What is the question word 'When' used for?
    Ans: 'When' is used to ask about time and date, e.g. 'When did you buy a new car?'
  • Q: What is the question word 'How often' used for?
    Ans: 'How often' is used to ask about the frequency of something, e.g. 'How often do you play cricket?'
  • Q: What is the question word 'How much' used for?
    Ans: 'How much' is used to ask about the quantity or price of something, e.g. 'How much money do you have?'
  • Q: What is the question word 'How many' used for?
    Ans: 'How many' is used to ask about numbers, e.g. 'How many siblings do you have?'

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar: Question Words (ii) Choose the correct word for each question

  • Q: ______ do you visit your grandparents? (What, How often)
    Ans: How often
  • Q: ______ do we need money? (Why, Where)
    Ans: Why
  • Q: ______ do you go to school? (Who, When)
    Ans: When
  • Q: ______ students are there in your classroom? (How many, What)
    Ans: How many
  • Q: ______ does this dress cost? (Who, How much)
    Ans: How much

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar: Prepositions of Movement and Direction (iii)

  • Q: Which word is the preposition of movement and direction in this sentence: 'Oh no! That policeman is coming towards us.'?
    Ans: towards
  • Q: Which word is the preposition of movement and direction in this sentence: 'A thief dived into the river.'?
    Ans: into
  • Q: Which word is the preposition of movement and direction in this sentence: 'They drove across the city.'?
    Ans: across
  • Q: Which word is the preposition of movement and direction in this sentence: 'The cat jumped over the wall.'?
    Ans: over

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar: Prepositions of Movement and Direction (iv) Make sentences

  • Q: Make a sentence using 'across'.
    Ans: We walked across the park to reach the school.
  • Q: Make a sentence using 'towards'.
    Ans: The children ran towards their friend Sara.
  • Q: Make a sentence using 'onto'.
    Ans: The cat jumped onto the table.
  • Q: Make a sentence using 'into'.
    Ans: He poured the water into the glass.

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar: Simple Present Tense (v) Sentence structures

  • Q: What are the sentence structures of the simple present tense?
    Ans: Affirmative: subject + base/-es form of verb + object. Negative: subject + do/does not + base form of verb + object. Interrogative: do/does + subject + base form of verb + object? The simple present tense is used to express regular or habitual actions and facts that do not change with time, e.g. 'The Sun sets in the west.'

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar: Simple Present Tense (vi) Change into negative and interrogative sentences

  • Q: Change into negative and interrogative: 'My mother washes clothes.'
    Ans: Negative: My mother does not wash clothes. Interrogative: Does my mother wash clothes?
  • Q: Change into negative and interrogative: 'The birds fly in the air.'
    Ans: Negative: The birds do not fly in the air. Interrogative: Do the birds fly in the air?
  • Q: Change into negative and interrogative: 'He likes swimming.'
    Ans: Negative: He does not like swimming. Interrogative: Does he like swimming?
  • Q: Change into negative and interrogative: 'Saad watches TV every day.'
    Ans: Negative: Saad does not watch TV every day. Interrogative: Does Saad watch TV every day?

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar: Hyphen (vii) Hyphenated words

  • Q: Read the given hyphenated words. What is a hyphen used for?
    Ans: Fractions: one-fourth, three-sixths. Numbers: forty-five, eighty-two. A hyphen (-) is used to join two or more words together. It is usually used with numbers and fractions.

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar: Hyphen (viii) Write five words using hyphens

  • Q: Write five words using hyphens with numbers and fractions.
    Ans: Twenty-one, thirty-six, ninety-nine, one-half, two-thirds.

options: To end every sentence we write

lessons.title: Writing
lessons.notes_html:
D) Writing — 1. Learning to Write (i) Qualities of a Good Person

  • Q: Look at the mind map and write about some 'Qualities of a Good Person'.
    Ans: A good person speaks the truth. He helps others and shares his things with the needy. He is kind and polite to everyone and respects his elders. He takes care of his friends and loved ones and never hurts anyone.

D) Writing — 1. Learning to Write (ii) Dialogue about 'Qualities of a Good Person'

  • Q: Write a dialogue about 'Qualities of a Good Person' in your own words.
    Ans: Ali: What makes a person good? Bilal: A good person always speaks the truth. Ali: What else should he do? Bilal: He should help others, share his things with them and take care of his friends. Ali: You are right. We should all try to be good persons.

D) Writing — 2. Creative Writing

  • Q: Write some ways to save your money and how you can use it.
    Ans: I save my pocket money in my money box and do not spend it on extra things. I buy only the things I need. In this way, I can collect enough money to buy useful things, like books, or to help a friend in need, as Abdullah and his friends helped Sara.

He is kind and polite to everyone
He helps only himself every time
He never shares anything with anyone

mcqs.why: The solved creative writing answer says the writer saves pocket money in a money box and does not spend it on extra things.

Only the things he really needs

To waste it on extra things

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Getting Started — Use the highlighted words in sentences

  • Q: Use 'devotion' in a sentence to show the meaning of patriotism or national pride.
    Ans: Our devotion to our homeland shows our love for our country.
  • Q: Use 'sentiment' in a sentence to show the meaning of patriotism or national pride.
    Ans: Every citizen shares the sentiment of love for the homeland.
  • Q: Use 'Patriotism' in a sentence to show its meaning.
    Ans: Patriotism is love and support for one's country; waving the flag proudly in our home is an example of patriotism.

Let's Talk — Tell the meaning in your own words

  • Q: Tell the meaning of 'Patriotism' in your own words.
    Ans: Patriotism is the feeling of love, devotion and a sense of attachment to one's homeland. It is love and support for one's own country.
  • Q: Tell the meaning of 'Devotion' in your own words.
    Ans: Devotion means great love and loyalty for someone or something, such as love for our country.
  • Q: Tell the meaning of 'Sentiment' in your own words.
    Ans: A sentiment is a feeling or emotion, such as the feeling of love for the homeland shared by other citizens.

Pre-reading

  • Q: Read the title and guess what the lesson is about.
    Ans: The lesson is about the Markhor, the national animal of Pakistan.
  • Q: What is the name of the animal shown in the picture?
    Ans: The animal shown in the picture is the Markhor, the national animal of Pakistan.

While-reading

  • Q: How many types of markhor are there in Asia?
    Ans: There are three species of Markhor found in Asia.

Post-reading

  • Q: Write any three interesting things about Markhor.
    Ans: 1. The Markhor is considered a symbol of bravery and intelligence, and it can jump downwards from mountain peaks with ease. 2. It kills snakes, and so it is called Markhor. 3. The male's long and curly horns are nearly 63 inches long, while the female's horns are around 10 inches long.
  • Q: Have you ever seen a markhor? Share your experience in a few sentences.
    Ans: I have not seen a Markhor in the mountains, but I have seen its picture in my book. It is a beautiful wild animal with long and curly horns. I wish to see a real Markhor one day in the northern areas of Pakistan.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension (i) Answer these questions

  • Q: What does Markhor eat?
    Ans: The Markhor eats grass in spring and summer, but in winter it feeds on leaves, herbs, fruits and flowers.
  • Q: How long are the horns of male and female Markhor?
    Ans: The attractive horns of the male Markhor are nearly 63 inches long, and the horns of the female are around 10 inches long.
  • Q: How long can a Markhor live?
    Ans: The Markhor has a lifespan of 12 to 13 years.
  • Q: List some reasons why Markhors are endangered.
    Ans: The Markhor is an endangered species because it is killed by hunters, particularly for its meat and horns. Its horns are used in traditional medicines and as trophies.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension (ii) Look at the calendar and answer the questions

  • Q: How many months have 30 days?
    Ans: Four months have 30 days: April, June, September and November.
  • Q: First of November falls on which day?
    Ans: In the given calendar, the 1st of November falls on Thursday.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension (iii) Read the pie chart: Endangered Species

  • Q: What numbers of endangered species are given in the pie chart?
    Ans: The pie chart 'Endangered Species' gives these numbers: Flowers 760, Fish 145, Clams and snails 109, Birds 92, Mammals 84, Reptiles 36, and Amphibians 25, besides Plants, Animals, Other plants and Other animals.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension (iv) Look at the pie chart again and answer the questions

  • Q: Which is the most endangered animal species?
    Ans: Fish is the most endangered animal species in the chart, with 145.
  • Q: What is the number of endangered flowers given in the chart?
    Ans: The number of endangered flowers given in the chart is 760.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension (v) Fill in the blanks with the correct options

  • Q: Markhor is the national animal of ______.
    Options: Iran / Afghanistan / Pakistan / Bangladesh
    Ans: Pakistan
  • Q: There are ______ species of markhor found in Asia.
    Options: two / three / four / five
    Ans: three
  • Q: Male markhor has nearly ______ inches long horns.
    Options: 60 / 61 / 62 / 63
    Ans: 63
  • Q: Like other goats, markhors are ______ animals.
    Options: omnivorous / herbivorous / carnivorous / hunter
    Ans: herbivorous

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 2. Analytical Reading

  • Q: What is the national animal of India?
    Ans: The national animal of India is the Bengal tiger.
  • Q: What is the national animal of China?
    Ans: The national animal of China is the giant panda.
  • Q: What is the national animal of the United States of America?
    Ans: The national animal of the United States of America is the bald eagle.
  • Q: What is the national animal of Australia?
    Ans: The national animal of Australia is the kangaroo.
  • Q: What is the national animal of Canada?
    Ans: The national animal of Canada is the beaver.

lessons.title: Sounds and Speaking
lessons.notes_html:
A) Oral Communication — 1. Learning the Sounds: Weak forms of 'will not' and 'shall not'

  • Q: What is the weak (short) form of 'will not'? Give an example from the book.
    Ans: The weak form of 'will not' is 'won't'. Example: 'It will not rain today' becomes 'It won't rain today.'
  • Q: What is the weak (short) form of 'shall not'? Give an example from the book.
    Ans: The weak form of 'shall not' is 'shan't'. Example: 'We shall not visit Peshawar next month' becomes 'We shan't visit Peshawar next month.'
  • Q: Make two sentences of your own using the weak forms of 'will not' and 'shall not'.
    Ans: I won't waste my pocket money. We shan't be late for school.

A) Oral Communication — 2. Learning to Speak (i) Dialogue: Haris and Mohsin

  • Q: Why does Mohsin need books on history?
    Ans: Mohsin needs books on history because he has to submit a project on famous personalities in history. Haris offers to help him and says he can borrow his books on this topic.
  • Q: Where is Haris going, and why?
    Ans: Haris is going to get medicine for his grandmother because she is not feeling well.

A) Oral Communication — 2. Learning to Speak (ii) Share an unforgettable moment

  • Q: Share any unforgettable moment of your life using expressions of joy, sadness or anger.
    Ans: I can never forget the day I won a prize at school. I was very happy, and my parents were also very glad. It was a moment of great joy for me.

mcqs.q: What is the weak (short) form of 'will not'?
mcqs.why: The solved sounds answer and the book's Read Me box both state that the weak form of will not is won't.

mcqs.q: What is the weak (short) form of 'shall not'?
mcqs.why: The solved sounds answer and the book's Read Me box both state that the weak form of shall not is shan't.

mcqs.q: 'It will not rain today' becomes which sentence in the weak form?
mcqs.why: The solved sounds answer gives this book example: It will not rain today becomes It won't rain today, using won't.

options: We won't visit Peshawar next month
We shalln't visit Peshawar next month

We shan't visit Peshawar next month
mcqs.why: The solved sounds answer gives this book example with shan't, the weak form of shall not, for the Peshawar sentence.

options: I won't waste my pocket money
I shan't waste my pocket money
I will waste my pocket money
I won't wasted my pocket money
mcqs.why: The solved answer's own sentence with the weak form of will not is: I won't waste my pocket money, using won't correctly.

options: We won't be late for school
We shan't be late for school
We shan't been late for school
We shall be late for school
mcqs.why: The solved answer's own sentence with the weak form of shall not is: We shan't be late for school, using shan't correctly.

options: He has to write an essay on the Markhor
He has lost all his history books

options: A new history book as a gift
Mohsin can borrow Haris's books on this topic
mcqs.why: The solved dialogue answer says Haris offers to help Mohsin and tells him he can borrow his books on this topic.

options: To get medicine for his grandmother
To a bookshop to buy history books
To school to submit a project
To Peshawar for a short visit

lessons.title: Language Focus
lessons.notes_html:
C) Language Focus — 1. Vocabulary Building (i) Words with their meanings

  • Q: What does 'elongate' mean? Use it in a sentence.
    Ans: Elongate means lengthy, or to become longer. Sentence: The Markhor's coats elongate in winter.
  • Q: What does 'predator' mean? Use it in a sentence.
    Ans: A predator is an animal that hunts. Sentence: The Markhor grazes on the peaks of mountains, so it is out of the range of predators.
  • Q: What does 'escape' mean? Use it in a sentence.
    Ans: Escape means to run away. Sentence: If the Markhor senses danger, it uses its excellent climbing skills to escape.
  • Q: What does 'endangered' mean? Use it in a sentence.
    Ans: Endangered means at risk or in danger. Sentence: The Markhor is an endangered species.

C) Language Focus — 2. Learning to Spell

  • Q: Fill in the missing letters to complete the word: __eak
    Ans: peak
  • Q: Fill in the missing letters to complete the word: __ravery
    Ans: bravery
  • Q: Fill in the missing letters to complete the word: endan__egred
    Ans: endangered
  • Q: Fill in the missing letters to complete the word: h__nt
    Ans: hunt
  • Q: Fill in the missing letters to complete the word: at__ractiv__
    Ans: attractive
  • Q: Fill in the missing letters to complete the word: troph__es
    Ans: trophies
  • Q: Note: spelling pattern 'endan__egred'
    Ans: The printed pattern has an extra letter space and transposed letters; the intended word, used in the lesson, is 'endangered'.

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar: Joining Words (i)

  • Q: Which joining word is used in this sentence: 'Markhor's lower legs are black and white.'?
    Ans: and
  • Q: Which joining word is used in this sentence: 'Markhor is a strong but peaceful animal.'?
    Ans: but
  • Q: Which joining word is used in this sentence: 'Did he come by bus or train?'?
    Ans: or
  • Q: Which joining word is used in this sentence: 'The bus was late because there was a crowd at the bus station.'?
    Ans: because
  • Q: Which joining word is used in this sentence: 'They have gone to the station so they can catch the train on time.'?
    Ans: so

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar: Joining Words (ii) Join the sentences using the correct joining words

  • Q: He worked hard ______ he could not stand first. (but, because)
    Ans: but
  • Q: She could not submit her plan ______ she was very ill. (so, because)
    Ans: because
  • Q: Mohsin has bought a new shirt ______ he will come to the party. (because, so)
    Ans: so
  • Q: She is studying history ______ culture for her assignment. (because, and)
    Ans: and

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar: Statements and Questions (iii)

  • Q: Is this a statement or a question: 'Markhor is the national animal of Pakistan.'?
    Ans: It is a statement. It gives information.
  • Q: Is this a statement or a question: 'He will not clean the house.'?
    Ans: It is a statement. It negates something.
  • Q: Is this a statement or a question: 'Has she written about the national bird of Pakistan?'?
    Ans: It is a question. It asks something.
  • Q: Is this a statement or a question: 'Will they join us?'?
    Ans: It is a question. It asks something.

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar: Statements and Questions (iv) Write 'S' for a statement and 'Q' for a question

  • Q: Write 'S' or 'Q': 'Markhor lives in mountains.'
    Ans: S (statement)
  • Q: Write 'S' or 'Q': 'How long can Markhors live?'
    Ans: Q (question)
  • Q: Write 'S' or 'Q': 'What do Markhors eat?'
    Ans: Q (question)
  • Q: Write 'S' or 'Q': 'Markhor is an endangered species.'
    Ans: S (statement)
  • Q: Write 'S' or 'Q': 'Markhors are killed by hunters for their meat and horns.'
    Ans: S (statement)

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar: Statements and Questions (v) Write five statements and questions each

  • Q: Write five statements.
    Ans: 1. Markhor is the national animal of Pakistan. 2. It lives in the mountains. 3. It eats grass in spring and summer. 4. It has long and curly horns. 5. It is an endangered species.
  • Q: Write five questions.
    Ans: 1. What is the national animal of Pakistan? 2. Where does the Markhor live? 3. What does the Markhor eat? 4. How long can a Markhor live? 5. Why is the Markhor endangered?

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar: Wh Question Words (vi)

  • Q: Which words are the question words in the given sentences?
    Ans: What, Where, Who and Which are question words. They are used to ask questions, e.g. 'What is the time by your watch?', 'Where is the National Park in Nathiagali?', 'Who is outside?' and 'Which is the most endangered animal of Pakistan?'

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar: Wh Question Words (vii) Write questions for the answers

  • Q: Write a question for this answer: 'Your books are on the table.'
    Ans: Where are your books?
  • Q: Write a question for this answer: 'This is my trophy.'
    Ans: What is this?
  • Q: Write a question for this answer: 'Liaqat Ali Khan was the first Prime Minister of Pakistan.'
    Ans: Who was the first Prime Minister of Pakistan?
  • Q: Write a question for this answer: 'I like cats.'
    Ans: What do you like?

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar: Wh Question Words (viii) Make questions

  • Q: Make questions by using the question words What, Where, Who and Which.
    Ans: What is your name? Where is your school? Who is your best friend? Which is the national animal of Pakistan?

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar: Present Continuous Tense (ix) Read the sentences

  • Q: Notice the use of the present continuous tense in the given sentences. Which one is affirmative, which is negative and which is interrogative?
    Ans: 'I am going to visit Naran tomorrow' is affirmative. 'I am not going to visit Naran tomorrow' is negative. 'Am I going to visit Naran tomorrow?' is interrogative. The present continuous tense is used to express an ongoing action in present time.

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar: Present Continuous Tense (x) Complete the sentences with the correct verb forms

  • Q: She is ______ cakes for the guests. (make, making)
    Ans: making
  • Q: They are not ______ their grandparents. (visiting, visited)
    Ans: visiting
  • Q: Am I ______ with you? (gone, going)
    Ans: going

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar: Present Continuous Tense (xi) Write six sentences

  • Q: Write six sentences using the present continuous tense.
    Ans: 1. I am reading my English book. 2. She is writing a letter. 3. They are playing in the park. 4. We are going to school. 5. He is eating his lunch. 6. The Markhor is climbing the mountain.

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar: Capitalisation (xii) Rewrite the paragraph with correct capitalisation and punctuation

  • Q: Rewrite the given paragraph with correct capitalisation and punctuation.
    Ans: Yesterday, Ali and Sana watched a documentary about the national animal of Pakistan. They enjoyed this documentary. They asked their mother to tell them more about the national animal of Pakistan. She told them, "The Markhor is a type of goat." It lives mostly in the northern areas of Pakistan. It is a strong and peaceful animal. "When will we go to Khyber Pakhtunkhwa to see Markhors?" asked Sana.

options: 'The Markhor is a type of deer.'
'The Markhor is a type of goat.'

lessons.title: Writing
lessons.notes_html:
D) Writing — 1. Learning to Write: Paragraph on the 'National Bird of Pakistan'

  • Q: Write a paragraph on the 'National Bird of Pakistan', keeping in mind: What is its most prominent feature? In which area is it found? Why is it endangered?
    Ans: The Chukar, also called Chakor, is the national bird of Pakistan. Its most prominent features are its plump body with grey-brown feathers, black and white bars on its sides, a black band running through its eyes, and its red beak and legs. It is found in the dry, rocky hills and mountain areas of Pakistan, including Balochistan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Punjab and Sindh. It is endangered because it is hunted for food and sport, and because its natural home is being destroyed.

D) Writing — 2. Creative Writing: Paragraph on 'Endangered Animals'

  • Q: Write a paragraph on 'Endangered Animals' and write a few steps you can take to save them from being extinct.
    Ans: Endangered animals are those animals which are at risk of dying out, like the Markhor of Pakistan. They are killed by hunters for their meat, horns and skin, and their homes are destroyed. We can save them by not hunting them, by protecting the forests and mountains where they live, and by telling others not to buy things made from their horns or skin. In this way, these beautiful animals will stay alive for the future.

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Reading — While-reading and Post-reading Questions

  • Q: While-reading: What kind of books did Hafsa's mother order?
    Ans: She ordered storybooks for Hafsa. Hafsa was anxiously waiting for them, because she wanted to read a new adventure story each day.
  • Q: Post-reading: Whom did Hafsa's mother write the letter to and why?
    Ans: She wrote the letter to Zain Book Company, Abbottabad, the seller. She complained that the company had mistakenly sent them a wrong parcel, returned the parcel, and requested the company to send the storybooks that she had ordered, as soon as possible.
  • Q: Post-reading: Why was Hafsa bored?
    Ans: The summer holidays had started and Hafsa was getting bored at home. She was anxiously waiting for the storybooks her mother had ordered for her, so that she could read a new adventure story each day.
  • Q: Name the labelled parts of the formal letter written by Hafsa's mother.
    Ans: The parts of the formal letter are: the writer's address, the receiver's address, the date, the subject, the salutation, the body of the letter, and the signature at the end.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension: i. Answer these questions

  • Q: What was wrong with the parcel?
    Ans: The book company had sent a wrong parcel. When Hafsa opened it, the books inside were not the storybooks that her mother had ordered for her, so she felt disappointed.
  • Q: What type of stories does Hafsa like to read?
    Ans: Hafsa likes to read adventure stories. She thought it would be real fun to read a new adventure story each day.
  • Q: Which storybooks do you like? Why?
    Ans: I like adventure storybooks, such as the stories of Sindbad the Sailor and the Arabian Nights shown in the lesson. I like them because they are full of exciting journeys and surprises, and I learn about new and strange places.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension: ii. Fill in the blanks with the correct options

  • Q: Hafsa was anxiously waiting for her ______.
    Options: food / storybooks / dress / flowers
    Ans: storybooks
  • Q: 'Doorbell' is an example of a/an ______ noun.
    Options: compound / abstract / proper / collective
    Ans: compound
  • Q: Hafsa's mother wrote a/an ______ letter to the company.
    Options: invitation / complaint / greetings / thank you
    Ans: complaint
  • Q: Her ______ ordered storybooks for Hafsa.
    Options: father / mother / friend / cousin
    Ans: mother

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 2. Analytical Reading: Read a formal and an informal letter and note their features and differences

  • Q: Read a formal and an informal letter. Note their important features and differences in your notebook.
    Ans: A formal letter has the writer's address, the receiver's address, the date, a subject, a formal salutation such as 'Respected Sir', a body, a closing such as 'Yours truly', and the signature. Its language is polite and official. An informal letter is written to friends and family; it has no subject, begins with a friendly salutation such as 'Dear Ahmed', and its language is personal and relaxed.

lessons.title: Sounds and Speaking
lessons.notes_html:
A) Oral Communication — 1. Learning the Sounds: i. Read the given sentences and notice the use of intonation

  • Q: Which intonation is used in: 'This scene is beautiful, isn't it?'
    Ans: Rising intonation. Our voice rises at the end of the statement.
  • Q: Which intonation is used in: 'Do you sell clothes?'
    Ans: Rising intonation. Rising intonation is used in yes-no questions.
  • Q: Which intonation is used in: 'Are you hungry?'
    Ans: Rising intonation. It is a yes-no question, so our voice rises at the end.
  • Q: Which intonation is used in: 'Where's the nearest bank?'
    Ans: Falling intonation. In falling intonation our voice falls on the final stressed syllable; it is used in wh- questions.
  • Q: Which intonation is used in: 'What is your name?'
    Ans: Falling intonation, because it is a wh- question.
  • Q: Which intonation is used in: 'Do not run on roads.'
    Ans: Falling intonation, because it is a command.
  • Q: Which intonation is used in: 'That's great!'
    Ans: Falling intonation, because it is an exclamation.

A) Oral Communication — 2. Learning to Speak: ii. Read and practise the given dialogue with proper intonation

  • Q: Read and practise the dialogue between Hafsa and Miss Sara. Why does Hafsa want to go home early?
    Ans: Hafsa politely asks, 'Teacher, could I go home early today?' Her grandfather is in hospital, and she wants to go and give him a bouquet. Miss Sara allows her to go after break time, but reminds her not to forget her leave application. Hafsa thanks her teacher.
  • Q: Practise a dialogue about how to take leave for a different reason, using polite words.
    Ans: Student: 'Teacher, could I please take leave tomorrow? I have to go to the doctor with my mother.' Teacher: 'Yes, you may go. Please bring your leave application with you.' Student: 'Thank you very much, teacher.'

mcqs.q: Which intonation is used in: 'This scene is beautiful, isn't it?'
mcqs.why: The solved exercise says rising intonation is used here because our voice rises at the end of the statement with a tag question.

mcqs.q: Which intonation is used in the yes-no question: 'Do you sell clothes?'
mcqs.why: The solved exercise explains that rising intonation is used in yes-no questions, and 'Do you sell clothes?' is a yes-no question.

mcqs.q: Which intonation is used in: 'Are you hungry?'
mcqs.why: It is a yes-no question, so our voice rises at the end. The solved exercise marks 'Are you hungry?' as rising intonation.

mcqs.q: Which intonation is used in the wh- question: 'Where's the nearest bank?'
mcqs.why: The solved exercise says falling intonation is used in wh- questions, and our voice falls on the final stressed syllable.

mcqs.q: Which intonation is used in: 'What is your name?'
mcqs.why: The solved exercise marks 'What is your name?' as falling intonation because it is a wh- question, not a yes-no question.

mcqs.q: Which intonation is used in the command: 'Do not run on roads.'
mcqs.why: The solved exercise says falling intonation is used here because 'Do not run on roads.' is a command, and commands take falling intonation.

mcqs.q: Which intonation is used in the exclamation: 'That's great!'
mcqs.why: The solved exercise marks 'That's great!' as falling intonation because it is an exclamation expressing a strong feeling.

mcqs.q: Why does Hafsa want to go home early in the dialogue with Miss Sara?
mcqs.why: In the dialogue Hafsa politely asks to go home early because her grandfather is in hospital and she wants to visit him.

mcqs.q: What does Hafsa want to give her grandfather in hospital?
mcqs.why: The solved dialogue answer says Hafsa wants to go and give her grandfather a bouquet during her visit to the hospital.

mcqs.q: What does Miss Sara remind Hafsa not to forget?
mcqs.why: Miss Sara allows Hafsa to go after break time, but reminds her not to forget her leave application, and Hafsa thanks her teacher.

lessons.title: Language Focus
lessons.notes_html:
C) Language Focus — 1. Vocabulary Building: i. Read the given words with their meanings

  • Q: What does 'console' mean?
    Ans: To comfort someone.
  • Q: What does 'adventurous' mean?
    Ans: Willing to try something daring.
  • Q: What does 'parcel' mean?
    Ans: A package wrapped for shipment.
  • Q: What does 'anxiously' mean?
    Ans: In a worried or nervous manner.
  • Q: What does 'disappoint' mean?
    Ans: To make somebody feel sad.
  • Q: What does 'expect' mean?
    Ans: To predict or believe that something will happen.

C) Language Focus — 1. Vocabulary Building: iii. Write the plurals of the given nouns

  • Q: Write the plural of 'hair'.
    Ans: hairs
  • Q: Write the plural of 'fly'.
    Ans: flies
  • Q: Write the plural of 'tooth'.
    Ans: teeth
  • Q: Write the plural of 'letter'.
    Ans: letters
  • Q: Write the plural of 'bench'.
    Ans: benches
  • Q: Write the plural of 'knife'.
    Ans: knives
  • Q: Write the plural of 'book'.
    Ans: books
  • Q: Write the plural of 'potato'.
    Ans: potatoes

C) Language Focus — Regular and Irregular Verb Forms: iv. Read the given regular forms of verbs

  • Q: Give the past form and the past participle form of 'accept'.
    Ans: Past form: accepted. Past participle form: accepted.
  • Q: Give the past form and the past participle form of 'change'.
    Ans: Past form: changed. Past participle form: changed.
  • Q: Give the past form and the past participle form of 'remember'.
    Ans: Past form: remembered. Past participle form: remembered.
  • Q: Give the past form and the past participle form of 'pack'.
    Ans: Past form: packed. Past participle form: packed.
  • Q: Give the past form and the past participle form of 'listen'.
    Ans: Past form: listened. Past participle form: listened.

C) Language Focus — Regular and Irregular Verb Forms: v. Read the given irregular forms of verbs

  • Q: Give the past form and the past participle form of 'arise'.
    Ans: Past form: arose. Past participle form: arisen.
  • Q: Give the past form and the past participle form of 'beat'.
    Ans: Past form: beat. Past participle form: beaten.
  • Q: Give the past form and the past participle form of 'choose'.
    Ans: Past form: chose. Past participle form: chosen.
  • Q: Give the past form and the past participle form of 'fly'.
    Ans: Past form: flew. Past participle form: flown.
  • Q: Give the past form and the past participle form of 'go'.
    Ans: Past form: went. Past participle form: gone.

C) Language Focus — Regular and Irregular Verb Forms: vi. Write three examples of regular and irregular verbs in your notebook

  • Q: Write three examples of regular verbs and three examples of irregular verbs.
    Ans: Regular verbs form their past forms by adding -ed: play — played, watch — watched, work — worked. Irregular verbs do not add -ed: eat — ate, sing — sang, write — wrote.

C) Language Focus — 2. Learning to Spell: Fill in the missing letters to complete the words

  • Q: Un__ortu__ately
    Ans: Unfortunately
  • Q: e__cite__ly
    Ans: excitedly
  • Q: a__xiousl__
    Ans: anxiously
  • Q: adven__urou__
    Ans: adventurous
  • Q: ex__ec__
    Ans: expect
  • Q: __isap__ointed
    Ans: disappointed

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar: Simple Past Tense — i. Read the given sentences and notice the structure of the simple past tense

  • Q: Identify the form of the simple past tense in: 'Hafsa got her parcel.'
    Ans: It is an affirmative sentence. Structure: subject + verb (past form) + object.
  • Q: Identify the form of the simple past tense in: 'Hafsa did not get her parcel.'
    Ans: It is a negative sentence. Structure: subject + did not + verb (base form) + object.
  • Q: Identify the form of the simple past tense in: 'Did Hafsa get her parcel?'
    Ans: It is an interrogative sentence. Structure: Did + subject + verb (base form) + object?

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar: Past Continuous Tense — ii. Read the given sentences and notice the structure of the past continuous tense

  • Q: Identify the form of the past continuous tense in: 'Hafsa was reading her storybook.'
    Ans: It is an affirmative sentence. Structure: subject + was/were + -ing verb form + object.
  • Q: Identify the form of the past continuous tense in: 'Hafsa was not reading her storybook.'
    Ans: It is a negative sentence. Structure: subject + was/were + not + -ing verb form + object.
  • Q: Identify the form of the past continuous tense in: 'Was Hafsa reading her storybook?'
    Ans: It is an interrogative sentence. Structure: was/were + subject + -ing verb form + object?

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar: iii. Make three sentences of your own using each of the tenses mentioned above

  • Q: Make three sentences of your own in the simple past tense.
    Ans: 1. I visited my uncle yesterday. 2. We played cricket in the park. 3. My mother cooked a delicious dinner.
  • Q: Make three sentences of your own in the past continuous tense.
    Ans: 1. I was reading a storybook at night. 2. The children were playing in the garden. 3. It was raining in the morning.

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar: Transitional Devices — iv. Read the given sentences

  • Q: Which transitional device is used in: 'I like to eat healthy fruit and vegetables; for example apples, bananas and spinach.'
    Ans: The transitional device is 'for example'. It links the two parts of the sentence by giving examples of healthy fruit and vegetables.
  • Q: Which transitional device is used in: 'I know some of the collective nouns; for instance team, class, flock, and army.'
    Ans: The transitional device is 'for instance'. It links the two parts of the sentence by giving examples of collective nouns.

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar: Transitional Devices — v. Write two sentences of your own using 'for example' and 'for instance' each

  • Q: Write two sentences of your own using 'for example'.
    Ans: 1. I like many fruits; for example, mangoes and oranges. 2. We play many games at school; for example, cricket and football.
  • Q: Write two sentences of your own using 'for instance'.
    Ans: 1. Some animals live in water; for instance, fish and frogs. 2. She can speak many languages; for instance, English and Arabic.

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar: Types of Sentences — viii. Read the given command sentences

  • Q: What type of sentence is: 'Show me your notebook.'?
    Ans: It is a command sentence (imperative sentence). A sentence that expresses a request or command is called an imperative sentence or command.
  • Q: What type of sentence is: 'Go and brush your teeth.'?
    Ans: It is a command sentence (imperative sentence), because it gives a command.
  • Q: What type of sentence is: 'Open the door.'?
    Ans: It is a command sentence (imperative sentence), because it gives a command.

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar: Types of Sentences — ix. Read the given instructional sentences

  • Q: What type of sentence is: 'Take me to the market.'?
    Ans: It is an instructional sentence. An instructional sentence gives advice or instructions and ends with a full stop.
  • Q: What type of sentence is: 'Add two teaspoons of sugar.'?
    Ans: It is an instructional sentence, because it gives an instruction.
  • Q: What type of sentence is: 'Turn to the left.'?
    Ans: It is an instructional sentence, because it gives an instruction or direction.

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar: Types of Sentences — x. Read the given exclamatory sentences

  • Q: What type of sentence is: 'Our team won the match!'?
    Ans: It is an exclamatory sentence. An exclamatory sentence expresses sudden emotions or feelings and ends with an exclamation mark.
  • Q: What type of sentence is: 'Ouch, My leg is bleeding!'?
    Ans: It is an exclamatory sentence, because it expresses a sudden feeling of pain.
  • Q: What type of sentence is: 'Wow, you are looking pretty!'?
    Ans: It is an exclamatory sentence, because it expresses sudden surprise and praise.

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar: Types of Sentences — xi. Write three sentences of each kind discussed above in your notebook

  • Q: Write three command (imperative) sentences.
    Ans: 1. Close the window. 2. Bring me a glass of water. 3. Sit down, please.
  • Q: Write three instructional sentences.
    Ans: 1. Add two cups of flour. 2. Stir the mixture well. 3. Bake it for twenty minutes.
  • Q: Write three exclamatory sentences.
    Ans: 1. What a beautiful garden! 2. Hurrah! We have won the match! 3. Oh! It is raining!
