D) Writing — 1. Learning to Write: i. Read the given letter and notice its features

  • Q: In the given letter, what is the writer's address?
    Ans: Hafsa, House No. 271, Sector B, Faisalabad.
  • Q: In the given letter, what is the receiver's address?
    Ans: XYZ Authority, Faisalabad.
  • Q: In the given letter, what are the date and the subject?
    Ans: Date: October 15, 2018. Subject: Rainwater Drainage.
  • Q: What problem does Hafsa write about in the letter, and what does she request?
    Ans: She writes about the issue of rainwater drainage. Every year in the monsoon season her neighbourhood is flooded with rainwater because the drainage system collapses. Although they have requested the area committee many times, the situation remains the same, and there is a real danger of a disease outbreak. She requests the authority to resolve this issue on a priority basis.
  • Q: How does the given letter end?
    Ans: The letter ends with the closing 'Yours sincerely,' followed by the writer's name, Hafsa.

D) Writing — 2. Creative Writing: Write a letter to the editor of any children's magazine about pollution in your area

  • Q: Write a letter to the editor of any children's magazine about pollution in your area.
    Ans: House No. 12, Street No. 3, Peshawar. October 20, 2026. The Editor, Children's Magazine, Peshawar. Subject: Pollution in Our Area. Respected Sir, I am writing this letter to inform your readers about the pollution in our area. Heaps of garbage are lying in our streets, and the smoke from vehicles and factories has made the air dirty. The drains are blocked, so dirty water flows on the roads and spreads diseases. Children cannot play outside in the evening because of the bad smell and smoke. I request the authorities, through your magazine, to clean our area and plant more trees. I also request all children to keep their surroundings clean and never throw litter on the roads. Yours truly, Ahmed Khan

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Getting Started — Let's Talk

  • Q: Is it good to fight over things? Discuss.
    Ans: No, it is not good to fight over things. Fighting hurts others and also harms us. We should share our things and solve our problems by talking politely.
  • Q: Have you ever fought over things with your siblings?
    Ans: Model answer: Yes, once I fought with my brother over a ball, just like the two kids in the picture. Later I felt sorry, because we could have played together with the same ball.
  • Q: What are the ways to avoid fight?
    Ans: We can avoid a fight by sharing our things, taking turns, listening to each other, speaking politely, and saying sorry when we make a mistake.

Reading — Pre-reading, While-reading and Post Reading

  • Q: Pre-reading: Look at the pictures and read the title of the poem. Guess five words related to it.
    Ans: Five words related to the poem 'Two Little Kittens' are: kittens, stormy night, quarrel, fight, and mouse.
  • Q: Pre-reading: Did you ever fight with anyone? Share.
    Ans: Model answer: Yes, I once quarrelled with my friend over a pencil. We stopped talking for a day, but then we said sorry to each other and became friends again. I learnt that fighting never solves a problem.
  • Q: While-reading: Why did the old woman send them out of the room?
    Ans: The two kittens began to quarrel and then to fight in the room. So the old woman took the sweeping broom and swept them both right out of the room.
  • Q: Post Reading: Why did the kittens begin to quarrel?
    Ans: One kitten had a mouse and the other had none, and that was the way the quarrel began.
  • Q: Post Reading: What is the main idea of the poem?
    Ans: The main idea of the poem is that quarrelling and fighting is a bad thing and we should always avoid it. When we fight with others, we often harm ourselves too, just as the kittens were sent out into the snow and became wet and cold.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension: i. Answer these questions

  • Q: What lesson did the kittens learn?
    Ans: The kittens learnt that fighting is a bad thing and it should always be avoided. They found it much better to lie by the fire than to quarrel and fight.
  • Q: Why is fighting a bad thing? Discuss.
    Ans: Fighting is a bad thing because it can harm us and others. The kittens fought, so the old woman swept them out of the house, and they became wet with snow and as cold as ice. In the same way, when we fight, we hurt others and often harm ourselves too.
  • Q: How do you relate this poem to your own personal experiences?
    Ans: Model answer: Once I quarrelled with my younger sister over a toy, and our mother sent us both out of the room. We felt sorry and ashamed, just like the kittens. Then we said sorry, shared the toy, and played together happily.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension: ii. Read the poem carefully and write answers to the given questions (inferential questions)

  • Q: What is the setting of the poem? Also tell which words helped you to understand the setting.
    Ans: The setting of the poem is a house on a stormy, snowy night, where the kittens lie by the fire in a room. The words that help us understand the setting are 'one stormy night', 'right out of the room', 'all wet with snow', 'as cold as ice', and 'to lie by the fire'.
  • Q: Do you think fighting is a good or bad thing? Give reasons for your answer.
    Ans: Fighting is a bad thing. It hurts others and harms us too. The kittens fought over a mouse and, as a result, they were swept out of the warm room into the snow, where they became wet and cold. Fighting never solves a problem; talking and sharing do.
  • Q: What is the moral of the poem?
    Ans: The moral of the poem is that we should never quarrel or fight with others. It is always better to live together in peace and love than to fight over small things.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension: iii. Read the given summary of the poem

  • Q: Write the summary of the poem 'Two Little Kittens' in your own words.
    Ans: This poem is about two little kittens. They started to quarrel with each other during a stormy night. One kitten had a mouse but the other kitten had none, so their quarrel began. The old woman became angry and swept them out of her house with her broom. Then they returned wet and cold. They realised their mistake and felt ashamed. They found that it is better to lie by the fire in the house than to quarrel and fight.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension: iv. Read the poem again and fill in the blanks with the correct options

  • Q: The two little kittens fought during a stormy ______.
    Options: night / morning / evening / afternoon
    Ans: night
  • Q: The old woman swept the kittens with a ______.
    Options: stick / broom / hanger / brush
    Ans: broom
  • Q: The kittens became wet with ______.
    Options: rain / sweat / water / snow
    Ans: snow
  • Q: One kitten had no ______ so they began to fight.
    Options: toy / food / mouse / blanket
    Ans: mouse
  • Q: They found it much better to ______ by the fire.
    Options: sit / stand / lie / fight
    Ans: lie

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 2. Analytical Reading: Read any poem about your favourite animal and write it down in your notebook

  • Q: Read any poem about your favourite animal from the internet/library and write it down in your notebook.
    Ans: Model poem: 'My little parrot, green and bright, / Sings a sweet song in the morning light. / It eats chillies and seeds all day, / And repeats the words that I say.' (Any short poem about a favourite animal may be written in the same way.)

options: No, fighting hurts others and also harms us
No, but we should never share things

mcqs.q: What is the main idea of the poem 'Two Little Kittens'?
options: Quarrelling and fighting is bad and we should always avoid it
Kittens should not live in houses
We should play in the snow at night
Old women should keep brooms in the room
mcqs.why: The solved answer gives the main idea: quarrelling and fighting is a bad thing and we should always avoid it, as the kittens learnt.

mcqs.q: What did the kittens find much better than quarrelling and fighting?

mcqs.why: The reading comprehension answer says the kittens found it much better to lie by the fire than to quarrel and fight with each other.

mcqs.q: How did the kittens feel after they came back in from the snow?
options: They realised their mistake and felt ashamed
mcqs.why: The summary in the lesson says they returned wet and cold, realised their mistake and felt ashamed of quarrelling and fighting.

mcqs.q: What is the moral of the poem?
options: We should always win every fight
We should keep our things hidden
We should not talk to anyone
We should never quarrel or fight, and live together in peace and love
mcqs.why: The inferential answer gives the moral: never quarrel or fight with others; it is better to live together in peace and love.

mcqs.q: The two little kittens fought during a stormy what?
mcqs.why: This is a book question from the poem. The kittens fought during a stormy night, as the first lines of the poem tell us.

mcqs.q: With what did the old woman sweep the kittens out of the room?
mcqs.why: This is a book question from the poem. The old woman took the sweeping broom and swept them both right out of the room.

lessons.title: Sounds and Speaking
lessons.notes_html:
A) Oral Communication — 1. Learning the Sounds: Rhythm, Stress and Intonation — Read the given poem with proper rhythm, stress and intonation

  • Q: What is rhythm?
    Ans: Rhythm is the repeated pattern of sounds at regular intervals.
  • Q: What is stress?
    Ans: Stress is the emphasis placed on a word or a syllable of a word.
  • Q: What is intonation?
    Ans: Intonation is the way a person's voice rises and falls in speech.

A) Oral Communication — 2. Learning to Speak: i. Read and practise the given dialogue

  • Q: Read and practise the dialogue about quarrelling. What do Maryam and Umar say?
    Ans: Miss Sadia asks whether it is good to quarrel or fight with each other. Maryam says, 'No, teacher, we should not quarrel. We should be kind to each other and help each other.' Umar says, 'Fighting is not a good thing. It can harm you.' The teacher praises them, and the students thank her.

A) Oral Communication — 2. Learning to Speak: ii. Read the given non-verbal cues with their meanings

  • Q: Give an example of body contact as a non-verbal cue.
    Ans: Shaking hands is an example of body contact.
  • Q: Give an example of eye movement as a non-verbal cue.
    Ans: Gazing is an example of eye movement.
  • Q: Give an example of hand movement as a non-verbal cue.
    Ans: Waving is an example of hand movement.
  • Q: Give an example of posture as a non-verbal cue.
    Ans: Slouching is an example of posture.
  • Q: Give an example of appearance as a non-verbal cue.
    Ans: Shrugging is the example given in the book with appearance. Non-verbal cues include facial expressions, body language and gestures, and they are used to communicate without words.

A) Oral Communication — 2. Learning to Speak: iii. Read the expressions with the given tones

  • Q: How is the word 'really' used to express something unexpected?
    Ans: 'Oh, really?' — said with a rising tone.
  • Q: How is the word 'really' used to express surprise?
    Ans: 'Really? I don't believe you.' — said with a rising tone of surprise.
  • Q: How is the word 'really' used for sad news?
    Ans: 'Really? But how?' — said with a falling tone.
  • Q: How is the word 'really' used for good news?
    Ans: 'Really? It's great news.' — said with a rising tone of happiness.

mcqs.q: What is rhythm?
options: The repeated pattern of sounds at regular intervals
The emphasis placed on a syllable
The way the voice rises and falls
The meaning of a difficult word
mcqs.why: The sounds exercise defines rhythm as the repeated pattern of sounds at regular intervals, as we hear in a poem.

mcqs.q: What is stress?
options: The rise and fall of the voice
The emphasis placed on a word or a syllable of a word
A heated argument about a small thing
mcqs.why: The sounds exercise defines stress as the emphasis placed on a word or a syllable of a word when we speak.

mcqs.q: What is intonation?
options: The emphasis placed on a syllable
The way a person's voice rises and falls in speech
The speed of reading a poem
mcqs.why: The sounds exercise defines intonation as the way a person's voice rises and falls in speech, as in the word 'really' examples.

mcqs.q: What does Maryam say in the dialogue about quarrelling?
options: We should quarrel only at break time
Well said, you both are right
We should not quarrel; we should be kind to each other and help each other
mcqs.why: In the dialogue Maryam tells Miss Sadia that we should not quarrel and should be kind to each other and help each other.

mcqs.q: What does Umar say in the dialogue about fighting?
options: Fighting is not a good thing; it can harm you
We should be kind and help each other
mcqs.why: In the dialogue Umar says fighting is not a good thing because it can harm you, and the teacher praises both students.

mcqs.q: Which is an example of body contact as a non-verbal cue?
mcqs.why: The non-verbal cues exercise gives shaking hands as the example of body contact, one way we communicate without using words.

mcqs.q: Which is an example of eye movement as a non-verbal cue?
mcqs.why: The non-verbal cues exercise gives gazing as the example of eye movement. The other options belong to different non-verbal cues.

mcqs.q: Which is an example of hand movement as a non-verbal cue?
mcqs.why: The non-verbal cues exercise gives waving as the example of hand movement, used to communicate without words.

mcqs.q: Which is an example of posture as a non-verbal cue?
mcqs.why: The non-verbal cues exercise gives slouching as the example of posture, which shows body position without any words.

mcqs.q: How is 'really' said for sad news in 'Really? But how?'?
options: With a rising tone of happiness
mcqs.why: The tones exercise says 'Really? But how?' for sad news is said with a falling tone, unlike the rising tone used for good news.

lessons.title: Language Focus
lessons.notes_html:
C) Language Focus — 1. Vocabulary Building: i. Read the given words with their meanings

  • Q: What does 'stormy' mean?
    Ans: Weather with strong winds and heavy rain or snow.
  • Q: What does 'quarrel' mean?
    Ans: A heated argument or disagreement, typically about a trivial issue.
  • Q: What does 'sweep' mean?
    Ans: To clean a room, surface, etc. using a broom.
  • Q: What does 'broom' mean?
    Ans: A long brush used for cleaning the floor.
  • Q: What does 'crept' mean?
    Ans: Moved slowly without making a sound. (In the book, the printed meaning ends mid-phrase: 'moved slowly without making a'.)

C) Language Focus — 1. Vocabulary Building: Writing a Poem — ii. Write a poem on the topic 'My Pet Cat' with the help of the given rhyming words

  • Q: Write a poem on the topic 'My Pet Cat' using the rhyming words: purr, fur; feet, treat; fish, dish; adore, bore.
    Ans: My pet cat is soft and sweet, / With silky fur and tiny feet. / She drinks her milk and eats her treat, / And plays with me in the street. / She loves her fish served in a dish, / And asks for more, as cats wish. / When she is happy, she starts to purr, / And I gently stroke her fur. / She is my friend whom I adore, / Playing with her is never a bore.

C) Language Focus — 1. Vocabulary Building: Analogy — iii. Read the given analogies

  • Q: Explain the analogy: 'Leaf is to tree as petal is to flower.'
    Ans: An analogy compares two things to show their similarity. A leaf is a part of a tree, just as a petal is a part of a flower.
  • Q: Explain the analogy: 'Apple is to fruit as carrot is to vegetables.'
    Ans: An apple belongs to the group of fruit, just as a carrot belongs to the group of vegetables.
  • Q: Explain the analogy: 'Turtle is to crawl as frog is to hop.'
    Ans: A turtle moves by crawling, just as a frog moves by hopping.
  • Q: Explain the analogy: 'Car is to road as boat is to ocean.'
    Ans: A car travels on a road, just as a boat travels on the ocean.
  • Q: Explain the analogy: 'Hungry is to eat as tired is to sleep.'
    Ans: When we are hungry we eat, just as when we are tired we sleep.

C) Language Focus — 1. Vocabulary Building: Analogy — iv. Complete the given analogies by choosing the correct words

  • Q: Cow is a mammal as snake is a/an ______ (insect, reptile)
    Ans: reptile
  • Q: Pencil is to write as scissors is to ______ (rub, cut)
    Ans: cut
  • Q: Moon is to night as sun is to ______ (day, evening)
    Ans: day
  • Q: Hat is to head as shoe is to ______ (foot, arm)
    Ans: foot

C) Language Focus — 1. Vocabulary Building: Similes — v. Read the given similes with their meanings and sentences

  • Q: What does the simile 'as light as a feather' mean? Use it in a sentence.
    Ans: It means very light in weight. Sentence (as given in the book): 'He is as light as feather.'
  • Q: What does the simile 'as brave as a lion' mean? Use it in a sentence.
    Ans: It means very brave. Sentence: 'My younger brother is as brave as a lion.'
  • Q: What does the simile 'as busy as a bee' mean? Use it in a sentence.
    Ans: It means very busy. Sentence: 'They are as busy as bees.'
  • Q: What does the simile 'as strong as an ox' mean? Use it in a sentence.
    Ans: It means very strong. Sentence: 'He can hit the ball towards the fans because he is as strong as an ox.'
  • Q: What does the simile 'have eyes like a hawk' mean? Use it in a sentence.
    Ans: It describes someone who sees every small detail. Sentence: 'My father is an engineer and he has eyes like a hawk.'

C) Language Focus — 1. Vocabulary Building: Similes — vi. Circle the similes in the poem and use them in sentences of your own

  • Q: Use the simile 'as quiet as mice' from the poem in a sentence of your own.
    Ans: When the teacher entered the classroom, all the students became as quiet as mice.
  • Q: Use the simile 'as cold as ice' from the poem in a sentence of your own.
    Ans: After playing in the snow, my hands were as cold as ice.

C) Language Focus — 2. Learning to Spell: Fill in the missing letters to complete the words

  • Q: symb__l
    Ans: symbol
  • Q: he__biv__rous
    Ans: herbivorous
  • Q: __ravery
    Ans: bravery
  • Q: h__nt
    Ans: hunt
  • Q: at__ractiv__
    Ans: attractive

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar: Simple Future Tense — i. Read the structures of the simple future tense with sentences

  • Q: What is the structure of an affirmative sentence in the simple future tense? Give an example.
    Ans: Structure: Subject + will/shall + base form of verb + object. Example: 'He will complete his homework.'
  • Q: What is the structure of a negative sentence in the simple future tense? Give an example.
    Ans: Structure: Subject + will/shall not + base form of verb + object. Example: 'He will not complete his homework.'
  • Q: What is the structure of an interrogative sentence in the simple future tense? Give an example.
    Ans: Structure: Will/Shall + subject + base form of verb + object? Example: 'Will he complete his homework?'

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar: Simple Future Tense — ii. Write five sentences of your own using the simple future tense

  • Q: Write five sentences of your own in your notebook using the simple future tense.
    Ans: 1. I will finish my homework in the evening. 2. We shall visit our grandmother tomorrow. 3. She will take care of her pet cat. 4. They will play a friendly match on Friday. 5. He will not quarrel with anyone again.

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar: iii. Read the given questions with different forms of 'be', 'do' and 'have'

  • Q: Which of the given questions begin with a form of 'be'?
    Ans: 'Am I cleaning my room?', 'Is this cat hungry?', 'Are the kittens fighting?', 'Was she sleeping in her room?' and 'Were the children making noise?' begin with forms of 'be' (am, is, are, was, were).
  • Q: Which of the given questions begin with a form of 'do'?
    Ans: 'Does Hina help you?', 'Do they come late at night?' and 'Did it rain yesterday?' begin with forms of 'do' (does, do, did).
  • Q: Which of the given questions begin with a form of 'have'?
    Ans: 'Has he completed his work?', 'Have they reached there?' and 'Had we locked the door?' begin with forms of 'have' (has, have, had).

C) Language Focus — 3. Grammar: iv. Write two questions using 'be', 'do' and 'have' each in your notebook

  • Q: Write two questions using a form of 'be'.
    Ans: 1. Are you reading a poem? 2. Is the cat hungry?
  • Q: Write two questions using a form of 'do'.
    Ans: 1. Do you like storybooks? 2. Does she help you?
  • Q: Write two questions using a form of 'have'.
    Ans: 1. Have you finished your work? 2. Has he reached home?

mcqs.q: What does the word 'stormy' mean?
options: Weather with strong winds and heavy rain or snow
Weather with no wind at all
Weather that is warm and dry
mcqs.why: The vocabulary exercise gives 'stormy' as weather with strong winds and heavy rain or snow, like the stormy night in the poem.

mcqs.q: What does the word 'quarrel' mean?
options: A friendly chat with a neighbour
A game played with a ball
A heated argument or disagreement, typically about a trivial issue
mcqs.why: The vocabulary exercise gives 'quarrel' as a heated argument or disagreement, typically about a trivial, or very small, issue.

mcqs.q: What is a 'broom'?
options: A small stick used for writing
A long brush used for cleaning the floor
A brush used for painting walls
A tool used for digging soil
mcqs.why: The vocabulary exercise gives 'broom' as a long brush used for cleaning the floor, like the sweeping broom of the old woman.

mcqs.q: In the analogy 'Leaf is to tree as petal is to flower', why are leaf and petal compared?
options: A leaf is a part of a tree, just as a petal is a part of a flower
mcqs.why: The analogy exercise explains that an analogy shows similarity: a leaf is a part of a tree, just as a petal is a part of a flower.

mcqs.q: Complete the analogy: 'Moon is to night as sun is to ____.'
mcqs.why: The analogy exercise completes it with 'day', because the moon belongs to the night just as the sun belongs to the day.

mcqs.why: The analogy exercise explains that when we are hungry we eat, just as when we are tired we sleep and take rest.

mcqs.why: The similes exercise gives 'as brave as a lion' with the meaning 'very brave', used for the younger brother in the sentence.

mcqs.q: What does the simile 'as busy as a bee' mean?
mcqs.why: The similes exercise gives 'as busy as a bee' with the meaning 'very busy', as in the sentence 'They are as busy as bees.'

mcqs.q: What does the simile 'have eyes like a hawk' describe?
options: Someone who sees every small detail
mcqs.why: The similes exercise says 'have eyes like a hawk' describes someone who sees every small detail, like the engineer father in the sentence.

mcqs.q: Which word completes the spelling pattern 'symb__l'?
mcqs.why: The spelling exercise completes symb__l as 'symbol', with the missing letter o filled in the middle of the word.

mcqs.q: What is the structure of an affirmative sentence in the simple future tense?
options: Subject + will/shall + base form of verb + object
mcqs.why: The future tense exercise gives this structure with the example 'He will complete his homework' in the simple future tense.

mcqs.q: Which sentence is a negative sentence in the simple future tense?
options: He will not complete his homework.
mcqs.why: The future tense exercise gives 'He will not complete his homework' as the negative form, using will not with the base verb.

mcqs.q: Which question begins with a form of 'be'?
mcqs.why: The grammar exercise lists 'Is this cat hungry?' among the questions beginning with forms of 'be' such as am, is, are, was and were.

mcqs.q: Which question begins with a form of 'have'?
options: Do they come late at night?
mcqs.why: The grammar exercise lists 'Has he completed his work?' among the questions beginning with forms of 'have' such as has, have and had.

lessons.title: Writing
lessons.notes_html:
D) Writing — 1. Learning to Write: i. Read the given poem and write its central idea in your notebook

  • Q: Write the central idea of the given poem about elephants.
    Ans: The central idea of the poem is that elephants walk together in a line, holding each other's tails with their trunks, just like holding hands. They do this while walking along the trails, in circus rings, at work and at play, and they always stay together and feel happy. The poem shows that living and moving together in unity makes life easy and joyful.

D) Writing — 1. Learning to Write: ii. Write three pairs of rhyming words about 'Rainbow' and write a poem

  • Q: Write three pairs of rhyming words about 'Rainbow' and write a poem with them.
    Ans: Three pairs of rhyming words: sky — high, glow — show, bright — light. Poem: 'After the rain, look at the sky, / A rainbow is shining bright and high. / Its seven colours softly glow, / And put on a beautiful show. / Red, green and blue, so clear and bright, / It fills our hearts with joy and light.'
  • Q: Note: About the printed wording of this task
    Ans: In the book, this instruction is printed incomplete: 'Write three pairs of rhyming words about Rainbow and write a' — the sentence ends there on the page. The teaching point for the task says 'Ask students to write a poem', so the model answer above gives the three rhyming pairs and a short poem on 'Rainbow'.

D) Writing — 2. Creative Writing: Write a paragraph on 'How we should take care of our pet animals'

  • Q: Write a paragraph on 'How we should take care of our pet animals'. Share your views.
    Ans: We should take great care of our pet animals because they depend on us. We should give them fresh food and clean water every day and keep their place clean. We should never beat them or leave them alone in the cold or heat, like the kittens in the poem. We should play with them, take them to a doctor when they are sick, and treat them with love and kindness. A pet that is well cared for stays healthy and happy and becomes our true friend.

mcqs.q: In the poem about elephants, how do the elephants walk?
mcqs.why: The central idea answer says elephants walk together in a line, holding each other's tails with their trunks as they walk.

mcqs.q: How do the elephants hold hands, according to the poem's central idea?
options: By walking side by side silently
By holding each other's tails with their trunks
By holding ropes with their trunks
mcqs.why: The central idea answer says they hold each other's tails with their trunks, just like holding hands, and always stay together.

mcqs.q: According to the central idea, how do the elephants feel when they stay together?
mcqs.why: The central idea answer says elephants always stay together and feel happy at work and at play, in trails and circus rings.

mcqs.q: Which is one of the rhyming word pairs given for the 'Rainbow' poem?
mcqs.why: The writing exercise gives three rhyming pairs for 'Rainbow': sky - high, glow - show and bright - light, and sky - high is one of them.

mcqs.q: Which is another rhyming word pair given for the 'Rainbow' poem?
mcqs.why: The writing exercise gives glow - show as one of the three rhyming pairs, along with sky - high and bright - light.

mcqs.q: How many colours of the rainbow are mentioned in the model 'Rainbow' poem?
mcqs.why: The model poem says 'Its seven colours softly glow', so seven colours of the rainbow are mentioned in the poem.

mcqs.q: How often should we give our pet animals fresh food and clean water?
mcqs.why: The pet care paragraph says we should give our pet animals fresh food and clean water every day and keep their place clean.

mcqs.q: What should we do when our pet animal is sick?
options: Leave it alone in the cold
mcqs.why: The pet care paragraph says we should play with our pets and take them to a doctor when they are sick, treating them with kindness.

mcqs.q: What should we never do to our pet animals?
options: Beat them or leave them alone in the cold or heat
mcqs.why: The pet care paragraph says we should never beat our pet animals or leave them alone in the cold or heat, like the kittens in the snow.

mcqs.q: How does a well-cared-for pet become, according to the paragraph?
options: Healthy, happy and our true friend
mcqs.why: The pet care paragraph ends by saying a pet that is well cared for stays healthy and happy and becomes our true friend.

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension: Answer the given questions

  • Q: Write the names of any five endangered animals.
    Ans: Five endangered animals are: the snow leopard, the Bengal tiger, the giant panda, the Asian elephant and the blue whale.
  • Q: What will be your future career and why?
    Ans: Model answer: I will become a teacher in the future. I choose this career because I love reading and learning, and I want to help children of my area to learn and become successful in life.
  • Q: What type of storybooks do you like to read? Give reasons why.
    Ans: I like to read adventure storybooks. I like them because they are exciting and full of surprises, and through them I learn about brave people, new places and different lands.
  • Q: What did the little kittens learn after the fight?
    Ans: After the fight, the little kittens learnt that fighting is a bad thing and should always be avoided. They found it much better to lie by the fire than to quarrel and fight.
  • Q: Why should we never fight with others?
    Ans: We should never fight with others because fighting hurts them and also harms us. It makes people angry and sad, and nothing is solved by fighting. We should solve our problems by talking politely and being kind to each other.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension: Read the given paragraph and summarise it

  • Q: Summarise the given paragraph about choosing a career.
    Ans: Summary: Choosing a career is one of the most important decisions of our life, and it greatly affects our future. Therefore, parents and teachers should guide their children to choose their future careers wisely.

mcqs.q: Which animal is named in the Review as an endangered animal?

mcqs.q: Which animal is also named in the Review as an endangered animal?
mcqs.why: The Review answer names the giant panda among the five endangered animals, along with the snow leopard and the Bengal tiger.

mcqs.q: Which animal is also named in the Review as an endangered animal?
mcqs.why: The Review answer names the blue whale among the five endangered animals, along with the Asian elephant and the giant panda.

To earn a lot of money quickly
To work only for a few hours

mcqs.q: What type of storybooks does the writer like to read, according to the Review?
mcqs.why: The Review answer says 'I like to read adventure storybooks' because they are exciting and full of surprises.

mcqs.q: Why does the writer like adventure storybooks?
options: They are very short and easy
They are exciting and teach about brave people, new places and different lands
mcqs.why: The Review answer gives the reasons: adventure stories are exciting and full of surprises and teach about brave people and new lands.

mcqs.q: What did the little kittens learn after the fight, according to the Review?
options: Kittens should play in the snow
Fighting is bad and it is better to lie by the fire than to quarrel and fight
mcqs.why: The Review answer repeats the kittens' lesson: fighting is a bad thing and should always be avoided; lying by the fire is better.

options: Fighting hurts others and harms us, and nothing is solved by fighting
Fighting is only bad for children
mcqs.why: The Review answer says fighting hurts others and also harms us, so problems should be solved by talking politely and being kind.

mcqs.q: According to the summary in the Review, who should guide children to choose their careers wisely?
mcqs.why: The summary says choosing a career greatly affects our future, so parents and teachers should guide their children to choose wisely.

lessons.title: Sounds and Speaking
lessons.notes_html:
A) Oral Communication — 1. Learning the Sounds: Read the given words, divide them into their syllables and write their number of syllables

  • Q: Divide 'stormy' into syllables and write its number of syllables.
    Ans: stor-my — 2 syllables.
  • Q: Divide 'complaint' into syllables and write its number of syllables.
    Ans: com-plaint — 2 syllables.
  • Q: Divide 'intelligence' into syllables and write its number of syllables.
    Ans: in-tel-li-gence — 4 syllables.
  • Q: Divide 'password' into syllables and write its number of syllables.
    Ans: pass-word — 2 syllables.
  • Q: Divide 'technology' into syllables and write its number of syllables.
    Ans: tech-nol-o-gy — 4 syllables.

A) Oral Communication — Look at the given pictures, observe the body language and write what they are doing

  • Q: Look at the first picture. What is the boy doing?
    Ans: The boy is jumping over a box.
  • Q: Look at the second picture. What is the boy doing?
    Ans: The boy is running.
  • Q: Look at the third picture. What is the boy doing?
    Ans: The boy is standing with his arms folded.

A) Oral Communication — Work in pairs and share any memorable event from your lives by using expressions of joy, sadness or anger

  • Q: Share any memorable event from your life with your partner, using expressions of joy, sadness or anger.
    Ans: Model answer: 'I still remember the day I won a prize at school. In the morning I was sad because I had lost my favourite pen, but when my name was called for the prize, I cried with joy, "Hurrah! I have won!" My friends clapped for me, and I felt very happy and proud.'

mcqs.q: How many syllables are there in the word 'stormy'?
mcqs.why: The Review exercise divides 'stormy' as stor-my, which has two parts, so the word stormy has 2 syllables.

mcqs.q: How many syllables are there in the word 'intelligence'?
mcqs.why: The Review exercise divides 'intelligence' as in-tel-li-gence, which has four parts, so the word has 4 syllables.

mcqs.q: How many syllables are there in the word 'password'?
mcqs.why: The Review exercise divides 'password' as pass-word, which has two parts, so the word password has 2 syllables.

mcqs.q: How many syllables are there in the word 'technology'?
mcqs.why: The Review exercise divides 'technology' as tech-nol-o-gy, which has four parts, so the word technology has 4 syllables.

mcqs.q: In the first body-language picture in the Review, what is the boy doing?
mcqs.why: The Review answer says the boy in the first picture is jumping over a box, which we can tell from his body language.

mcqs.q: In the second body-language picture in the Review, what is the boy doing?
mcqs.why: The Review answer says the boy in the second picture is running, which we can tell by observing his body language.

mcqs.q: In the third body-language picture in the Review, what is the boy doing?
mcqs.why: The Review answer says the boy in the third picture is standing with his arms folded, a clear example of body language.

options: He had lost his school bag
He had missed the school bus
He had lost his favourite pen
mcqs.why: The model answer says the narrator was sad in the morning because he had lost his favourite pen, before the happy prize event.

mcqs.q: In the model memorable event, what made the narrator cry with joy?
options: His name was called for a prize at school
His friends gave him a gift

lessons.title: Language Focus
lessons.notes_html:
C) Language Focus — 1. Vocabulary Building: Read the given words and write their meanings in your notebook

  • Q: What does 'crept' mean?
    Ans: Moved slowly without making a sound.
  • Q: What does 'disappoint' mean?
    Ans: To make somebody feel sad.
  • Q: What does 'endangered' mean?
    Ans: In danger of dying out; at risk of becoming extinct.
  • Q: What does 'facilitate' mean?
    Ans: To make something easier or to help something happen.
  • Q: What does 'quarrel' mean?
    Ans: A heated argument or disagreement, typically about a trivial issue.

C) Language Focus — Read the given text and fill in the blanks with the correct prepositions of direction and movement

  • Q: As we were walking ______ the hill, it suddenly started to rain.
    Ans: up
  • Q: Luckily, there was a cave nearby and we ran ______ it.
    Ans: into
  • Q: My friend and I took out our torches and started walking ______ the cave.
    Ans: through
  • Q: As we were going ______ a wall, we were surprised to see drawings on it.
    Ans: past
  • Q: We waded ______ the lake and kept going on our journey.
    Ans: across

C) Language Focus — Read the given sentences and write their types

  • Q: Write the type of the sentence: 'Open the window.'
    Ans: Command (imperative) sentence.
  • Q: Write the type of the sentence: 'Wow! What a beautiful sight it is.'
    Ans: Exclamatory sentence.
  • Q: Write the type of the sentence: 'Are you going to the park?'
    Ans: Interrogative (question) sentence.
  • Q: Write the type of the sentence: 'Don't make noise.'
    Ans: Command (imperative) sentence.
  • Q: Write the type of the sentence: 'It is a pleasant day today.'
    Ans: Declarative (statement) sentence.
  • Q: Write the type of the sentence: 'Turn off the tap.'
    Ans: Command (imperative) sentence.

C) Language Focus — Rewrite the given text by using correct punctuation and capitalisation

  • Q: Rewrite the given text using correct punctuation and capitalisation: 'turkey is one of the most beautiful countries in the world have you ever been there i love it the main cities of istanbul and antalya are great some of the views of these cities are stunning'
    Ans: Turkey is one of the most beautiful countries in the world. Have you ever been there? I love it. The main cities of Istanbul and Antalya are great. Some of the views of these cities are stunning.

mcqs.q: What does the word 'endangered' mean?
options: In danger of dying out; at risk of becoming extinct
Kept as a pet at home
mcqs.why: The Review vocabulary gives 'endangered' as in danger of dying out, that is, at risk of becoming extinct, like the snow leopard.

mcqs.q: What does the word 'facilitate' mean?
options: To make something easier or to help something happen
mcqs.why: The Review vocabulary gives 'facilitate' as to make something easier or to help something happen in a smooth way.

mcqs.q: What does the word 'disappoint' mean?
mcqs.why: The Review vocabulary gives 'disappoint' as to make somebody feel sad, the same meaning as in Unit 13 of this book.

mcqs.q: What does the word 'quarrel' mean?
options: A game played in the playground
A heated argument or disagreement, typically about a trivial issue
mcqs.why: The Review vocabulary gives 'quarrel' as a heated argument or disagreement, typically about a trivial, or very small, issue.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank with a preposition of direction: 'As we were walking ____ the hill, it suddenly started to rain.'
mcqs.why: The Review exercise fills this blank with 'up', because the walkers were moving upward along the hill when the rain started.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 'Luckily, there was a cave nearby and we ran ____ it.'
mcqs.why: The Review exercise fills this blank with 'into', because they ran inside the cave to take shelter from the rain.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 'My friend and I took out our torches and started walking ____ the cave.'
mcqs.why: The Review exercise fills this blank with 'through', because they walked from one side of the cave to the other with torches.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 'As we were going ____ a wall, we were surprised to see drawings on it.'
mcqs.why: The Review exercise fills this blank with 'past', because they were moving beside and beyond the wall with drawings on it.

mcqs.q: What is the type of the sentence: 'Open the window.'?
mcqs.why: The Review exercise marks 'Open the window.' as a command, or imperative, sentence because it orders someone to do something.

mcqs.q: What is the type of the sentence: 'Wow! What a beautiful sight it is.'?
mcqs.why: The Review exercise marks this sentence as exclamatory because it expresses a strong feeling and uses an exclamation.

mcqs.q: What is the type of the sentence: 'Are you going to the park?'?
mcqs.why: The Review exercise marks 'Are you going to the park?' as an interrogative sentence because it asks a question.

mcqs.q: What is the type of the sentence: 'It is a pleasant day today.'?
mcqs.why: The Review exercise marks 'It is a pleasant day today.' as a declarative sentence because it simply states a fact.

mcqs.q: In the corrected Turkey text, why does 'Turkey' begin with a capital letter?
options: It is the first word of a sentence and the name of a country
It comes after a question mark
It is the name of a person
mcqs.why: The corrected text begins 'Turkey is one of the most beautiful countries in the world', with a capital T to start the sentence.

mcqs.q: In the corrected Turkey text, which punctuation mark ends 'Have you ever been there'?
mcqs.why: The corrected text writes 'Have you ever been there?' with a question mark, because the sentence asks a question.

mcqs.q: In the corrected Turkey text, why are 'Istanbul' and 'Antalya' written with capital letters?
options: They are the names of countries
They are the names of particular cities
mcqs.why: The corrected text calls Istanbul and Antalya the main cities, and names of particular places begin with capital letters.

lessons.title: Writing
lessons.notes_html:
D) Writing — 1. Learning to Write: Write a letter to your friend telling him/her about your recent visit to Neelum Valley

  • Q: Write a letter to your friend telling him/her about your recent visit to Neelum Valley.
    Ans: House No. 45, Main Bazaar, Peshawar. November 10, 2026. Dear Ali, I hope you are fine. Last week I visited Neelum Valley with my family, and I want to share my joy with you. Neelum Valley is a beautiful place with green mountains, tall trees and a clear blue river flowing between them. We saw waterfalls, ate fresh fruit and enjoyed the cool and pleasant weather. The people there were kind and friendly. I wish you were with us; we would have had great fun together. Please plan a visit with us next time. Give my regards to your parents. Your loving friend, Bilal

mcqs.q: Who wrote the model letter about the visit to Neelum Valley?
mcqs.why: The model letter ends with 'Your loving friend, Bilal', so Bilal is the writer of the letter about Neelum Valley.

mcqs.q: To whom is the model Neelum Valley letter written?
mcqs.why: The model letter begins with 'Dear Ali', so it is written to the writer's friend Ali to share the joy of the visit.

mcqs.q: From which address is the model Neelum Valley letter written?
mcqs.why: The model letter gives the writer's address as House No. 45, Main Bazaar, Peshawar, dated November 10, 2026.

mcqs.q: With whom did Bilal visit Neelum Valley?
mcqs.why: The model letter says 'Last week I visited Neelum Valley with my family', and he wants to share his joy with his friend.

mcqs.q: What scenery of Neelum Valley is described in the model letter?
mcqs.why: The model letter describes Neelum Valley as a beautiful place with green mountains, tall trees and a clear blue river.

mcqs.q: What flows between the mountains in Neelum Valley, according to the letter?
mcqs.why: The model letter says a clear blue river flows between the green mountains of Neelum Valley, making it beautiful.

mcqs.q: What did Bilal and his family see during the visit, according to the letter?
mcqs.why: The model letter says 'We saw waterfalls, ate fresh fruit and enjoyed the cool and pleasant weather' during the visit.

mcqs.q: How was the weather in Neelum Valley during the visit?
mcqs.why: The model letter says they enjoyed the cool and pleasant weather of Neelum Valley during their visit with the family.

mcqs.q: How does the model letter describe the people of Neelum Valley?
mcqs.why: The model letter says 'The people there were kind and friendly', and Bilal wishes his friend had been with them.

mcqs.q: How does the model Neelum Valley letter end?
options: With the closing 'Your loving friend, Bilal'
With the closing 'Yours truly, Ahmed Khan'
mcqs.why: The model letter ends by giving regards to Ali's parents and signing off with 'Your loving friend, Bilal'.
